<!-- AUG:hazrat-zia lecture 1 -->

In the name of Allah, all our madaris and taqarir, etc., are finished. And I am starting the series of sabaq today. Although there are very few days, I have until the 13th, and inshallah, I will have to depart from here. And the visa and the time is long, so time is short. I want us to cover as much as possible, for if the lessons are not completed, there will be great regret.

So, it is clear that whatever the…

I will pass through the main roads. It is not possible to go into the side streets. And even from the main roads, one has to pass very quickly. For this reason, in some way, these lessons… that you may be able to reach... and the falsafa of Aale Muhammad, alayhis salatu was salam, that you may be able to understand it, that we, on which din we are, and how pure our din is, and which of all these matters our din contains.

The very first and most fundamental thing, as I have said before and have explained in this gathering, is the tasawwur of God. Because the matter, everything that begins, begins with the zikr of Allah Ta'ala. And the tawhid of Rabb al-'Alamin, meaning, to consider Allah Ta'ala as one, is the greatest of all 'ulum. Meaning, among the 'ulum, the knowledge that is greater than all is the tawhid of Allah Ta'ala. To consider Allah Ta'ala as one. You will say that considering Allah Ta'ala as one, what kind of 'ulum is this? And how is this matter so vast? How is there such breadth in it that Allah Ta'ala should be considered one? Just consider Him one, and it's over. Then in considering Him one, how did such breadth emerge that we refer to it as 'ulum, and we interpret tawhid through 'ilm?

So the matter, in fact, is that we understand that one seed, when it is sown, is a small, ordinary seed, but when it brings forth its fruit, you see how large and mighty a tree it becomes. It has branches, and... In the same way, we are understanding this, but when you see its breadth, you will realize that the zikr of Allah Ta'ala and the tawhid of Allah Ta'ala, to affirm His Oneness, is not an ordinary matter. There is a very vast expanse in it that you will find.

I have told you before this that the world's civilization, in what way it has taken turns, and we have passed through an era on the surface of the earth when the people of Rome and Greece had divided God into lakhs of gods. And they had deities of different gods, and they used to perform puja-path of them. This is something everyone knows. But an era also came, which is called the Renaissance, when civilization took a turn, and that thing... was nullified, and Hinduism was born. And in Hinduism, this thing happened, that they said that, well, 'ubbad al-asnam (idol worship) is better to be called; that is, the puja of sanams should certainly be done, the parastish of but (idols) should certainly be done, but for but-parasti, so many buts are not needed. If you take a select few buts, that will be better. So they... 365 days are in a year, they made 365 gods, and each day they began to do puja-path with one god. And these were the buts that... whose puja they used to do where most of all? In Makkah Mu'azzama. The Arabs living in Makkah Mu'azzama are the very first, fundamental Hindus who started Hinduism. It is done. And Makkah Mu'azzama, Khana-e-Ka'bah Muqaddas, is their very first deval, where they had placed the buts. You must have heard this.

So those buts were placed there, and they saw that it is difficult to bring and place 365 buts at the Khana-e-Ka'bah, so they had divided them into three buts, and had brought and seated three buts there, whose names were Lat, Manat, and 'Uzza. Lat, Manat, and 'Uzza. This was it. And in some places, it has also been mentioned that 'Uzza, in fact, was a temple built in Ta'if, where this goddess was worshipped, the 'Uzza goddess. And with Lat and Manat was Hubul. So Lat, Manat, and Hubul, these three deities were made, and they were kept there. And a strange thing is that when Hinduism was finished, and when its great philosophers, who are of Hinduism, such as Radhakrishnan and Jawaharlal Nehru and the great philosophers who have passed of Hinduism, they considered that no, this is not an appropriate thing, that we should be called worshippers of 365 gods or worshippers of buts. It is better that we too divide these 365 into three, that would be good. So they... even today, if you take out and see their philosophy, the Puranas and these Vedas and their old books, if you see them, then in them you will get hints that the three gods they were believing in, those three gods were what? Shiv, Vishnu, and Brahma. These were their three deities. One who creates, one who destroys, one who sustains. These were the three deities whom the Hindus used to worship.

Well, these three were there, and besides that, 365 gods were with them. But the era passed so much that after this, that period came when Hazrat `Isa Masih` came to the world and he gave the teaching and you explained taslis. And the teaching that Hazrat `Isa` was giving, who was Ruhullah, who was a nabiyy of God, a respected nabiyy, who was a high-ranking nabiyy, after Hazrat Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim and Musa, Hazrat `Isa` had come. So you can imagine that 124,000 nabiyys had passed, and every nabiyy in his place had given the call to Allah, whose central idea which they had presented was the parastari of the One God. So it is clear that in the parastari of the One God, the matter of three cannot be included. How could Hazrat `Isa` explain three? But it was the misfortune of his followers, who were affirming him, that those who were the followers of Hazrat `Isa`, and especially his hawaari as they were being called, they also went on this wrong path. And what was that? That they, these three things: Father, Son, Ruh al-Qudus. Father, Son, and the Holy Ghost. In these three things, their trinity came, and they became the affirmers and believers of taslis.

So in reality, it was not so. Hazrat `Isa` was not giving such a teaching. But when Hazrat `Isa` used to call out, "Father, Father, listen to me," the people used to understand that they are calling out to a father, so they must be sons. And they used to say that Jibril is coming to me and bringing me this message, just as prophets used to say in their time. So when `Isa` used to say this in his time, and people used to say that, O `Isa`, who came to you and who brought and delivered this message? He would say the Ruh al-Qudus brought it. So the Ruh al-Qudus brought it, so these people established the Trinity: Father, Son, and Ruh al-Qudus. So in this way, these followers of theirs, those who were their followers, had made this kind of taslis. Otherwise, he, na'udhubillah, na'udhubillah, was a worshipper of tawhid, and he was doing the parastari of the One God.

Well, the era of taslis also came, and his followers divided it into three, three gods. But after this, an era came when in Iran this idea was born that this taslis and all these 365 days of a year and dividing them among gods, all these things are wrong. In reality, we see that in this world there are only two things: good and evil. Good or evil. Whoever does anything, some work will be good or some work will be bad. Good and evil, heaven and hell, virtue and vice. We see only these two concepts, of good and evil. For this reason, we think that in the world there can only be two things, only two deities can exist, only two gods can exist. And who are they? Ahraman and Yazdan. Ahraman and Yazdan, they named it. The Iranians. And Ahraman and Yazdan. That is, the god of evil is Ahraman and the avatar of virtue is Yazdan. So they presented the concept of Ahraman and Yazdan. And taking that concept, they moved forward. This was the era of jahiliyya, which is famous as the jahiliyya of the Arabs. And what should I describe to you about that jahiliyya? You know that the Arab had become an abode of every kind of evil. And all evils were present in them. There was no such defect of the world that was not present in those Arabs before the arrival of the Sarwar-e-Kainat. When the zuhur of the Sarwar-e-Kainat happened, your sacred zuhur, and you, Sarwar-e-Kainat, came into the world, at that time this was the situation. And you, `huwa alladhi ba'atha fil-ummiyyina rasulan` (He it is Who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves), when this verse came and you were made a nabiyy, then the very first thing you did was this, that look, it is not so, O people, because the example was being given before you, of taslis too, and of many gods too, and the closest matter that was coming was of two gods. The matter of the two gods of Iran was coming. So the Prophet said that look, my Quran, the word of Allah, has come down upon this, and what does this word say? You think and understand, use your intellect, and think, and do not fall into such disgrace. These two gods, three gods, all these things are wrong. God, His being is one, and it should not be divided in this way.

To explain this, you presented this verse of the Quran Majeed: `law kana fihima alihatun illallahu lafasadata` (If there had been in them any gods except Allah, they would both have certainly been in a state of disorder). If there were two gods, O people, then remember this universe would have been ruined. There would be destruction, and complete destruction would occur. One god would say, "Let it rain," the other god would say, "Don't let it rain." Today, just as is the condition of your sheikhs, the situation of squabbling, at that time what the condition of the gods would have been, you can imagine. So in this way, if it were so, then the whole system… one would say that I will make the sun rise from the east, the other would say I will make the sun rise from the west. One would say that the sun has been given heat and the moon has been given coolness, the other god would say, no, from today the moon has been given heat and the sun has been given coolness. What would happen then? It would become a matter of great chaos. So na'udhubillah, these concepts are extremely nonsensical concepts. And the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, refuted them and explained that look, leave all these things and you people have fallen into misguidance. And you people, consider that one institution cannot have two directors. One scabbard cannot hold two swords. One place cannot have two masters. How do you accept two gods? `law kana fihima alihatun illallahu lafasadata.` And he refuted it and you said that no, it cannot be, you must believe in one God.

When the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, was presenting this thing, the Muslims, who were they? They were but-parast. They were worshippers of Lat, Manat, and Hubul. They were those who had many wives; the situation was that some had 100, some 200, some 300 wives. Whatever they were, and how they were, they ate these animals, and what animals did they eat, you know? They ate crocodiles. Along with eating goat meat, they would also roast and eat the goat's skin. They ate crocodiles. They ate elephants. They drank blood. So this was their condition. The state of their evil habits was this, and the state of the tribes' savageness was this, that a man, after killing an enemy, would remove his skin and drink wine in his skull. Women would dye their clothes with his blood. And the situation was such that for target practice, to aim correctly, they would use children, placing children and then aiming. So this was the peak of barbarism. Such barbaric people, such uncivilized Arabs, of which you all are having a good experience. Beyond this, nothing more can be said. Such Arabs, whom the Sarwar-e-Kainat, the Mercy to the Worlds, was setting right, and you are seeing that today 65 Muslim states are glittering with Islam. This wave of Islam that spread, the Sarwar-e-Kainat spread it. And what must have been your efforts? What effort must not have been made? You can imagine, they were being put on hot sand, entrails were being thrown on your head, you were being beaten, you were called mad, called a poet, you were given all the bad titles of the world. Your name was Muhammad, and you were called Muzammam. Muzammam is being said. That is, the reviled one is being said. Muhammad means the praised one, not, but Muzammam is being said. So the Prophet endured all the taunts. For what? For guidance. And you used to say, O Lord, save my community from misguidance. And like Nuh, you did not curse that my community should be destroyed. Like Hazrat Ibrahim, you did not do that. Just like Hazrat Adam or Musa and `Isa`, but you endured it, and after enduring it you said that, O Lord, they do not know, if they understand, it would be very good. Do not send down Your punishment upon them, O Lord. Do not send down punishment upon them. So this was the Mercy to the Worlds.

So the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, used to teach this. But what happens is, the real point is this, that the people who are attached, attached how? You will think, being attached by the hem, meaning sitting very close, they became attached. Or, if a person living is very far away, but his heart is connected, then even if he is a lakh of miles away, he is near. And if you are sitting very near, and your heart hates him, then you are very far. So this is a simple matter. In the same way, those who were sitting near the Prophet of God, you must be thinking that they must have received mercy and they must have understood all things well from the Prophet of God. No. It is dark right under the lamp. It is dark right under the lamp. You cannot see light under it. So it was the same situation. I mean, those sitting with the Prophet of God, among them was his uncle Abu Lahab, Abu Jahl was also there. These kafirs were also there. So everyone came. So did they all become pure? Did they become Muslims? Was there true Islam in their hearts? Nothing was there. So you will say, they used to sit and stand with the Prophet of God day and night. So I am telling you that this is guidance. Whoever got it, got it. It is guidance for whoever wants to take it. He who moved forward, took guidance. He who stayed back, did not find guidance.

So the Prophet of God was giving this guidance to everyone, that look, the very first thing I teach you is to practice tawhid of Rabb al-'Alamin, recite the kalimah of la ilaha illallah. There is no god worthy of worship except Allah. What happened then? People came and wanted to give gold equal to Jabal Abi Qubays. A mountain. A mountain of gold. And they said, we will provide you with a legion of the most beautiful women. You take all this. And we will give you the government of the entire Arab world in your hands, you can rule as you wish. The Prophet said, I need neither wealth, nor beauty, nor government, nor gold. I don't need anything, O people. So they said, this Prophet is strange. He is not ready to take anything and be persuaded. So how to convince him now? So the last resort that exists, the first is targhib, the second is tarhib. The first is targhib, after that is tarhib, after that is tarkib. What happens in targhib? Giving temptation. They gave temptation to the Prophet, he didn't accept. And after that, they started tarhib. Tarhib means beating and killing. Calling you names, calling you mad, calling you a poet. They inflicted so much pain that these words came from the Prophet's mouth: `ma udhiya nabiyyun mithla ma udhitu` (No prophet was harmed as I was harmed). What pain must not have been inflicted? All this pain. But they saw that despite giving pain, this nabiyy is patient and grateful. Then they got tired.

Now they used a third resort. What was that resort? Tarkib. And what is tarkib called? Compromise. This is the strategy of Satan. Compromise. What does compromise mean? You believe some of our things, we will believe some of yours. You bend a little, we will bend a little. This is what happens. So to make a compromise, they told the Prophet that, O Messenger of Allah, we will do this, we will make some compromise with each other. This very compromise Allah Ta'ala has described in the Surah of `qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun` (Say: O you disbelievers). You read that Surah, you will find out. Otherwise, they finally told the Prophet that, O Messenger of Allah, they are not going to agree. Allah Ta'ala says that they will never agree. Because what had they done? This Surah came down at the time when they came before the Prophet and said, look, Messenger of Allah, let's do one thing, so that you are also happy and we are also happy. You don't speak ill of our gods, we won't speak ill of your God. We, we will worship our gods, you worship your god. We will also... and if you insist a lot, we will also include your God among our gods. There were 365 gods, what's the delay in them becoming 366 gods? But you do this one thing. So the Prophet said, no, what is the point of accepting this? So they, the others said, that such a Prophet will not agree, we have to be a bit cunning. So they were cunning. What did they do? They said that, O Messenger of Allah, all this is acceptable. We accept everything of yours. Do one thing. Don't make us recite this kalimah of `la ilaha illallah`. These were Arabs. You understood? These were those Arabs, those uncivilized Arabs, who came before the Prophet and said this. Leave this kalimah, and you kindly change this kalimah by one kalimah. And that kalimah should be this: `Allahu ilahun` (Allah is one among the gods). That `la ilaha illallah` which is causing a big commotion, which is piercing the heart, is causing us great pain. You, please change this to `Allahu ilahun`. The matter was the same. What was its meaning? `Allahu ilahun` means that God is one among the gods. Meaning, the Prophet was being told that among all the gods, your God is also one. It was the same thing. The Prophet said, no, this cannot be. I am trying to say that I am negating the godhood of all gods, as if wiping them out with a wrong pen, and establishing my God. And you are saying that... no. You must do the parastari of the One God.

So you made the parastari of the One God... to make them understand, you said that you all recite the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah`, you will become pure. When you said this, and when some people... who were they? Only one woman, who came forward, she was Hazrat Khadijah al-Kubra, your wife. And only one boy, who was eight years old, who was `Maula-e-Kainat` `Amir al-Mu'minin` `Ali`. And only one man, who came forward later, who was Hazrat Abu Bakr. That's it. So all this happened and they became Muslims. But no virtue is established from this. If virtue were established, then they would have also kept Islam properly. They did not keep Islam properly.

So the point is that when the Prophet made them recite this kalimah, after making them recite the kalimah, they began to say, "Look, I am telling you, but... its explanation... telling is my job, explaining is not my job." Just listen to this point. Telling is my job, explaining is not my job. For explaining, this Ali is sitting. This is my mubayyin, my musharrih, this is the one who explains, this is my wasi, this is my wazir, this is my brother, this is the one who explains all things. Ali is the one who explains everything. You listen from me, and understand from Ali. My job is only to tell, Ali's job will be to make you understand.

Now the situation was such that if they had become attached to Amir al-Mu'minin, then correct knowledge would have come to them. We tell you that look, among you, in your view, `shi'an-e-Ali` is famous. Who are `shi'an-e-Ali` called? The party of Ali. People of Ali's party. Today, there are hundreds of thousands of Shias present. Did the Shias who are connected to Hazrat `Ali`, did they get that explanation of the Prophet? If the Shias had gotten that explanation today, then today their condition would not be with the Sunnis. So it turns out that one who has no history, what would he have gotten from Ali? Because we... there were only a handful of people, who could be counted on fingers. Amir al-Mu'minin, with whom they used to be attached, and from whom they used to learn things, they were a few who... with whom, in reality, we have been attached, they were Hazrat Salman al-Farsi, they were Hazrat Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, they were Abu Dharr al-Ghiffari, they were 'Ammar ibn Yasir, they were... these great personalities, Hudhayfa al-Yamani, these were those great personalities of religion, they were the shining lamps of Islam, they were the mountains of knowledge, who, in the court of Amir al-Mu'minin and in the court of the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, used to sit, used to listen, and they used to learn. And those attached to them were our ancestors, attached to them were our A'immah, attached to them were our du'at, attached to them were we. We became attached to these du'at, because of which this 'ilm came to us, and this became our wirsa.

So now you imagine how reality is reached. So the Prophet had said that look, my job is only to convey the kalimah, and this... you... look, I will tell you a special thing about it. The Prophet said that `man qala la ilaha illallah dakhala al-jannah` (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' will enter Paradise). Whoever recites the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah`, he will enter paradise. And after that, you turned towards Amir al-Mu'minin and smiled, looked at him, and then said, `man qala la ilaha illallah mukhlisan dakhala al-jannah` (Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' with sincerity will enter Paradise). Whoever recites the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah` with sincerity, he will enter paradise. So with sincerity... now people were astonished that just now the Prophet has said that whoever recites the kalimah will enter, then again... so you explained that, "O people, I am saying and I am also explaining it, that with sincerity." People said that, "O Messenger of Allah, what is that sincerity?" You said that, "Whatever you have to understand, understand from Ali." Listen from me and understand from Ali. So it turns out that the one who explains sincerity is Ali. So what happened? That those who were attached to Ali, they understood tawhid correctly. The Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, those attached to him were who? Muslims. These all Muslims, they had heard the Prophet say this, and they said, "That's it, we have heard tawhid from the Prophet, we will go to paradise." And they went away, and reached their tribes. And they got involved in the same life of comfort and pleasure. And they said that we have heard it. Now because we have accepted the Prophet, accepted Islam, so let's believe in the One God, `la ilaha illallah`... just as today you see the condition of Muslims, that they recite the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah` one lakh times, recite it two lakh times, recite it so many times that their heart starts to race. They recite it so many times that boxes of custard apple seeds are prepared, that this is of two lakhs, this is of three lakhs, such boxes of seeds are brought and kept, and on them, two lakh times the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah` is recited. So does the kalimah of `la ilaha illallah` pass down the throat by reciting it two lakh, three lakh times? Hey, reciting the kalimah just once is enough, but it has to be recited with sincerity. You recite it two lakh, three lakh times, who has told you to? So just as Muslims are doing today, the Muslims of before have also done this. These are their descendants. These are their descendants. Who have turned their faces away from the Prophet in this manner... close the door. Who have turned their faces away from the Prophet in this manner, and they have done wrong.

Hazrat `Ali ibn Abi Talib` was the one who explained the true meanings and subtleties, and he explained that look, reciting the kalimah with sincerity is this, that you believe this... अरे, you, if all Muslims, even today, I am saying that, that all Muslims today, you pick up any book, take any thing, take any tafsir, you will see that among them this thing is written, that God is one. God is one. Is God one? It is wrong. You will say, what? God is not one? Hey, we have been hearing this since childhood that God is one. The matter, in fact, is this. There is a difference between speaking and understanding. Hazrat `Ali ibn Abi Talib` said that look, this kalimah of the Prophet is explaining that God is one, this is not it, but it is explaining that God is `ekta` (unique). You will say, if you say God is `ekta`, it still means one. No, there is a difference of heaven and earth between `ek` (one) and `ekta` (unique). God is not one, God is unique. There is a big difference. You understood? Meaning, Amir al-Mu'minin explained this, that in considering God as one, it will be that God, if he is one among humans, one among woods, one among fans, one among lamps, then God is one god among gods. By saying one, this becomes necessary. This is what philosophy and `mantiq` teach. You said that never call God one, but whenever you speak of God, what should you say? God is `ekta`. God is unique. This is what you should say. For this reason, in the Quran Majeed, you see, what has come? `qul huwa allahu... ahad` (Say, He is Allah, the Unique). Say `wahid`. No, `wahid`? No, not `wahid`. What is the meaning of `wahid`? And you are well-versed in Arabic. What is the meaning of `wahid`? One. And the meaning of `ahad`? `ekta`. So in the Quran itself it has come that `qul huwa allahu ahad`. That say that Allah is `ekta`. Despite this clear, explicit statement, what do Muslims today say? God is one. Is saying God is one correct? Hey, God is `ekta`. God Himself is saying, `lam yalid wa lam yulad` (He begets not, nor is He begotten). He is negating all things, that He has no son, nor does He have a father for anyone, nor... `wa lam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad` (And there is none like unto Him). Hey, He has no equal, no peer, no opposite, no peer. He cannot be counted in any way. What are you people holding onto? So all these things were negated by the Quran Majeed. And it has said it clearly and explicitly. So it is known that all Muslims, because they are of the Prophet's `tanzil`'s quality, and Amir al-Mu'minin is of the `ta'wil`'s quality. They are of the exoteric quality, this is of the esoteric quality. They are exoteric worshippers, and they only want to take from the nabiyy. They don't even turn towards Ali, they don't want to learn from Ali. So because of this aversion, what happened? The whole of Islam went wrong. I told you, that if a... a brick is placed... if a foundation is laid with a crooked brick, the wall will go up crooked. So this fundamental thing went wrong for the Muslims. The entire concept of God of the Muslims got distorted. Did you see, brother? The entire concept got distorted. You will say, brother, I can show you books where Muslims have also written that God is `ekta` at their own place. They definitely write it, they have written it in some places, in prose. But they don't believe it, do they? They don't accept it in that way, in that manner of interpretation. And well, well, if we even assume that they believe it, that God, they have written `ekta` somewhere and they also believe in `ekta`, some Muslims. Even so, they have not believed it in the right way. For this reason, the Prophet's wasi, Amir al-Mu'minin `Ali`, said and explained for all of life, the biggest task you accomplished was giving us the lesson of `tawhid Rabb al-'Alamin`. And for `tawhid Rabb al-'Alamin`, he explained that you should understand that look, O people, this `nawwad o nunam` that you speak of, this `dhanniyan o naam` that you recite, which is also recorded in our sahifas, so you should read it with understanding, what these `nawwad o nunam` are. `la karimu ya rahim, ya qa'im ya da'im, ya 'alim ya ra'uf, ya rahman, ya quddus ya mu'min ya muhaimin`, all these things you keep saying, and you... now when the zikr comes, what do you say? That Allah is `'alim mutlaq` (absolute knower). Allah is `raziq mutlaq` (absolute provider). What does it mean? That... if Allah is `'alim mutlaq`, `raziq mutlaq`, then you are also something in your own place. So, that means that when you said `mutlaq`, then you also became some kind of `'alim`, didn't you? Only then are you `mutlaq`. So the word `mutlaq` had to be added. If He is `mutlaq`, then you are also a little `'alim`. So being called an `'alim` itself became shirk. And if this is not shirk, then come, I will explain it to you with logic. With logic. For example, that Allah is `'alim`. Allah is `'alim`. So first I will tell you that Hazrat `Ali` explained that these 99 names, snatch them from Allah. Not a single name can apply to Him. अरे, these are His creation. These are the names of His creation. Allah, whom no one has seen nor recognized, neither understood nor comprehended, nor has any clue or address, and does not know anything, for Him just say `hu` (He), just point, say nothing other than that. So when we can only point to Him, we cannot say anything to Him, then in what way do we describe Him with attributes? We can never describe Him with attributes. ...what difference would it have made? Tell me. Allah is `'alim mutlaq`. Alright. Allah is `'alim mutlaq`. So what does it mean? He is the fountainhead of knowledge, the content is there. Alright. Allah is `'alim mutlaq`. So Allah became `'alim mutlaq` only when He has knowledge of something. So we will say, what does He have knowledge of? So it's clear, what is the biggest thing? The world. He has knowledge of the universes, and that's why He is `'alim`. Right? So it turns out that the universes exist, whose knowledge He has, and because of having this knowledge, He is `'alim`. So three things emerged. One is the universes, so it is the `ma'lum` (the known). It is called the `ma'lum`. And its `'ilm` (knowledge) is a second thing. And the one who has its knowledge became the third thing, the `'alim` (the knower). `'alim`, `ma'lum`, `'ilm`. One is God. He has knowledge of what? Of the world. And the `'ilm` of the world, what is it? It's a separate thing, the `'ilm`. And so it turns out that God of the Muslims cannot become an `'alim` as long as the world does not exist. So it turns out that their, the Muslims' God, is `muhtaj` (dependent) on the world. If the world exists, then he will be called an `'alim`. A wonderful point. It is from `mantiq`, it has been proven by `mantiq`. And in the same way, there is power, the powerful, the kind, the merciful, you take all things, take three things each, it's over. So it turns out that when he, whether you call him `'alim mutlaq`, it cannot be anything. We are... now you, the world... Hazrat `Amir al-Mu'minin` explained that the world is made of `sabab wa musabbab`. It is made of `athr wa mu'aththir`. It is made of `'illat wa ma'lul`. Meaning, here a thing is made, so it becomes the cause for making something. And from this `sabab wa musabbab`, the entire creation of the world has happened. It might have happened from water, from fire, from air, from earth. It might have happened from some elements, but it has definitely happened. So we, if we follow the chain of all these things, the last cause that comes, all Muslims, their view on this is that `The last cause is the God`. The last cause is God. What do we say? Hazrat `Ali` has taught us, `The last cause is not the God`. `The creator of the last cause is the God`. Did you see? How big a difference there is. That the creator of the last cause is God. He... all Muslims say this... our `mu'min`, `mu'min`, `muhaimin`, `rahman`, `rahim`, these all... `nawwad o nunam`, `dhanniyan o naam`, are the names of Allah. We say that first, what is a name? Amir al-Mu'minin explained to us, what is a name? A name... of anything... if you today, instead of calling a handkerchief a handkerchief, call it a watch. Is there any power for anyone to say that today, instead of a watch, someone should call a handkerchief... a watch? He will say, "You have gone mad." Hey, this is a watch. I will say, "Hey, this is not a watch, it is a handkerchief." He will say, "We... you... you have your own... the whole world calls this a handkerchief, you are calling it a watch." So what the whole world called a watch, today... what the whole world called shoes, you are calling it shoes, otherwise, if the whole world had named it a cap, it would have become a cap. And the name of the cap would have become shoes, it would have become shoes. So what would you say? So it is known that a name is that by which a thing is known. `ma yajur bihi al-shay'`. That by which a thing is known. If you don't name anything in the world, then no thing is recognized. For this reason, you name your children, you have your own name, everyone has... so that there is recognition. Otherwise, how would you be recognized? And if in some place, there are three or four Ahmads, and there are four or five Alis, and some other names have come up, then there will be juniors and seniors. Meaning, they will be called small and big, or they will be number one, number two, number three. In some way or another, they make some signs so that you can call them by that name.

So a name is that by which a thing is known. So that by which the `ma'rifat` of Allah can be obtained, the beings that make us recognize God, in reality, they are His names. So there are some spiritual beings, whose mention will come, I will do it before you. They are spiritual beings, spiritual servants, and when they were created, where they were created, how they were, what they were, what they were not, all will be mentioned. I am just saying that there are some such people who, in reality, have become `Rahman` and `Rahim`, have become `Mannan` and `Karim`, have become `Ra'uf` and `Rahman`, have become... they are such servants, by whom the `ma'rifat` of God is obtained, and they have become the names of God. So the names of God, they themselves have become. How can it be his name? He is nameless and without a trace. He is free from description. He is transcendent. So he can neither be known nor recognized, nor can he be thought of. So thought, imagination, and suspicion, the one who does not come into them, he does not come into anything. He has no title, no address, no clue. And there is nothing. The Prophet has said that you cannot deny that you are seeing this entire universe. Pick up a single leaf and see, pick up a single stone and see, you will see the signs of Allah Ta'ala. His `ma'rifat` will be seen. What power the Lord of the worlds has. A single drop of water is enough for you. So it is known that by seeing all these powers of Allah Ta'ala, we... its greatness... we acknowledge its greatness. So those who gave you all this information, who explained it to you, through them his `ma'rifat` is obtained. So Hazrat `Ali` explained to us that you should separate all these names from Allah Ta'ala, then in reality you will do `tawhid`. You will separate the names, then you will do `tawhid`. The Muslims say that you will take one name at a time and apply it, then `tawhid` will happen. Did you see? What a difference there is between us and the Muslims. Whether he is a Shia, a Sunni, or so-and-so, a Mu'tazili, or from a sect, any sect, any practice, anyone, pick up any sect and see, there they are all calling by these names. We are removing the names, and the true `tawhid` of Allah is being established. True `tawhid` is being established for us, and their `tawhid` is being distorted. As they add names, in the clean, clear mirror, hairs are appearing. And that concept, the divine concept, which is completely pure, which Allah Ta'ala is saying, especially in the Quran Majeed, `shahida allahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa` (Allah bears witness that there is no god but He). Allah has given witness that there is no god worthy of worship except `hu`. `hu`, `hu` means a pointer. Only a pointer. So when the Prophet, alayhis salatu was salam, is saying this in the Quran by the command of Allah, then what right do you have, sir, to remember him by 99 names? You will say that in the Quran Shareef, Allah Ta'ala has described 99 of his own names. `huwa al-musawwiru al-quddusu al-mu'minu al-muhayminu`, all these, line after line, he has described his names. Hey, the names he has described are of those people whom Allah Ta'ala... who provide his true `ma'rifat`. He is not giving his own `ma'rifat`, he is giving the `ma'rifat` of the people he created. But you are applying it to Allah. For this reason, if it were not so, then this verse would not have come in the Quran Majeed, `ta'ala Allahu 'amma yasifun` (Exalted is Allah above what they describe). Just ponder on this. `ta'ala Allahu 'amma yasifun`. Exalted is the Lord of the worlds from what the people describe in His attribute. What does it mean? That these people who describe the attributes, that He is `Rahman`, `Rahim`, `Raziq`, so-and-so, Allah Ta'ala is exalted from this. So it is known that all these attributes should be removed. They are removed. When all these attributes are removed, this verse comes, so we ask the Muslims that this `ta'ala Allahu 'amma yasifun`, what verse is this? "Oh, these are all just things, just for Allah." Hey, it is for Allah, but what is He saying? One verse is like the staff of Musa for these Muslims. To silence them, to finish them, it's just a pinch of salt to be placed on the tongue and it's over. This is a cyanide for them. They cannot answer this. What can these Muslims stand before us? So I was telling you that you see, if we present this verse, `ta'ala Allahu 'amma yasifun`, the Lord of the worlds is exalted from what the people describe in His attribute, so what meaning can the Muslims give for this? Those who are sitting with 99 names, so what... You see, in how many places posters are put up, in how many places... put them all up, but your concept has changed. Your concept has changed. For example, you are... as you have said, "Son." I have seen you and said, "Father." You are also speaking the truth, I am also speaking the truth. In what way am I speaking? That you are the father of the son. You are saying that you are the son of your father. If there were no attribution, the names would be invalidated. But what is here? Here, these attributes are of the people created by Allah Ta'ala. And they have applied it to Him. For this reason, Amir al-Mu'minin has absolved him from all these attributes and said that he is free from all attributes. And for this reason, it has come in the Quran that `shahida allahu annahu la ilaha illa huwa`. That Allah's testimony has not been given by anyone except `hu`. Meaning, say `hu`. So these are two things. Now, Hazrat `Ali` has said that when you Muslims... we admonish them. To us, you... who were attached to your hem, who were holding your hem, you taught them that look, the true `tawhid` of Islam is not what the Muslims practice `tawhid` in this way. This is all wrong, and the Muslims are misguided. Hazrat `Ali` has said that the Muslims are severely misguided. You pick up any book, any `tafsir` of the Quran Majeed, go and grab any Muslim `maulvi`, you will find out that there you pick up and see the Quran Shareef, see their `tafsir`, see their books, in them it is clearly written that Allah Ta'ala is `qadim` (eternal) and the world is also `qadim` (eternal). Fine. When both things are `qadim`, then what happened to Allah? A companion was created. Didn't you understand? Neither is Allah's opposite nor his peer, nor his equal nor anything. Hey, he is the one who creates the non-existent from non-existence. Neither in our intellect nor in our understanding, in anything... Hey, a... a... a chair, the one who makes it is a carpenter. Does the chair have the power to recognize the carpenter? It cannot be. The creation can never recognize the creator. So how is it possible that the `ma'rifat` of the creator can be obtained? It cannot be. So people used to think, and even today in the era you see that people do `chilla`, people do `tapasya`, they do meditation, they go to forests. These are all absurdities. Utter absurdity. And in Muslims you will see, there is `zikr`, they sit with a cloth on, they have also given it some names, and some meditations happen, `muraqabas` happen. These are all deceptions, and they are all lowly things, absurdities. These are things to cheat. Absurdities. What? And what do they sit and do? When we ask them, "Sir, what are you doing?" Because you people are just hearing this, because you people have not seen it. We have not just seen it, but have participated in it. So that we can also taste its flavor and see how it is. So when they start to do `zikr`, they put on a cloth. Then they said that one person will sit and do `zikr`, so loneliness will bother him. So include another person. So alright, you... there is a cloth on my head, I will put it on your head too. Now both of you have sat down, now `zikr-e-ilahi` has started. `la ilaha illallah`. You are also hitting your head, he is also hitting his head. Now reaching, reaching the state where sometimes heads are colliding, sometimes this way, sometimes that way, sometimes this way, sometimes that way. Meaning, the frenzy of `la ilaha` has taken over so much that now you have gone here and there. So all these absurdities are going on. Among Muslims.

So Hazrat `Ali` has explained that look, this will not work by just doing `zikr-vikr`. You will recite the `kalimah` once, but if you recite it in the right way, then that `tawhid` will be `tawhid`, otherwise you will ruin the `tawhid`.

So even today, if you read the books of the Muslims, in them you will find that the world is `qadim` (eternal), and... because these discussions have become very long, that the world is `hadith` (created) or `qadim`. Meaning, new or old. They say, "The world cannot be `hadith`, it must be so old. How much time has passed since Adam, alayhis salam? How many generations have been born from Baba Adam?" They say, "Alright, the world is `qadim`, and Allah is also `qadim`." Hey, how can you join two `qadims`? You say something about it. So it is clear that if they bring the discussion of `qadim-qadim`, then... Ali was the one who erased all these things, who refuted this, who erased it and you said that look, if you want to do true `tawhid`, then you first have to remove `shirk`. Just listen. You have to remove `shirk`. Meaning, `shirk`... you will say that we are not making anyone a partner of Allah Ta'ala. Why aren't you making a partner? In considering the world as `qadim` and Allah as `qadim`, did you not become a partner? You have done `shirk`. How is `shirk` done? He explained that `shirk`. You will say, "Hey, I believe Allah is `wahdahu la sharik` (One, He has no partner), so that... he is not a partner to anyone. No one helps him in his work. He is handling such a big task, the whole world. He must need a lot of help. So let's make some assistant, that would be good." This is... `na'udhubillah`, who will he make? But I will tell you that we also commit `shirk`. `na'udhubillah`, `na'udhubillah`. We also commit `shirk`. This is the point I want to tell you. This is the main point. How do we commit `shirk`? The point is that we consider Allah Ta'ala as pure and clean, we do everything. But you understand, for example, here a... a... hypnotist's show has come, or some... play has come to you, someone has come to you and shown his powers, etc., for that, some demonstration has been done. So understand hypnotism. He showed you that he can make you a child, he goes to the theory of reincarnation, to the theory of rebirth, he tells you some new things, miracles, and you see them and you are amazed, "O Allah!" This world of consciousness, subconsciousness, and superconsciousness... that God who, our Lord of the worlds, is the master of all powers, is the master of all wonders, is the master of all things, and He Himself is the master of creating it, you, in his praise, did not say `subhanallah`, if you had said that, "Exalted is the Lord who created such a man," "Exalted is the Lord who is pure and clean, who has bestowed such powers on man," if you had said this, the `shirk` would have ended. You put a period to it. So you saw, this `shirk` was created. Or you saw "That's Incredible." "What power!" "What a great thing!" "This is absolutely impossible." "How is he doing this?" "What kind of power is this?" If you had said `subhanallah` there, you would have been saved. If you had said `mashallah`, you would have been saved. You neither say `mashallah` nor `subhanallah`. You are clapping, or you are just saying, "Wow, wow, wow." So in saying "wow, wow," if there is even a particle of the concept that... that... "there is no man greater than him." And what is happening? Now these people who perform these programs, you go and ask them. They believe that they are gods in their own right. That is, it is an impossible thing that they are doing. For this reason, this is the biggest thing.

So this, in reality, is this defect, and this creates `shirk`. For this reason, what did the Prophet say? Do you know? `al-shirku fi ummati... akhafa min dabib al-naml al-aswad 'ala al-sakhra al-sawda' fi al-layla al-zulma' 'ala al-sakhra al-sawda'` (Shirk in my ummah is more hidden than the crawling of a black ant on a black rock on a dark night on a black rock). `Shirk` is hidden in my ummah in such a way as the crawling of a black ant on a black rock on a dark night. The crawling of a black ant on a black rock on a dark night, as it is hidden, in the same way, `shirk` is rampant in my ummah. You will say, "The Prophet has said it, so... mashallah." So now you... the Prophet is saying it is hidden in my ummah. So it is in the ummah, isn't it? It is hidden. So this is the `shirk` where you did not say `subhanallah` or `mashallah`, and you just... praised it, so there you have joined with God. So this `shirk` is happening in us. It is the biggest sin. And you know that among the major sins, the biggest sin is `shirk`. To associate a partner with Allah. How many times are we making this mistake? May Allah forgive us. Because this is the biggest sin. There is no sin bigger than this. `shirk`.

So this... now what is `kufr`, what is `shirk`, what is `irtidad`, which is called `murtad`, what is `mulhid`, these are all terms, I am leaving all these things because the discussion will become longer. So leaving that, I am saying that Amir al-Mu'minin has taught us that look, if you want to practice `tawhid`, then the pure, clean `imani` `tawhid` is this, its summary is this, in just a few words you have explained, and in what unparalleled way you have explained, that `tawhid` is the name of three things. `tawhid`, `tawhid` is the name of three things. One is what? `Tawhid`. The second is `tanzih`. And the third is `tajrid`. What? `Tawhid`, `tanzih`, `tajrid`. `Tawhid` means that you consider God as `ekta` (unique). `Tanzih` means that you purify God. `Tajrid` means that the power of creating from nothing, you should reserve it for Allah. And I will explain it. Just listen carefully. `Tawhid` means to consider Allah as `ekta`. How will it be possible to consider Allah as `ekta`? As long as you do not consider yourself as `ekta`. You are also `ekta` in your own place, you are unique. You will say, "Wow, today I have also become something in my own place. I had not understood this. Today, my position has also become something." Sir, He, Allah, is unique, so He has also created you unique. Your individuality is established. If individuality were not established, then you... you would have become someone else. There is a difference of heaven and earth between you and another. You will say, "I am his brother." Hey, sir, in the capacity of being a brother, there will be a blood relation, everything will be there. But your nature is hot, his nature is cold. You like cold, he likes hot. You are like this, he is like that. You will find a world of differences between two brothers. So what are these things? The point I am making is that you should consider yourself as `ekta` in your own place, that there is no one like me. And the one who created me is also an `ekta` being. He has created me `ekta`. You understood? I am also created `ekta`. There is no one like me. You will say, "Wow, our two eyes... everyone is sitting... we have a nose, we have a mouth, we have two limbs. We feel cold and hot, everyone feels it." You will say, "We are like..." Hey, if you want to show resemblance, then just look at the faces, no one's face will match another's. You will say, "No sir, a lot of resemblance has come out, there are duplicates, triplicates of Hitler." If you want to bring it out like that, then I can convince you with another resort. If you have found someone's face to be like another's in the world, then I will tell you that Allah Ta'ala has made your faces different for this very reason, to show your individuality, that I am also `ekta`, and I will also create you `ekta`. I will create you `ekta`, I will maintain your individuality. And if you don't understand this, then to show your individuality, He has put a seal. What is that seal? Your thumb. You don't know how to sign, just like your sheikh, so what does he do? He puts his thumbprint. He puts his thumbprint. He doesn't know how to sign, what can he do? He is a sheikh. So he doesn't sign, so he puts his thumbprint. So what is the thumbprint? That the lines on this, those lines do not match any other line. Wow! Hey sir, 10 people, 15 people, 20 people, 100, 200, 1500, a thousand, two thousand, it will match someone's. Hey, it will not match lakhs of people's, it will not match crores of people's, it will not match anyone's. So if no one's matches anyone's, then what thing did not match? Only the thumb. Hey, look at the size of the thumb, and look at the lines in it, and look at the crores of humans, and the matter of thumb impression is going on in such a way that it has been recorded, and the computer is working, and from it, it immediately finds the criminals and separates them and tells. So it is known that the power that is there, this seal has been put. This seal has been put to show that your individuality is established. This seal is there.

So Amir al-Mu'minin has taught us that look, you are `ekta` in your own place. So `tawhid` means that we... from a religious perspective, the way we will define it, we will say from a religious perspective that the Lord of the worlds is `ekta`, and He, whether it is the physical world or the spiritual world, all the boundaries, whether physical or spiritual, He has created them as `ekta` in their own place. He has created them `ekta` at their respective levels. This is defining it in the language of shari'ah. Now, if you have not understood that, "Sir, what did you say, that He has created them as `ekta` in their own place?" I will explain it to you in a moment. I will tell you, are all of you believers or not? You will say, "Wow, alhamdulillah, we are believers, we are Sulaimanis." Alright. I will ask you that do you all give importance to salat or not? The other person will say, "I give a lot of importance, and I give so much importance that I always tell my wife to pray salat." The wife says to the husband to pray salat. "I cannot pray, but I tell her that she must pray." This much is there. Or, that so-and-so person should fast on my behalf, and I also give him money, that you take this much money, sir, fast on my behalf. But the importance of fasting is there. But there is one who fasts himself. Some think that I don't perform Hajj, my Hajj-e-Badal... Hey, brother, do you have some chronic illness? Are you lame, crippled, na'udhubillah? Or have you got some dangerous disease? Why can't you go for Hajj? "I have heard that there is a large crowd of people there. The crowd, I am allergic to it. I cannot go. This allergy is a very terrible thing. This color allergy, crowd allergy, and God knows what else they will become allergic to." So what is it? He is not ready to go for Hajj. Oh, what a thing!

So now what is it? You see, everyone's concept is something else. In your view, what is it? That the best obligation Allah Ta'ala has established is that of zakat. "As long as you give money, you are free. This is a very good thing, sir. This is something where you are free by just giving money. I have a lot of bank balance, alhamdulillah, and I get free by giving this, I fulfill this obligation. The other obligations, I am excused from." Namaz, etc., may be missed, but other things... but look, this obligation I fulfill. I will ask you, he will say, "I take great care of purity, sir. Whatever happens, I maintain purity." So you all believe in all the obligations, but at the moment you are believing in one thing, another person is not believing in that thing. What the second person is believing, the third is not believing. You also accept it, but in some capacity. The importance you are giving to salat at this time, he is not giving. The importance he is giving, you are not giving. So it is known that our conception, our concept, is fluctuating. And because it is fluctuating, everyone's state is becoming different. So our form is becoming different. Just see, in the wave, you have given a slight movement, a movement like a hair's breadth, and the wave has gone somewhere else. The matter has gone somewhere else. Just now you were listening to the BBC, now it has gone somewhere else. Now from where did you start catching it? So it is known that with a difference of a hair's breadth, it goes somewhere else. If there was a difference of a hair's breadth, then instead of reaching the moon, it would have reached somewhere else. So it is known that aiming the target is a very difficult matter. Our thoughts and concepts, man cannot get out of this world of concepts. Man does not get out of this shell. He is a slave of concepts. And because of that, his thoughts are moving away.

So it is known that man is with his concept. And he cannot get out of this world of concepts. So this fluctuation that happens, because of that this has to be believed, that you are `ekta` in your own place. And the other believer, he is `ekta` at his own level. You will say, "No, there is some difference, it is like this, it is like that." So you, inshallah, in the next lesson you will find out how this difference was created. All things will come. And that is what is called the `tartib` of `musafa`. "Hey, brother, everything is fine with us, but this `tartib` of `musafa`, I don't understand. So-and-so sir is much younger than me, how is he going on top? I don't understand." This is very... it is against the spirit. That one who is going up, this thing I don't like. Everything else is fine, this `musafa`... The other gentleman says that what you have put in this `tartib`, I don't like `musafa` at all. "Hey, why? What is this, listening to the hand? I don't understand. What is this `musafa`, `musafa`?" So this `musafa` will also come, the `tartib` of `musafa` will also come, inshallah, and its details will also come before you, inshallah.

So what I was saying is that in terms of concept, our state is different. So Amir al-Mu'minin explained that you should consider the high and low orders as `ekta` in their own respective places, this in reality is `tawhid`. This is the `tawhid` he explained. `Tawhid`'s first part is `tawhid`. It is a part and also a division. The second thing is `tanzih`. `tanzih` means to purify. Meaning, Allah Ta'ala, na'udhubillah, is impure, so pour buckets of water and purify him? No, it's not like that. Impure means that the words that are attached to him, you snatch all of them from him. He needs to be purified. And what are those? These things that you have said, `Quddus`, `Mu'min`, `Muhaymin`, `Muhaiman`, these `nawwad o nunam`, snatch them from him and apply them to his creation. They are not befitting of him. This is called `tanzih`. `tajrid` is said for skinning a goat's hide. This is a daily observation, especially in Arabia, goats are slaughtered day and night. So you see, the skinning of a goat's hide is called `tajrid`. `tajrid` is said for... to establish `tajrid` for Allah Ta'ala, you do this, that all the creations, all the beings that exist, all the creation, from that entire creation, you take one thing, that to create from nothing, no one has the power. No one has the courage to create from nothing. You snatch this thing from everyone and reserve it for Allah Ta'ala, that only God's work is this, that he created from nothing. To do this is... you have said that this is `tajrid`. And you have said that whoever does `tawhid`, `tanzih`, and `tajrid`, he is a `muwahhid`. He is the one who does the `tawhid` of Allah. So in reality, who is the one who does `tawhid`? That `muwahhid` is the one who does `tanzih`, `tajrid`, and `tawhid`. The one who does `tawhid`, `tanzih`, `tajrid`, in reality, he is a `muwahhid`.

This is what Amir al-Mu'minin explained to us. Do the Muslims have this thing? No. The Muslims, they consider Allah as one, they do not consider Allah as `ekta`. And if they even say the word `ekta`, they do not accept it. They... from a philosophical perspective, they do not see it in that way. So it is clear that for the Muslims, they neither do `tajrid`, nor `tanzih`, nor `tawhid`. How will you consider them Muslims? How will you do `tawhid`? Because they had only heard from the Prophet, said `amanna billah`, accepted Islam, recited the `kalimah` of `la ilaha illallah`. And they apparently became Muslims. You may call them Muslims, but in their hearts, that Islam did not shine in the right way. It could not.

Well, I will end with this. After this, inshallah, I will describe to you that the Lord of the worlds, how He did the creation, how the `ruhaniyyat` came, and this `nawwad o nunam`, for whom it can be befitting, how were those creations created? And how did Allah Ta'ala create the spiritual world? This will be described tomorrow.

<!-- AUG:hazrat-zia lecture 2 -->

Now, what are those five things? These five fundamental beliefs which I have explained, they are five. They are the work of the heart. The work of the heart that I previously enumerated. After that are the acts of worship. The acts of worship, as you know, are *ṭahārah* (purity), *namāz* (prayer), *roza* (fasting), *zakāt* (alms), *ḥajj* (pilgrimage). But everything is at its own time. You will perform *jihād* when the *imām* appears. You will perform *ḥajj* once in a lifetime when you feel the need. If you have the means, you will have the capacity, you will have peace of mind, there will be no trouble, then you will make arrangements for your wife and children. You will fulfill the rights of your parents. You will perform *zakāt* when 40 rupees have accumulated with you, then one rupee from that you will give, or if you have 2.5%, you will pay the *zakāt*. When you have that much money. And in this way, you have to do it in such a way that you aren't fasting every day. No, only during Ramaḍān Sharīf will you fast. Allow Ramaḍān Sharīf to come, and get ready for fasting. What preparation? The preparation for *iftārī*. You prepare for *iftārī* for the fast. That's all. Whatever it is, you make preparations. Ramaḍān Sharīf is passing, and you are going to be people who fast, *alḥamdulillāh*, *alḥamdulillāh*. You have already prepared for it. The fasts will take place, Ramaḍān Sharīf will come, you will fast. Similarly, if you are *nāpāk* (ritually impure), you will perform *ṭahārah* (purification). If you have a minor ritual impurity, you will perform *wuḍū'*. If you have a major need, you will perform *ghusl*. But the thing that is always with you, the only thing, the only *farḍ* (obligation) from Allah is the five daily prayers. And that too, what has Allah done? He has kept such a time for it, that the first is the time of dawn. It doesn't happen that it's suddenly the time for *Fajr*. No. You know, you sleep late at night, now how will I pray *Fajr*? So Allah has said, don't worry, sleep, get up at two, three o'clock, what's the hurry? The time for *Ẓuhr*, it's a very good time. And during that time all the work is done, you get half an hour, and that too Allah has arranged in such a way that what will you eat? Okay. And similarly, the time for *'Aṣr*, for *Maghrib*. What a time. The time for *'Ishā'* is when everyone has had their dinner. So the five prayers are there. And in our religion, what has been done is that this has been divided into three prayer times. That is, *Maghrib* and *'Ishā'* can be prayed together, and *Ẓuhr* and *'Aṣr* can be prayed together. The three prayer times, pray this prayer. And a clarification has been given, a *sunnah* has been stated. Some people have made *Ẓuhr* separate and *'Aṣr* separate. When you pray *Maghrib* prayer, I will also pray *Maghrib* prayer. What about *'Aṣr*? I will pray *qaḍā'* (missed) prayer. May Allah protect us! They say, I will pray *qaḍā'* prayer. What happened, sir? It wasn't on time. I am performing the obligation. So when you are performing the *qaḍā'* prayer, it is also a compulsion. When you see the hadith, what is written in the hadith? It says that for the one who prays *qaḍā'*, there is destruction. God destroy the one who prays *qaḍā'* prayer. You are praying *qaḍā'* prayer, should you pray *qaḍā'* prayer? When a curse has been invoked for the one who prays *qaḍā'* prayer, what will happen to the one who does not pray? You can estimate that. You have the choice. Now, this is the situation. So, *farḍ* is *farḍ*. If you don't fulfill it here, you will have to fulfill it. One thing is that you are, for example, tied in a procession, in a relay, in a race. If you don't support your companion, if you don't run, what will happen to you? You will have to run, in any case, with force. And if you cannot run, then you will be dragged, they will drag you away. They will drag you away. So the matter is exactly like this, that without fulfilling these *farā'iḍ* (obligations), there is no choice. If you did not do it here with happiness, how much time does it take to do *wuḍū'*? And how much time does it take to pray? If you have spent your life with some laziness, then in the grave, your heights, which are so tall and wide, now there, a dead person cannot even get up, nor can they turn on their side. There is constriction, there is darkness, and there is no question of getting up from there. Now, there you will pray. Now when you pray, Allah will make you pray with more severity. Be certain of this. You will have to face more hardship than if you pray to Allah with happiness now, that would be much better. So that hardship will be much more, and because those who are our elders, who are our teachers, this trouble is also going to come upon them, because they often say, "Brother, for God's sake, pray *namāz*." So both are involved, one who guides and one who is guided. Both are there. For which you are urged to pray *namāz*. This is why there is so much emphasis. What was the last word? *Namāz*, *namāz*, *namāz*, *namāz*. And if there is no *namāz*, then there is nothing. If there is no *namāz*, he is not ours. If there is no *namāz*, he is not our friend. If there is no *namāz*, he is not our brother. If there is no *namāz*, then he is nothing. He has no relation. The one who leaves the five prayers, the Prophet says that he is a *kāfir* (disbeliever) and a Muslim has no connection with him. The one who leaves the five prayers. Now you will say that we, since becoming Bāwājī, how many prayers have gone? The prayers that have gone is another matter, but from the moment you have heard, you should be bound. You should become bound. You know, they call me Vijulā'ī. I am not worthy of being Vijulā'ī. But Vijulā'ī, those who were before you used to be like this and those who were after them used to be like this. But you were bound by it, and you will have to be bound by it. If you don't do it, then... One *farḍ* of Allah, and that too a *farḍ* that comes to you in 24 hours. If you had been given 50 prayers, what would you have done? If it had been said that these seven *farā'iḍ* all come at once, and Ramaḍān Sharīf also comes, and *zakāt* also has to be given at once, then look, you would join hands and say, "I am leaving." That's it. It would happen, wouldn't it? So Allah Ta'ālā has divided five things for you. He has given you ease. He has made you prosperous, and he wants you to fulfill just one *farḍ*, and you are negligent even in that. Anyway, Muslims think that we, by performing the *farā'iḍ*, by performing *ḥajj*, by praying *namāz*, by giving *zakāt*, have fulfilled the seven *farā'iḍ*. Hey sir, you are putting up lights at the butcher's shop, and this lamp is putting a very big filter on it, and I am sitting here watching that the strings of lights are being put up, and how beautiful it is, how big it is, and it is glittering, and people are... from here there is everything. And here you are putting up a small bulb from the butcher's, where there is no electricity, and here there is electricity. Which one will you appreciate? The one where there is light, you will appreciate that one. But where is the light? Because there is no *jān* (life/soul) in it. As someone said, a child was born, 10 pounds. You are very happy, there will be a party, 10 pounds child. The celebration is tomorrow, what happened? The child died. So the same is the case here, that everything is there, but the situation is that it is death. Everyone's life is death. What is the issue? That the foundation of *walāyah* is not there, which is the first obligation. There should be the love of 'Alī. There should be the desire for 'Alī. Now you are also involved in the love of 'Alī. Hey sir, in the same way that there is an expression of love, in the same way that there is an expression of love, love in that way. Your love for 'Alī means that you love 'Alī, you believe in 'Alī, so believe in 'Alī's words. Believe in 'Alī's actions. Follow him. Act in that way. That will be believing in 'Alī, that will be believing in the Prophet. Otherwise, you don't believe. So it became known that without *walāyah*, this is not the case for Muslims. That's why all their actions are useless. It becomes like scattered cotton, it becomes like scattered dust. It becomes like dust. All their deeds will be thrown in their faces, and they will be struck with them. So there is no result of action without *walāyah*. Now don't create sorrow in your heart that, O, the sorrow of the whole world is in our liver, what will happen to us Muslims, and they sit down and think. One time, a phone call came late, at 11 o'clock at night. I was worried, it was 11:15, 11:30. It was 11:15, 11:30 or 12:15. And I picked up the phone. I was worried, my wife was sleeping. Whose phone call is this? It was some reality that a sister was telling me, and she had phoned me, saying, "Please give me an answer." I was worried, what happened to you? "It's nothing." Because she lives alone, she lives far away, and she is poor. And the thing is, she doesn't have money, but she is poor. And she said... Now I was worried, what is the matter that at such a late hour... She said, "I am sitting here on a chair, and I am watching the river flowing. When will this river be cleaned?" This big river, when will it be cleaned? I said, "For God's sake, now you look at your own matters, for God's sake, leave the cleaning of the river. Now you, you look at this." So this is the situation. If we create sorrow in this way and sit down, it will be very difficult. That thing... The worry that one gets is about one's own affairs. What about others? So as I was telling you, this system, Allah Ta'ālā, this divine government, this divine system and arrangement, He has established it in such a way that for everyone, `li-kulli qawmin hād` (for every people a guide), a guide kept coming. No nation can claim that a prophet did not come to it. But what kept happening? That `wa takhadhu rusuluhu huwwā`. Oh, what a pity. I used to send prophets, the Qur'ān says. I used to send prophets, but you made a joke of them. You threw stones at them. You called them insane, you called them magicians. Alright, alright. Now get ready for the retribution. And my blow will be such that you will know. What will you do in taking revenge on someone? At most, if you take revenge, you will strike with a dagger, you will kill. That's it. Your revenge is this. Hey, the divine revenge starts from here. When you understand what divine revenge is, there is no sound in its blow. There is no sound in its stick. And its blow is severe. You will not even know, like a leaf you will fly away. What is your status, you are a worthless speck in the universe. What is your standing? But your situation is that you sit down to count your own standing, then you become equal to Allah. So I was saying that the divine system was established, and guides kept coming to us. And this chain remained established. In every era, in the time of Ādam, in the time of Ibrāhīm, in the time of Nūḥ, in the time of Ibrāhīm, in the time of the *A'immah*, all of them, whether it was Mūsā or 'Īsā, or our Prophet, peace be upon them, the chain of prophets continued in the universe, the chain of *A'immah* continued to be established. They kept coming, they kept giving guidance, which was their work of guidance, and they kept delivering guidance, and they kept doing their work and going. But those who had to take guidance, took it, those who did not have to take guidance, did not take it. They prepared the provisions for their grave. Those who did not, they will suffer in the grave forever, they will suffer torment. This is a permanent thing. This is a temporary thing. This life is for a few days, it will pass, and this, this intoxication will wear off. This face of ours, as you were seeing your face in the mirror, while looking, you are startled that your black hair is turning white. Then you see that there are wrinkles on my face. Then you see that the face has changed. And you are getting scared of your own face. You have not yet seen your real face. Your real face is to be seen at the time of the last gasp. What a face it will be. So in that face, may Allah protect our honor, and may Allah protect our dignity. May the Lord of the worlds give us salvation for the sake of His *A'immah*. This is salvation. Otherwise, what is this salvation that we have made provisions for? Anyway, I was saying that these *A'immah* kept doing their work. When they, just as we have day and night, in their religion too, there are nights and there are days, which are called *satr* (concealment) and *kashf* (manifestation). And in *satr* and *kashf*, what happens? Sometimes the *imām* is manifest, sometimes he is concealed. The time of concealment came. He went into concealment. Just as it is night now and it is also ending. So the time of concealment came, he went into concealment. And what did he do by hiding? It doesn't happen that Allah has hidden the sun, so now he has made you dark. No, he has given you the moon. Take its light. He has given you the stars, take their light. And if you need a lot, then light a lamp in your house, you will get light from that. In the same way, the system remained established for us. The *dā'ī* is present, your elders are present. So they keep this system going. And from there, Allah Ta'ālā, the *Imām* (peace be upon him), this is not our power. This is not some elder's doing. Whichever speck the sun shines upon, it starts shining. Otherwise, it has no capacity. It is a worthless speck. But when it shines, it shines. When it becomes, then its obedience becomes obligatory. And it gives guidance. And taking guidance is your job, giving guidance is its job. So this guidance, this chain is going on in its place. This era of the master of the universe came, when the pride of all existence, Aḥmad al-Muṣṭafā, Muḥammad al-Muṣṭafā (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came to his place, and this world was illuminated. And the ignorance of the Arabs became disbelieving, and after the darkness was removed, the light of dawn appeared. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) came. He spread Islam. He spread the religion. He taught everything, explained everything. But, just as you had to come at a certain time, as a human being, you were being presented. So you, as a human being, also had to become sick, you had to tie a stone to your stomach, you had to be hungry, you had to have a fever, you had to laugh, you had to cry. Exactly a human life had to be presented before us. Otherwise, we would not see him as a human, but we would see him as something else. So he had to be presented before us as a human, so that we too could shape our lives according to his example. So when the Prophet was about to pass away, whom did he appoint in his place? It is obvious that when you were about to depart from the world, you said that now in my place... people said, "O Messenger of Allah, we used to see you and fast, we used to see you and do *iftār*, we used to see you and do good deeds, we used to see you and do this and that." Now, what do they know? Pay attention to early Islam, in that era, they used to say, "We used to see you and do everything." He said, "Whatever you used to do by seeing me, now do it by seeing 'Alī." So he made a will, he established his successor. Whom did he do it to? Amīr al-Mu'minīn 'Alī. How did he establish him? What was the incident? This incident is a great incident that comes in the explanation of Ahd-e-Sharīf. And since this incident comes in the explanation of Ahd-e-Sharīf, I will briefly narrate it to you. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), when Masjid al-Qubā', a large mosque in Madīnah Munawwarah is Masjid al-Qubā'. This very mosque is mentioned in the Holy Qur'ān: `ussisa 'alat-taqwā` (founded on piety). The foundation of which was laid on piety, this is that mosque. This mosque is a very blessed mosque. There are many signs in it. And in the niche of that mosque, the Prophet was standing. The Sūrah *Idhā Jā'a* was revealed. Jibrīl Amīn descended, and you got the good news that your demise is about to happen, it is near, and with it, this good news was given that Makkah will be conquered, and after that, the time of your demise is near. Allah Ta'ālā wants to meet you. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) turned. He said to the people, "O people, the time is near that I should go. And now there is a need that before separating from you, I should explain some things to you." People started crying. They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what are you saying? Your separation is a great sorrow for us." He said, "It will happen, but what to do? We have to go, in any case. And Allah is our master. And before going, I want to fulfill the last obligation of *Ḥajj*, so that you can see once how the rituals of *Ḥajj* are performed. I will also perform it, you also see it and understand." When the obligation of *Ḥajj* was mentioned, people happily agreed. If he had said that I am going to tell you something else, then these Muslims, these weak-minded Muslims, those who had malice in their hearts, those whose minds were rusted, whose hearts were filled with filth, whose hearts were filled with hatred for 'Alī, they would never have agreed, nor would so many have gathered. A crowd of two hundred thousand gathered. It was the occasion of *Ḥajj*. And now these Bedouin Arabs were thinking that goats will be slaughtered, camels will be slaughtered, food will be available, and we are with the Prophet. What kind of fun it is, and what kind of things happen. The entire gathering of two hundred thousand was with him, and the honorable Prophet was going. He reached Makkah. There, you... Makkah had been conquered. After the conquest of Makkah, you purified Makkah. That is, the idols that were there, you had them thrown out. Through whom were they broken? They were broken through 'Alī. And after that, you performed *Ḥajj*. After performing the entire *Ḥajj*, because after a long time the Prophet got a chance to perform *Ḥajj*, because Makkah, Ka'batullah, was in the hands of the disbelievers, the idolaters, the Quraysh. When you conquered Makkah and performed its *Ḥajj*, after performing *Ḥajj*, now you said that I am returning. I am going from the station of Juḥfah towards Madīnah. There was a path in those days. People thought that the Prophet had come by one path and was going by another path. Just as it is said for the Friday prayer that one should come by one path and go by another. It is better. We will keep changing paths, will we build two or three paths to the mosque? It's not like that. Anyway, the Prophet returned by another path. People were thinking that the Prophet has taken this path. It was called the path of Juḥfah. And the station came, and on the station of Juḥfah, this verse was revealed, which I recited before you. `Yā ayyuhar-rasūlu balligh mā unzila ilayka` (O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you). Whatever has been revealed to you, convey it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) paused. For a moment, he waited. Jibrīl descended again. He said, `balligh`, O Messenger, `mā unzila ilayk`, `wa in-lam taf'al fa-mā ballaghta risālatah` (convey what has been revealed to you, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message). If you have not conveyed it, it is as if you have not conveyed the message. You have not done any work. See what a threat it is, how severe the verse is. What kind of tone it has, what kind of mood the verse is showing. When this verse was revealed, three times Jibrīl descended. Now the Prophet was helpless. And he looked towards the sky. Jibrīl descended and said, "O Messenger of Allah, why do you worry? Perhaps you... perhaps you are worried that they should not cause any harm to you, that people should not create any trouble over this announcement." `wallāhu ya'ṣimuka minan-nās` (and Allah will protect you from the people). Allah will protect you from the people. Their evil will not work at all. You announce. Don't worry, do whatever you want. Did the Messenger of Allah have any worry? No. The matter is that in praise of Amīr al-Mu'minīn, the Prophet wanted a promise to be revealed from Allah, so that people may see. Because when love is born, every aspect of the beloved is adorned. Everything is said, and sometimes it needs to be said with exaggeration. Here there was no exaggeration. But praise was necessary. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was praising him. And what did Allah Ta'ālā do? That `Allāhu ya'ṣimu...` Allah will protect you from the people, will protect you from their evil. The Prophet, at that very moment, what did he do? You had reached that place which is called Ghadīr Khumm. *Ghadīr* means a pond. It was a pond, a pit, there. You had reached there, the name of which was Khumm. You had reached the place of Khumm, and there you stopped. And after stopping, you said, "Those who are coming, stop them. And those who have gone ahead, call them back." Everyone was called back, everyone came. And after that, you said, "This desert, in this desert, there are many thorny trees. Remove these thorny trees." People immediately got ready. It was the command of the Prophet. Someone took a pickaxe, someone took a spade, and they removed all the thorns from there. Hey, the Prophet was not giving an outward command.
