In fact, the thorns that were in their hearts, the jealousy that was in their hearts, he was removing those. Anyway, the ground was cleared. And the desert was vast. And the thorns were not fitting even in the clothes. Now, what a celebration it was, that the sky, as long as it exists, and as long as it has existed, it was yearning for this celebration. That its eyes may see this celebration. This celebration. And this was the occasion of the celebration. It was the occasion of the greatest Eid, Eid-ul-Akbar. The Prophet said that I want to give a sermon before you. Immediately, the saddles of the camels, the saddles of the camels were brought and placed there. A pulpit was made from them. Otherwise, where would a pulpit come from? This was made into a pulpit. The Prophet came upon it. And after coming, he said, "Assalamu alaykum." You said salaam. After that, he said, "`Alastu awlā bikum min anfusikum?`" (Am I not more worthy of you than your own selves?). Are you... am I not greater than your own selves? "O people, am I not greater than you?" They said, "`Qālū balā yā Rasūlallāh`" (They said, "Yes, indeed, O Messenger of Allah!"). "Indeed, you are greater than us, O Messenger of Allah. And our parents be sacrificed for you." He said, "Did I not tell you about heaven and hell? Did I not warn you about hell and give you the desire for heaven? Did I not tell you about prayer, fasting, zakat, etc.? Did I not teach you everything? You were lying somewhere, from where I took you out. You were lying in misguidance, in ignorance. Look at your ignorance. In what evils you were lying. From all the evils, I took you out or not?" They all said, "O Messenger of Allah, indeed, our parents be sacrificed for you. You took us, we were like animals. We were animals." When he took this confession, when they said, "Yes, we were like animals. You made us human. You taught us everything." Then what did he do? He said, "Look, since you believe in me and acknowledge it in this way, that I am greater than you, I am greater than your own selves, then remember that now I am saying that I am your master. And being the master, I am saying that `Man kuntu mawlāhu, fa-hādhā 'Alīyyun mawlāhu` (Of whomsoever I am the master, this 'Alī is also his master). Of whomsoever I was the master, from today, 'Alī is his master." You, in that gathering, there would have been 30-50 'Alīs. It's a gathering of two hundred thousand. So 'Alī, what if the Prophet had just said this much and stopped? Then any Tom, Dick, or Harry would have been caught and made 'Alī, and the name 'Alī would have been given. Or whichever 'Alī it was, he would have been caught and brought, and a garland of flowers would have been put on him, and he would have been seated in the Prophet's place. This is what Muslims were like. This was the public's voice. You know how mob mentality is. So the Prophet did not do that. Rather, he took Haḍrat 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib, took him and raised him with both hands, raised him up and said, "This is 'Alī. `Man kuntu mawlāhu, fa-hādhā 'Alīyyun mawlāhu` (Of whomsoever I am the master, this 'Alī is also his master). Of whomsoever I was the master, from today, this 'Alī is his master. The entire nation is entrusted to him. And now obey him." He prayed, "`Allāhumma...` I... if 'Alī... befriend him who befriends 'Alī. And humiliate him who humiliates 'Alī. Love him who loves 'Alī." He said all this and says, and what a strange statement, and all these statements are present with the Muslims. After that, he says, "`Adir al-ḥaqqa ma'ahu ḥaythu dār`" (Make the truth revolve around him wherever he turns). O Allah, make it so, O Lord of the worlds... see, he is praying, the Prophet. That make it so that the truth follows 'Alī. 'Alī wherever he goes, the truth should go there. He did not say that 'Alī should follow the truth. Did you understand? That wherever 'Alī goes, the truth should be there. After saying this, you prayed two rak'ahs of prayer, and Amīr al-Mu'minīn also prayed. After that, he sat in the tent. First Abū Bakr came, then 'Umar came, then 'Uthmān came. They all came. "`Bakhin bakhin laka yabna Abī Ṭālib, asbaḥta mawlāya wa mawlā kulli mu'minin wa mu'minah`" (Congratulations, congratulations to you, O son of Abī Ṭālib! You have become my master and the master of every believing man and woman). They were saying that congratulations, congratulations, O son of Abū Ṭālib! You have become our master and the master of all. They kissed his hand, gave their allegiance, and all the companions came, Ṭalḥah came, Zubayr came, all these accursed ones came and after congratulating 'Alī, they left. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was smiling and watching. He was smiling and watching who was congratulating, what they were doing. After that, he said, "O people, the hypocrites among you, the two-faced ones, the two-hearted ones, who have hatred for 'Alī in their hearts and show love on the outside, if I want, I can identify each one of them. I can identify each one of them. It's not that I don't know. But I don't like to tell. But I am telling you, so remove this hatred. Cleanse your impurities and love 'Alī, be devoted to 'Alī. And if you are desirous of heaven, then love 'Alī. Follow 'Alī. And if not, you will go to hell." He said this, after that the matter ended. You returned. You came. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) became ill. After that, you had a deathly illness. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed away from the world. Haḍrat 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib's lap was where the Prophet's head was. And at that time, your last breath that you took, the Prophet, he wiped it. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) passed away. Haḍrat 'Alī was the guardian of the shrouding and burial. You gave the *ghusl*. And on the command of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him). And there, when all the Ahl al-Bayt were in an uproar, everyone was grief-stricken. The master of the universe had left the world. The mercy to the worlds had left the world. What would not happen? Could there be a greater sorrow than this? You tell me. There cannot be a greater sorrow in the world than the master of the universe leaving the world. It was not a small thing. But what was the situation? That here, the matter of shrouding and burial was going on. There, Abū Bakr and 'Umar, and the Muhājirūn and Anṣār, they all gathered together, and there, at Saqīfah Banī Sā'idah, a place, today that place, that cursed place exists. Where they went and sat, and started consulting, that now who will sit in the Prophet's place? Hey brother, what the Prophet was saying his whole life, did you not hear that? Did you not see that he appointed 'Alī? Did you forget the incident of Ghadīr Khumm? No, all that was gone from their minds. No, such a big task the Prophet has entrusted to us. Such a big property, such a big government, such a big task, after all, if we don't do it, who will? This task we have to do. There, the Muhājirūn started fighting. We are Muhājirūn. We are the ones who lived with the Prophet. We spent our lives in Makkah with the Prophet. There, the Anṣār started fighting. We gave refuge to the Prophet in Madīnah. We have the right. We should become the caliph. There, if I were to narrate this to you now, hours would pass. Such fights happened. Abū 'Ubaydah was a sensible person, he was wise. There, the leaders of the Anṣār's tribe stood up. There, the leaders of the Muhājirūn's tribe stood up. Anyway, whoever's influence was working, he was moving forward. Haḍrat 'Umar was working with a lot of force. And he saw this, that if I take the lead and take the upper hand, the matter will be spoiled. This is because perhaps these people will not listen to me. But it is better that right now, I make Abū Bakr the caliph. And make him the caliph, so that then he will make me the caliph. They made this kind of trickery. And they grabbed Abū Bakr's hand and kissed it, and said that from today, the caliph is Abū Bakr. There were long, drawn-out situations. Big, big speeches were made there. And after that, 'Umar did this trickery. And he said that my sword will cut and throw away whoever comes forward. I am kissing Abū Bakr's hand, he is the Caliph of the Messenger. Well, he became the Caliph of the Messenger. After that, what happened? That now, he had said in the ears of Abū Bakr, "I am making you, but take care of me. As you go, make me. It shouldn't be that you forget me. I am making you the caliph for this very reason, that you make me the caliph. If you don't make me, then just as I am scaring people with the sword, I can also break the caliphate into pieces." So Abū Bakr nodded his head and said, "'Umar, don't worry, *in shā' Allāh*." When there were gestures between them, he said, "Brother, just take care." That's it. Now all this has happened. After it happened, drums started beating. Just as in the old days, the announcers would beat drums and make announcements. "Look, so-and-so has happened, this has happened." It's an old era. Beating drums, they are speaking, the announcement is happening. And that announcement, Abū Bakr himself wrote the message. Why? Because his father was present. And to inform his father, he wrote that I have been chosen as the caliph and I have become the Caliph of the Messenger, *alḥamdulillāh*, and this and that is the matter. He sent that letter with someone. That Abū Quḥāfah was on his rooftop. He was very old. He was sitting on some high place. And the messenger came and gave the letter, saying, "Your son has given this." He said, "Brother, my eyesight is weak, I can't see. What is written, what is it?" He said, "Sir, please come closer and read it, because it is a very special letter. He told me to give it into the father's hand." The letter arrived, and Abū Quḥāfah took it and read that letter. And in the letter, it was written that I have become the Caliph of the Muslims. Sometimes he writes Caliph of Allah, sometimes... Now he is reading, he is not understanding what he is writing. Sometimes he writes Caliph of Allah, sometimes he writes Caliph of the Prophet, sometimes he writes Caliph of the Muslims. And in the end, the signature is exactly my son's. He asked, "What has happened?" And when he read it, he understood that he has sat in the place of the Prophet. My son has sat in the place of the Prophet. He asked the messenger, "What is the matter? Why did people make my son the one? After all, what did they see in him that they made my son the caliph? Was 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib not there? Did people not hear that `anā madīnatul-'ilmi wa 'Alīyyun bābuhā` (I am the city of knowledge and 'Alī is its gate)?" Who is saying this? Abū Quḥāfah is saying it. Abū Bakr's father. So he is saying, "What happened that my son was chosen?" The messenger said, "Sir, the real matter was that your son was the most senior. *Mā shā' Allāh*, he had a long beard, and he was the most senior, he was a companion of the Prophet, he was with him in the cave. He had so many great qualities." He said, "Hey brother, if it was because of seniority, because of being older, that he was made, then the father is me. Why was I not made?" I am his father, sitting here. Why was I not made? Anyway, there are many jokes, and there are many such stories. Anyway, it passed, it passed. And what befell the master of the universe, only Allah knows best. The pain you had was for your son. Just as I will tell you, two mothers came fighting to Haḍrat 'Alī. Two mothers came fighting. In this era, a mistake cannot happen in a hospital. Before, in maternity hospitals, a lot of mistakes... What was a hospital? The house itself was the maternity hospital. Now there, a mistake happened. They used to live, tribal people used to live, and Bedouin people, you know very well how they live. Because you have lived with them. Now, what happened was that by chance, at the same place, two children were born to two mothers. And what happened? That... one child passed away. Now the other mother saw that my child has passed away. What did she do? She snatched that child and said, "This dead child is yours, this child is mine." Now both were fighting that the living child is our child. Now both of them reached Haḍrat 'Alī. The Caliph of his time. They reached him and said, "O 'Alī, decide that this child is ours." She said that the child is ours. What did you say? You called Qambar, your servant. "Qambar, bring the sword." He brought the sword, Qambar. You said, "This child, from the middle, exactly, see, don't make a mistake. Exactly from the middle, cut it in half. Half a child to you, half a child to you." Now the real mother, she cried out, "O 'Alī, what a disaster you are doing! For God's sake, don't give it to me, but let it live." You did this. You said, "This mother is a liar, this mother is truthful. Give the child to her." So what was the matter? The pain for Islam was with 'Alī, because it was his child. This Islam was 'Alī's child, it was a thing of their house. 'Alī had the pain for Islam. What pain would anyone else have? When a messenger reached the Caesar of Rome and he did not get an answer, what of it? And when the Negus of Abyssinia did not get an answer, what of it? If you are being asked about some verse in the Qur'ān Sharīf, then it is being asked, "Is this verse in the Qur'ān Sharīf?" The Caliph is sitting. And you... see, pick up their books and read. There are not one, there are thousands of stories. Not one, there are hundreds of stories. Now, for whom will you mourn this? For the Muslims? Or for the Caliph-makers? Or for the Caliphs? Anyway, there is a lot. We have nothing to do with it. We don't have to humiliate anyone, nor do we have to do anything. Anyway, we look at ourselves. So the real mother, she had the pain for Islam. That's why what did she keep doing? She saw that there should be no bloodshed in my Islam, so she remained silent for 30 years. But when the Caliphate came to her door, and they said to 'Alī, "'Alī, now take the Caliphate." At that time, what was 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib doing? He was sitting and mending his shoes. He was mending his torn shoes. So people entered his house and said, "'Alī, now take charge. Haḍrat 'Uthmān has been martyred. The Caliphate is over. There is no one else. Who should we appoint besides you? Ṭalḥah and Zubayr, who were there, they have also gotten into some trouble. They are fighting with each other. It is better that you take the Caliphate. This is your right, and you..." You smiled and looked at them. First, he kept getting angry. When he saw that these people are not listening, they are doing this, he said, "O people, why are you making such a commotion at my door? My door is weak, my house is weak. If you make a commotion, my house will also fall. I live in a weak house, O people. And why are you making a commotion? And you see what work I am doing." They said, "O 'Alī, what work are you sitting and doing? You are sitting and doing the work of a cobbler. You are sewing shoes." So you said, "O people, what would be the price of my shoes?" They said, "O 'Alī, your shoes are so torn, torn from all sides, and you are trying to sew them, you are patching them. What value does it have? No value." You said, "O people, by God, the value of these shoes in my eyes is more than your Caliphate." Did you see? This was the sarcastic reply of 'Alī. This was a slap on the face of the nation, on their assembly, on their democracy, on their republicanism. That you... you count people, you don't weigh them. You don't weigh. You are those people who... 200 sheep... 200 goats, from these people, if you gather a little bit of their intellect, can the intellect of one human be formed? Can the intellect of one human be formed by gathering a little bit of the intellect of 200 sheep? Your system is exactly like that. You have chosen someone by joining heads. Your choosing is different, God's choosing is different. This is the divine system. How did you choose? If you confess that yes, we are leaving the system in our hands, then I will accept. You... you do not have the right to appoint. Hey, when God and the Prophet have appointed me, how... That's why when 'Alī went and took the Caliphate, and they confessed that yes, God and the Prophet have appointed you, we are not appointing you. Then you said, "Confess." When they confessed, you reached the mosque. And at that time, your condition was that you were wearing ordinary clothes, and when you came to the pulpit for the Caliphate, your condition was that you were getting up, you were sitting among the people. People were getting up. So people did what? They took you by one hand, another person took you by the other hand, and they sat you down. "Hey old man, where are you getting up?" They are saying to 'Alī. See, people had become so ignorant. They had even stopped recognizing 'Alī. Now they said, "Hey, O old man, where are you getting up? 'Alī is coming." "Hey, I have heard his name a lot. He is a great rider, he has innate knowledge. Hey, he is a great rider, he won the Battle of the Trench, and he won Tabūk, and he won Badr, he won Uhud. Hey, he was the Prophet's special man. Hey, he was a brother, he was a successor. Hey, just think, what are you doing? 'Alī is about to come. Sit down in your place." He said, "O people, the 'Alī for whom you are saying this, I am that very 'Alī. Leave me, O people. Let me go and sit on the pulpit." This was 'Alī. There was no grandeur of kingdoms, nor were there forts, nor were there curtains of gold and jewels. All things were thrown away. There was an ordinary cloak, a black turban, a stick in his hand. Amīr al-Mu'minīn was coming after 30 years, to that very pulpit of the Prophet. And you came and, stumbling, when you went and sat, you sat in the Prophet's place. The custom had become that when Haḍrat Abū Bakr came, you sat one step lower. And people said, "O Abū Bakr, why are you sitting lower?" He said, "To sit in the Prophet's place... this is a place of respect. Who can sit? Who will sit in the Prophet's place?" So he sat lower. The second gentleman came, when Haḍrat 'Umar became the Caliph, he left Abū Bakr's place, he took a step lower. 'Uthmān came, he left that step. Now they were descending one step at a time. Now, in the time of Hishām ibn 'Abd al-Malik, a discussion arose, that this commotion that happened, why did they descend these steps? When Haḍrat 'Alī came, what did you do? He went straight ahead, stumbling, and sat in the Prophet's place. People said, "Why did you not maintain the custom? You should have also taken a step lower." You gave a slap of a reply. "What a foolish thing you are saying! I am the one who will sit in the Prophet's place. The Prophet sat me here. I will sit in the same place." This is sitting in the right place. Now what happened? In the time of Hishām ibn 'Abd al-Malik, a discussion started, whether this was right or wrong. Hishām said, "Brother, whether it was right or wrong, leave that, but 'Alī did a great favor to us. If the Caliphs had kept descending one step at a time, it would have gone into a well. The pulpit would have become a well, and one step would have descended. It would have become a joke." So, anyway, this was the Caliphate of the Muslims. This was our Caliphate. 'Alī's. And it was the day of Ghadīr Khumm, and the appointment was for Amīr al-Mu'minīn. And you were the Caliph of the Prophet. But after becoming the Caliph, what work did you do? The same work of the Prophet, that `mā ātākumur-rasūlu fa-khudhūhu wa mā nahākum 'anhu fantahū` (what the Messenger gives you, take it, and what he forbids you, refrain from it). What the Prophet gives, take it. What the Prophet forbids, stop from it. This was also 'Alī's work. Amīr al-Mu'minīn, as soon as he came, he said, "Beware, when the time for prayer comes, it should not be that the prayer is not done." And "Beware, do not even look at such a thing." It is a wrong thing. One should not even look at a wrong thing. One should not eat it, one should not drink it. And the thing from which I am stopping you, stop. The thing from which I am not stopping you, don't stop. And what things did he stop from? You think that Islam has placed many restrictions. No. Only in plants, the plants that we have, in those plants, there is only one thing that you have been stopped from. And we are not even aware of that. We are so ignorant. We say we are Sulaymānī, Mu'minīn, etc., we take the name of hadith, but we don't know. In plants, there is one thing not to eat. You will say, "What's in plants?" What do you know, sir? What reality are you aware of? You are not even aware of your own reality. Tell me, the one you keep calling your own, your own, your own hand, your own head. Are you aware of any reality? Your... in your stomach, inside you, what treasure is running in your body, what is happening, can you tell now? No. When you put a machine on, you will know. How much is the pressure, you will know. Sir, with a machine... Sir, you look inside yourself, it is your world. Look into your world. So you are aware of something, how can you say? Anyway, in plants, one thing is forbidden by Allah, and that is mushroom. Mushroom is forbidden. It is haram. Its soup, etc. You will say it has so many varieties, etc. Those varieties are all hellish. This is hell. It should be avoided. Don't touch it with your hand. You will say, "We have drunk so much of it until now, so much..." All that is wrong. It is a wrong thing. Mushroom is haram. If you are a follower of 'Alī, don't touch it with your hand. Don't even look at it. If a new thing is created, what do you do? I ask you, there are seven colors, aren't there? You will say, "Yes, there are seven colors." If there was an eighth color, what would it be like, tell me. Hey, I am asking a simple question, tell me the eighth color. Hey sir, there isn't one, so what can I tell you? No, tell me. You have created a sixth sense. So here, bring an eighth color. Why don't you bring it, sir? You have created a sixth sense. Just give it a name. Sixth sense's name should also be... "No sir, it's just XYZ." Hey, what is this XYZ? Give it a name. Why don't you give it? You don't give it. So in the same way, you should understand that what is haram is haram. In plants, it is this one thing. And in animals, the pig. *Na'ūdhubillāh, na'ūdhubillāh*. That animal that feeds only on filth. You just look at it, look at its face, look at its mouth. Look at its form. *Na'ūdhubillāh*. The pig is a pig. And some people say, "What difference does it make? It's just meat. You can eat anything." The one who eats filth, you eat him? And if you are so fond of eating, then eat a dog too, eat a kite too. Eat a cheetah, eat a tiger too. Eat everything. "No sir, we don't eat cheetahs." "Hey, if you don't eat cheetahs, you start. Start eating cheetahs too." You can eat humans too. Become cannibals. Why don't you eat? No, your nature does not accept it. So you will have to leave it. You will have to leave this. And in animals, what is the other thing? And the things for which the desire has been created, I am counting those things. Crab is haram. You will say, "What about crab?" It's a very tasty soup. Chinese soup. In Chinese restaurants, it's the best thing. Crab. The crab has now become fashionable. They catch it from the middle of the river and eat it roasted there. This is all haram. You will see that all animals will walk, they will walk on their mouths. Every animal will walk, every human will walk, they will walk on their mouths. You walk upside down. You are saying strange things. You walk upside down. But this animal... Shrimp is haram. Crab is haram. Lobster is haram. These are all wrong things. Shrimp is permissible. The fish that has scales, that fish is halal. There isn't much. These are just a few things that are haram. But the desire for haram is greater. This was about eating and drinking. And if I wanted, I would narrate some other things to you, that if you see the condition of this animal, the pig, you will see a world of difference between a rooster and it. Hey, what's the difference? This also has meat, that also has meat. This is also an animal. What's the difference? What's the difference between this and a goat? Hey, you will see that this rooster, when it is with its female, if another rooster comes there, it will peck it with its beak. It will not let it come near the female. This is the halal gaze. Protecting one's female. This is a matter of nobility. And what happens there? That this animal is such an animal that it will hit its female, "You go to others." Did you see? This is vileness, vileness. This is the result of eating filth. So God has placed a magnet. A bad thing attracts a bad thing. And you don't touch that bad thing. And the magnets that are there, you will say, "How are these English people, how are their minds?" "German-made mind." "How have they... in science... what have they done?" "Life has been made a little easy, besides that, what have they done?" "Have they made our death easy? Have they made the stages after death easy?" "In life, they have shown some new things. So you have made them gods?" "It is because of eating this pig that they have progressed." And because of drinking some things, they have progressed. Allah had forbidden only one thing. That "Look, this is wine, this is a fiery thing. This is haram. Drinking it is haram, seeing it is haram, its agency is haram, selling it is haram, seeing it being drunk is haram, its business is haram, carrying it is haram, seeing it is haram, keeping it in the house is haram. Everything is haram." Now you will say that since you have reached Kuwait, Dubai, and have mixed with Arabs, you must have come to know something. And because of mixing with Arabs, you have a greater connection with Arabs. As for knowledge, first of all, they don't have scholars. The scholars are few and far between. If you have met any of their scholars, and if he has explained to you, that "Look, where is it written in the Qur'ān Sharīf? Where is the word haram?" Look, `hurrimat 'alaykumul-maytatu wad-damu wa laḥmul-khinzīr` (Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine). It has come in the Qur'ān. Allah Ta'ālā says, "Haram is upon you." Listen carefully, brothers. `hurrimat 'alaykumul-maytatu wad-damu wa laḥmul-khinzīr`. The first thing he is mentioning is that dead animals are haram for you. After that is blood is haram for you. After that, the flesh of the pig is haram for you. He is mentioning three things. Dead animals, you know. Whatever dead things are, you don't eat them. Blood, just as in Germany or other places in Europe, they collect the blood of horses, etc., solidify it, and make things like falooda and eat it. It is haram for you. You don't have to eat blood. There is another thing, but this is not it. This thing is not haram. And after that, what is he saying? `laḥmul-khinzīr`, the flesh of the pig. These three things are haram. After that, Allah Ta'ālā says that, "O Prophet, in drinking things, there is a need to be careful." `yas'alūnaka 'anil-khamri wal-maysir... fīhi ithmun kabīr wa manāfi'u lin-nās wa ithmuhumā akbaru min naf'ihimā` (They ask you about wine and gambling... in them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit). The Qur'ān Sharīf says, and it is a verse to remember. Allah Ta'ālā says, "O Prophet, they ask you about what? About `al-khamr`," that is, *khamr* means an intoxicating thing, wine. They ask you about this. And `wal-maysir`, gambling. They ask you about gambling. These two things, O Prophet, they ask you about. So you tell them that in this, there is a lot of sin. But in this, there is also benefit for people. `fīhi manāfi'u lin-nās`, the Qur'ān is saying. That in this, there are benefits, benefits for people. Just for a moment. After that, he says, `wa ithmuhumā akbaru min naf'ihimā`, "But its sin is greater than its benefit. Beware, don't touch it with your hand. The benefit that it has, leave it. But its sin is severe. Its sin is greater." Now what did he say? You will say that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade it in such a way, and what did he do? The matter is that what happens is that the thing from which one is stopped, the desire for it is greater. The desire for that thing is greater. And the Messenger of Allah, how did he stop it? That here, the question is that there are only three verses in the Qur'ān Sharīf about wine. And there, the word haram has not come anywhere. From this, who has taken advantage? The Muslims. And you know how these Bedouins drink wine. And they take advantage of this and drink. Although it is strictly haram. Now you will say that why did the word haram not come? I am explaining that. Listen carefully and remember. That Allah Ta'ālā says in another place that in this, this wine, this is a satanic act. `'amalush-shayṭān`. In a third place, he says that Satan creates enmity and quarrels among you through wine. There are three verses in the Qur'ān Sharīf. So he said, "Avoid it." "Stay away from it, abstain from it." See, what happens is... The one who is considered haram, I am proving him, and I am telling you, that according to the statements of the *A'immah*, according to the statements of the Prophet, countless statements are present in which wine has been declared `ummul-khabā'ith` (the mother of all evils). If there is a root of evil, it is this wine. But because it is not in the Qur'ān Sharīf, they are taking advantage of it. To explain that, I am telling you why this happened. Why did the word haram not come? See, before this, I had explained slavery to you. That slavery in Islam... its sin is greater. Now what did he say? You will say that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) forbade it in such a way, and what did he do? The matter is that what happens is that the thing from which one is stopped, the desire for it is greater. The desire for that thing is greater. And the Messenger of Allah, how did he stop it? That here, the question is that there are only three verses in the Qur'ān Sharīf about wine. And there, the word haram has not come anywhere. From this, who has taken advantage? The Muslims. And you know how these Bedouins drink wine. And they take advantage of this and drink. Although it is strictly haram. Now you will say that why did the word haram not come? I am explaining that. Listen carefully and remember. That Allah Ta'ālā says in another place that in this, this wine, this is a satanic act. `amalush-shayṭān`. In a third place, he says that Satan creates enmity and quarrels among you through wine. There are three verses in the Qur'ān Sharīf. So he said, "Avoid it." "Stay away from it, abstain from it." See, what happens is... The one who is considered haram, I am proving him, and I am telling you, that according to the statements of the *A'immah*, according to the statements of the Prophet, countless statements are present in which wine has been declared `ummul-khabā'ith` (the mother of all evils). If there is a root of evil, it is this wine. But because it is not in the Qur'ān Sharīf, they are taking advantage of it. To explain that, I am telling you why this happened. Why did the word haram not come? See, before this, I had explained slavery to you. That there is no slavery in Islam. This religion of freedom has come to us to eradicate slavery. Slavery has come to us to eradicate it. You will say, "Then how did the rules and laws of slavery come?" Hey, it came in such a way that you build a dam, and you stop the water. When you stop the water, it is obvious that when you stop the water, you should not bring a single drop of water here. Stop all the water. You will say, "How will I stop it like this, brother?" When I build a dam, some water will remain, and then it will dry up. So what happened later was that the water remains and then dries up. In the same way, the rules of slavery came. In the same way, these Arabs who were addicted to wine, the Bedouins who lived in the desert, where there was no water, who were in great difficulty, they did not get water for miles, so they used to drink this wine. It was in their blood. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), Allah Ta'ālā, used this wisdom, that if he had declared it haram at once, they would have been very shocked. They would have had a great problem. That's why He... He induced a desire in them for it, and the verses for wine came gradually, so that they could be stopped and explained. And look at it from a psychological point of view. From a psychological point of view, it happens that you go to a doctor. You go to the doctor. And why do you go to the doctor? When you are sick, you go. You don't just go to the doctor like that. Unless he is a friend, then you go, that's a different matter. If he is a relative, you go. Otherwise, when you are sick, you will go. When you go to the doctor sick, what do you say to the doctor? "Sir, I have this problem, this illness. Please treat me." And that doctor will check your pulse, etc. After seeing everything, he will say, "You have this illness, etc." But what will the doctor say? It is obvious that a doctor is wise, and he is a physician. So obviously, first of all, he will tell you prevention. And you know that this saying is famous in the world, and we are bound by it: Prevention is better than cure. Prevention is better than cure. So, prevention first, treatment later. No, you will not see such a doctor who tells you the treatment first and the prevention later. No. First, he will tell you the prevention, and that too with emphasis. Then he will say, "Take these pills, drink this syrup, or take this injection." So the doctor will treat you in this way. And how will he treat you? That first of all, he will make you sit and he will read out a list to you, that you will have to abstain from these things. Now you are sitting in the doctor's office. Just imagine the scene. The doctor is also here, and the patient is also ready. Now the patient went, and both of them said to the doctor, "Doctor, this is the disease, and please treat it." And the doctor saw it. After seeing it, he said, "Look brother, you have a lot of cold, you have bronchitis, and you will have to abstain from such and such things." Now he started listing the names before you. He started listing so-and-so name, so-and-so thing, so-and-so thing. "Brother, don't eat this vegetable, don't eat brinjal, don't eat potatoes, don't eat pumpkin, don't eat this thing." You don't even like those things. You kept listening quietly. He kept reading out the list. And you kept listening. And while listening, when he named such a thing which you are very fond of, and you drink and eat a lot of it, then you said, "Doctor, this too?" Why? Until now you were not startled. Why did you jump from your chair? You immediately jumped from your chair and said, "Doctor, this too?" And the doctor was also surprised, "O God, this man will kill me, what will he do? Now should I tell him or not? And in reality, it is poison for him. But now how to explain it to him?" So he also used great wisdom. First, he read out the list which you did not like. Whatever strange things he read out, you said, "I don't eat those things anyway." You said, "I have left everything." The doctor said, "That's good." "No problem." He said, "No problem." And the doctor kept listing things, and you showed no reaction. "No problem, no problem," you kept saying. As soon as he named that thing, the color of your face changed. "Hey doctor, this too?" The doctor said, "Hey, not wine!" The physician of the nation, our doctor, the doctor of doctors, the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), when he named this thing, you were startled. "Hey, wine! Hey, hey, wine! Now that too is not allowed? Hey, first there is no water in the desert. And now we used to live by drinking this. Now wine is also not allowed?" Now, if you think, that doctor is wise, so he will try to explain it to you gently. "Hey, wine... for God's sake, son. Look, it's not good for you." He will explain it with such coolness. If he had said, "It is poison for your nose. You will die." Then... you would have left that doctor and gone to another doctor. "This doctor, shoot him." You would have gone to another doctor. So it became known that the matter becomes difficult. This is the psychology of a human. That where you forbid, there you have a desire. And the things whose list he gives, there you are startled, because you have a desire for it. So this physician, our physician of the era, and the physician of the nation, the leader of the mystics, the leader of the prophets, he, how did he work with wisdom? He, through the Qur'ān, Allah and the Prophet were united. They were not separate. Whatever the Prophet said, Allah said, whatever Allah said, the Prophet said. `wa mā yanṭiqu 'anil-hawā` (Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination). So the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) conveyed the command of Allah in such a way that he did not use the word haram. If he had used the word haram, the heart of this Arab would have broken. "Oh, haram!" Like that... So he explained it with coolness. "Look brother, in this, it is a satanic act. It is this thing." So there, he gave them a warning by revealing different verses, he scared them first. And the other things he mentioned, "You can eat this, you can do this," he made them happy. And then he brought one thing and said, "Leave this, brother. Just leave this." But what advantage did they take from it? "Look, the word haram is not there, so come on, drink." So this subtlety, do you know who did it? The second Caliph. The second Caliph, he was the first to make it permissible. He said, "The light wine, which has a little intoxication, like beer, what's the harm in drinking that?" Come on, drink. When he drank, the third Caliph was very pious. He said, "The Caliph Awwal and the Caliph Thānī are drinking, what's the harm in drinking a little?" He also drank. So this custom started from there. So, anyway, when he was forbidden, he had to stop. And for this reason, this is the prohibition. So don't fall into the illusion that the word haram has not come. This is wrong. One should not fall into illusion. So, anyway, one has to stop from these five things. And in intoxicants, these are the things. And other intoxicating things, you will say, "What about... tobacco..." Oh, tobacco, today they are saying cancer, cancer. Hey sir, they are saying cancer. Our Prophet, 1400 years ago, had said that this is a cancer for your soul. Now why are you concerned about the cancer of the body? This is a cancer for your soul. If you smoke a pipe, you will be destroyed. If you smoke a cigarette, your heart will burn. And if you do anything, you will be ruined. What was said was said, it is a line on a stone. No, sir. "We... we are permitted to smoke a cigarette. And for that, we have this... and our fast is accepted from this." "The next day, you can fast." You should ask. "What is the connection between fasting and a cigarette?" "But if you smoke a cigarette, you can fast." What could be more foolish than this? And "My mind starts working. My mind starts working, this factory, from what?"
