They became counted among the `Kallamam`. This `Kallamam` is a very great entity, and its gnosis (`ma'rifat`) is very difficult to explain. What I want to say is that Allah Ta'ala... in the workshop of power, in the workshop of pre-eternity, He gave to each what seemed appropriate to Him. So, this was the divine plan (`taqdīr-e-ilāhī`), to place everyone in their station. To place them in that very place. This was what justice (`'adl`) demanded, and this was what equity (`inṣāf`) demanded. And just as the Lord of the Worlds was just, in the same way, you have seen that all were organized, and all were established in succession, and everyone's ranks were fixed in their places. One after the other, they were established in succession, and being established, where did the matter reach? It reached the `Kallamam`. And these `Kallamam` were those, as I said, who said "yes" after saying "no." Or they had accepted after refusing. And that small... and what is that mistake called? It is called a small mistake (`zarā sī bhūl`). If your clothes are white, completely white, completely, so if a little black comes on it, a tiny speck, yet what will happen? It will be very visible. It will be very visible. Why? Because you are completely white. If your clothes were multi-colored, or dirty, then nothing would be visible on it. But if the whole thing is completely white and fair, then there, a little blackness is very visible. So, in the very same way, these who were, were pure and clean entities. A small blemish came upon them. A small thing came. So, that small thing, its ratio, that proportion, you should see from this perspective, that they were completely pure and clean. Meaning, whether secondary perfection (`kamāl-e-thāni`) had been achieved or not, that I will say now. But what I am saying is, they are `qudsāni` (holy), `Raḥmāni` (of the Merciful), `ilm`, `qudrah`, and `ḥayāt` (knowledge, power, and life) are with them in their primary state. And they are endowed with all attributes. And they are living in that spiritual realm. They are those beings. Although they have heard some different calls, they have, through their actions, shown at the last moment... that is why they say, `inna-l-a'mālu bi-l-khawātīmihā` (Indeed, actions are judged by their endings). That every action's outcome is what matters. The ending will be seen. That is why they say, "May Allah Ta'ala grant a good ending." What does it mean, a good ending? Meaning, it will be seen whether at the time of your death, at the time of your departure from the world, on what religion you were. Did your ending happen with good or not? Did your ending happen on the divine religion, on Islam, on faith, or not? So, this was the main thing. This was the last thing. So, in the very same way, these all were sanctified beings, blessed beings, luminous beings, holy people. But a small spot came on them, and that spot was a very strange spot, that they said "yes" after saying "no." So the Lord of the Worlds, what did He do? He counted them in such a way that now two things happened for them. And what were those two things? That now, `qudrat` (divine power) wants... `qudrat` meaning? The last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`. Now, `qudrat` means the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`. He also wants to punish them, and he also wants not to punish them. Now both things should happen. Now, how can both things happen in one being? And that he should get punishment and not get punishment. How can that be? So, you see that just as there is a small thing, for example, there is a page and a pencil mark is made on it, you can erase it with an eraser. It is erased and becomes clean. In the very same way, it had to be erased. This was its punishment, that it had to endure so much there. So, `qudrat` put them in a dual trial, how to give them punishment and not give them punishment. And the desire of `'Āshir` is this, and the desire of the First Intellect and the Second Intellect and all the intellects is also this, that they should be punished and not punished. It's a very difficult stage. For `qudrat`, a very difficult stage had come. And at this stage, he, who is the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`, he began to look with longing at his heavens above. His higher ones, who were, those `qudsāni` and `nurani` and principles, towards all of them he began to plead, that "It is better that you suggest. I don't understand what to do with them now." "What to do with them, and what... should I give them punishment or not, and how should I give it, and if I give it, then how?" Now you'll say, "Sir, did he not understand?" The thing is that when a major issue comes up, you don't use your own pen. Rather, your wisdom is in taking advice. That is why the Prophet was commanded, `wa shāwirhum fi-l-amr` (and consult them in the matter). What did he do? He started entrusting it to the ones above. Now the chain went up. It reached the First Intellect. And all of them, he sought their help. `Iyyāka na'budu wa iyyāka nasta'īn` (It is You we worship and You we ask for help). We worship only Him, and we seek help only from Him. This is it. This is the true meaning of `iyyāka nasta'īn`, that seeking help is this. You, in this world, the matter of help and worship is there, but the word for help (`istiyānat`) began from here. So, help was sought from him. And the matter of help went up through all the circles, that "They need help. They need to be guided. They need to be done. They need to be told what they should do now, how they should do it, and how they should be judged." This was a great stage that had come. For whom? For the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`. Now, this last individual, who is made `'Āshir`, he saw that all these souls, for them, what should happen? When all of them, with their insights, with their analyses and syntheses, and dialogues, saw, and with all their spiritual insights, they cast them. On whom? On `'Āshir`, who is the last individual of `Labbu-Nidā`. So, it was suggested to him. This perfection reached him, it was suggested that it should be done in such a way that neither should they be kept with the bad people, nor joined with the good. Rather, they should be given a middle form. That is why the Prophet said, `khayru-l-umūri awsaṭuhā` (The best of affairs is the middle way). `khayru-l-umūri awsaṭuhā`, that the best of affairs is the middle way. You understand? So, at what stage has he said this? We see moderation as good in everything, but at what extreme has this been said, the Messenger of God is saying. Now, you can enjoy this `ḥadīth`. So, this, placing them in the middle, was the command. It was suggested, it was advised. And the work that had to be done, who had to do it? The last individual of `Labbu-Nidā` and `'Āshir` had to do it. `'Āshir`, what did he do to them? He said, "Brother, you, although you have said 'yes' after saying 'no', and accepted after refusing, yet, you cannot be punished with everyone. You cannot be put into the three dimensions. And nor can you be placed in this spiritual world. You cannot become intellects, nor can it happen here that you are put into this progeny, into this physical world. And you are hanged in this gallows. Neither can you be in this place, nor in that place. Rather, we will place you in the middle." And what was that middle form? It was that of the Prophets (`anbiyā`), and `awliyā`, and `a'immah`, and `aṣfiyā`, `atqiyā`, `khulafā`, `aṣḥāb`, `abdāl`, `awtād`, `shuhadā` (saints, imams, the pure, the pious, caliphs, companions, substitutes, pegs, martyrs). All our guides. All our `du'āt` (summoners), `alayhimuṣ-ṣalātu was-salām`, and all our perfect guides who have passed, one hundred and twenty-four thousand. All of them. This number, one hundred and twenty-four thousand, that is coming along, do not go by this number. You will say, "Sir, their number must also have been one hundred and twenty-four thousand." No. This one hundred and twenty-four thousand is a number that the Prophet mentioned in one place, but that one hundred and twenty-four thousand, when its exegesis comes, I will tell you where one hundred and twenty-four thousand is established. But for now, just understand that they are countless, innumerable. And all of them are, and all of them have been stopped in the middle. They have been stopped. Neither are they fit to go to that world, nor to this spiritual world. They have been stopped in the middle. And the place where they have been stopped... now you'll say, "Sir, was there a place there?" Neither was there a place, nor was there time, nor was there space. I have already told you that space is where there is support. Time is what is called where there is the motion of the sun and moon. And where there is neither ahead nor behind, neither first nor last. That is the state. So, all those people, in the state in which they were stopped, that is called `Tāmūr`. Got it? `Tāmūr`. That is called `Tāmūr`, that is called `markaz` (center), that is called `Ka'ba-e-rūḥānī` (the spiritual Kaaba), that is called `markaz`. That is called the celestial sphere... the gate of the world of holiness. And that is also called the workshop of spirituality (`kārkhāna-e-rūḥānī`). The entire workshop of spirituality was established. The real Kaaba was made. It became the center of everything. Everything was made, so what was made? This. `Tāmūr`. The `Tāmūr` was made. Now, this is... so this is called the Active Field. Now, these who came to this Active Field were all the Imams, they are the Prophets, they are the `awliyā`, `aṣkiyā`, `atqiyā`, all the beings are, the `du'āt` are, everyone is. Now, do not connect from here to there yet. As I will later explain in `bāzūn`, how to connect them. Because in connecting, there will be a mistake. So, but anyway.

<!-- AUG:hazrat-zia lecture 6 -->

This group that is *Kal-lamam*... who in reality is that group of *Kal-lamam*? That very group is our *Anbiya* (*'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*), our *Awliya*, our *A'imma*, our *Du'at*. They are our *Asqiya*, our *Asfiya*, our *Sayya*, our *'ubbad*, our *Zuhhad*. These are all the things. Right now you do not have the spiritual understanding of this. You only understand that there is a *Nabi* and there is a *Rasul*. The matter stops at the level of *Nabi* and *Rasul*. If it goes a little further, then the spiritual understanding goes up to the level of *Imam*. So, other than the three terminologies of *Imam*, *Nabi*, and *Rasul*, we do not take a third term. Come, I will now count out some ranks (*darajat*) for you. When a *Momin* traverses the ranks and progresses, it is so that you may know how many heavens are stacked one upon another. When we first take the *'ahd-e-sharif* (sacred covenant), at that time, at the moment of taking the *'ahd-e-sharif*, the condition of our *nafs* (soul) is such that... the *Du'at* describe that condition by saying that we are *Mustajib* (responders), those who accept the *da'wat* (call). So, it is the state of a *Mustajib*. From *Mustajib* we become *Momin* (believer). From *Momin* we become what is called a *Mukasir*. From *Mukasir* we become *Ma'dhun*. From *Ma'dhun* we become *Da'i al-Mahsur*. From *Da'i al-Mahsur* we become *Da'i al-Mutlaq*. From *Da'i al-Mutlaq* we become *Da'i al-Balagh*. From *Da'i al-Balagh* we become *Hujjat*. From *Hujjat* we become *Bab*. And from *Bab* we become *Imam*.

So you have seen these ranks. But count them for a moment. The *Mustajib* is one. It is a single rank, just one. And after that, as soon as he steps into the rank of *Momin*, when he enters the circle of *iman*, he has to traverse ten ranks there. To say it, everyone is a *Momin*, no doubt. But someone is in the first rank, someone in the second, someone in the third, someone in the fourth, someone in the fifth, and someone in the tenth. And if someone completes their tenth rank, then just as in a college or school, after succeeding, you are not made to sit in the old class—that is a matter of humiliation—you are made to sit in a higher class. So, *Qudrat* (Divine Power) will arrange it such that as soon as your soul is elevated, you are given the rank that is above. So you will step into *Mukasarat*.

You reach the rank of *Mukasarat*. You... the apparent way we are given opportunities and so on, do not go into those things. My point is this: you should examine and see this from an academic (*'ilmi*) perspective. You reach *Mukasarat*; there are ten ranks there. When you traverse those ten ranks, you reach the rank of *Ma'dhun*. When you traverse the ten ranks of *Ma'dhun*, you reach the rank of *Da'i al-Mahsur*. Now, it is a different matter of spiritual knowledge what a *Da'i al-Mahsur* is, what a *Da'i al-Mutlaq* is, what a *Da'i al-Balagh* is. This is a separate discussion. I will digress from the topic, so I am leaving it for now. Now, after *Da'i al-Mutlaq* there is *Da'i al-Balagh*, after *Da'i al-Balagh* there is *Hujjat*, after *Hujjat*... all of them have ten ranks each.

So, just as this is, in the same way, you have to understand the ranks of the *'Aalam-e-Ruhani* (Spiritual Realm). The very first and lowest rank is that of *Nubuwwat* (Prophethood). A *Nabi* (Prophet) is at the most ordinary rank. The most insignificant, the lowest rank, the first rank, at the threshold, right at the entrance—that rank is called *Nubuwwat*. And when a *Nabi* completes that task, when he accomplishes the task of *Nubuwwat* and resolves its many responsibilities, then from *Nubuwwat* he comes to *Risalat* (Messengership). He becomes a *Rasul*. He will not be called *Ya ayyuha'l-Nabi*, he will be called *Ya ayyuha'l-Rasul*. And above *Risalat* comes... the rank of *Imamat*. And upon *Imamat* comes... tell me... the rank of *Wasayat*. Upon *Wasayat* comes the rank of *Nutq-e-Ilahi*. And *Nutq-e-Ilahi* has three degrees: *Jaddiyyat*, *Fathiyyat*, and *Khiyaliyyat*. After traversing these degrees, the rank that comes is that of *Hujjiyyat* or *Imamat-e-Ruhaniyya*. Upon *Imamat-e-Ruhaniyya* comes *Nutq-e-Ilahi*. In *Nutq-e-Ilahi* come three degrees... *Jadd*, *Fath*, and *Khiyal*. Upon that comes *Hujjiyyat*. Upon *Hujjiyyat* comes *Hijabiyyat*. Upon *Hijabiyyat* comes *Anzariyyat*. Upon *Anzariyyat* comes *Ahadiyyat*. Upon *Ahadiyyat* comes *Samadiyyat*.

Are you understanding the ranks? These are the ranks. And the one who is called a *Nabi* is at the very initial rank. Now, for now, do not trouble yourselves. Do not start judging our Prophet (*'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*) and others. If I have given you a scale, do not start measuring immediately, please. Just understand that these are the ranks. This many ranks have to be traversed. So now, who has traversed how many ranks and what, I will explain this to you later. For now, what you have to understand is that these are the steps of the *'Aalam-e-Ruhani*, and these are its ranks. And *Nubuwwat* is the initial rank. Now, you see that there, all those who were of the *Kal-lamam*... they were of the *Kal-lamam*, those who had said "yes" after saying "no," who had affirmed after denying—all of those people, all those lofty souls (*nufus-e-'aliya*), those personalities of saintly attributes (*qudsi-sifat*), what did they do? They did say "yes" after saying "no," but... in changing their "no" to a "yes"... in turning their "no" into a "yes," they took on two relations (*nisbat*s).

Now you will say, what kind of relations? The very same relations that the *'aql-e-awwal* (First Intellect) had left behind. Because such relations were created with the *'aql-e-awwal*... just as... what happens? When you live here in the city, you get very big, wide roads. But if you go to a village for a moment and see in the village how there are footpaths (*pagdandi*s). Why are they called footpaths? It is because near the fields there are very small paths, paths for just one person to walk on. So you walk on that footpath. How is that footpath formed? That footpath is formed... the poor farmer, to plow his field and to bring his bullocks and so on, when he walks on a path, then on his... his... footsteps, and on his very footprints, people walk, and a path begins to form. And a footpath is made. So, in exactly the same way, a mark was left by the *'aql-e-awwal* of two relations, which are called *nisbat-e-adna* (the lower relation) and *nisbat-e-'ala* (the higher relation). I had told you that the two intellects that arose after seeing this *'aql-e-awwal*, the vision of both of them was more or less different. One's vision was... was on the exoteric, one's was on the esoteric. One's was on the effect, one's was on the cause. One was looking at the inner character, another was looking at the outer form. These conditions that existed, these two separate conditions, why were they created? It was because the *'aql-e-awwal* had performed its profession of the monotheism of the Lord of the Worlds with two relations. I had told you that one relation was *ila dhatihi* (towards its own self), meaning it was towards its own self, that it looked at itself and then it looked at all those of its own kind, and thought, "Did I create them, or did they create me?" It said, "No." But then it said that "It must be that there is a creator of all of us." This relation was the higher relation, and its own relation was the lower relation. So these two relations that the *'aql-e-awwal* had left, that very track was of use. Here, those relations were running, and from this very relation all the intellects (*'uqul*) were becoming more or less similar. And these very relations, descending lower and lower, upon reaching the *Kal-lamam*, became even more divided. And how were they divided? The *Kal-lamam*'s group, which is an innumerable group, that group, what did it do? Some people, some souls, accepted that relation which was more noble (*ashraf*). Some souls accepted that relation which was lower (*adwan*).

Now, the question remains, who were those who accepted the *ashraf* relation? And who were those who accepted the *adwan* relation? Those who accepted the *adwan* relation became the *Du'at* and the *Anbiya*. All the *Anbiya* and all the *Du'at*, all of them accepted the *adwan* relation. I mentioned the *Anbiya* in this regard because we are very familiar (*ma'nus*) with them. A human being is most familiar with their mother. But the superiority of the father has been stated by Allah Ta'ala everywhere. In the Quran, there is the superiority of the father. So, the point to be made was that these... who are the *anbiya-e-kiram* (noble prophets), all of them are in the *nisbat-e-adna* (lower relation). They are in the *nisbat-e-adna*. And who became part of the *nisbat-e-'ala* (higher relation)? The Imams became part of it. Whom the *duniya-e-islam* (world of Islam) does not know at all. Well, it neither knows the *'Aalam-e-Ruhani*, nor does it know any of these things. In fact, it does not even know these terminologies, what the difference is between an Imam and *Nubuwwat* and what these things are. For them... for them, even someone who has written four books can be an Imam. This terminology of Imam has become so common that everyone becomes an Imam. But becoming an Imam is not easy. An Imam is a *Hadi* (guide) and a *Rahbar* (leader), but what kind? He is one who possesses the *nisbat-e-'ala*. Where did the *nisbat-e-'ala* begin? From *Imamat*, from *Wasayat*—all these are of the *nisbat-e-'ala*. And where is the *nisbat-e-adna* from? From the *Du'at*, from *Nubuwwat*, from *Risalat*, from all... from the *Wasayat* here—all these relations are *adna*.

Now, when those souls were divided between *nisbat-e-'ala* and *nisbat-e-adna*, then their station (*qiyam*) and their residence also became... since we are helpless servants (*'ajiz*) and we discuss in terms of physical realities (*jismaniyyat*), and without that, we do not understand, for this reason, the explainers have explained it this way. Although there are no places there, there is no station, no one is ahead or behind. But the explainers have told us in such a way that if they are of the *nisbat-e-'ala*, the *A'imma*, then they are all above. And if they are of the *nisbat-e-adna*, then they are all below. Why? Because they are their slaves. The *A'imma* are the masters (*aqa*), the owners (*malik*), and all the *anbiya-e-kiram*, they are all slaves. They are all their... their... fostered ones (*parwarda*), their slaves, subservient (*ta'be'*) to them. They are subservient to the commands of the Imam (*ahkam-e-imam*). So, *Imamat* is lofty, it is exalted, it is of the *nisbat-e-ashraf* (more noble relation). *Nubuwwat* is of a lower station (*dheeley*), *Nubuwwat* is of the *nisbat-e-adna*, and it is much lower (*niche*).

Now, if you were to see this here, how should we understand it here? Since I am telling you that the place where they all gathered and stopped, that very place we call the *Ka'bah*. That is what we call the *Ka'bah-e-Ruhani* (Spiritual Ka'bah), the *Markaz* (Center), the *Qalb* (Heart). That is what we call the *Ta'mur*, that is what we call the *Dakhil-e-'Aalam-e-Ruhani* (Entrance to the Spiritual Realm), and that is what we call the *Bab-e-'Aalam-e-Ruhani* (Gate of the Spiritual Realm). So, since that is the *Bab-e-'Aalam-e-Ruhani* and the *Ka'bah-e-Ruhani*, you must have some relation to this *Ka'bah-e-Ruhani* through this Ka'bah. So, come to this Ka'bah. Let's reflect within this Ka'bah on what their station (*maqam*) would be. Meaning, reflect here and understand it over there. You have to reflect here and understand it there. You have to reflect here. You have to understand it there. That of this *Ka'bah-e-Ruhani*, the one that is the *dakhili Ka'bah* (internal Ka'bah)... the inner part of the Ka'bah, this Ka'bah is... what shape is it? It is of a conical (*makhruti*) shape. It is not square (*chaukhut*). It is not like this, with four sides made in this way. The Ka'bah is not like this. The Ka'bah is such that a wall comes from here, and this wall is called the *Hateem*. Its name is also *Hijr-e-Isma'il*. If you were to include this and draw a circle (*da'irah*), you would realize that a conical shape is formed.

So, the shape of the Ka'bah is conical, and the conical shape is that of our heart. This is the heart. The heart of the entire world (*jahan*) is the Ka'bah. And inside this Ka'bah, just as our heart has three membranes (*parde*), in the same way, it has three membranes. It has three parts (*hisse*). Of that Ka'bah. Because... now you will say, "If we dig the earth there and see..." You won't see anything by digging the earth. These are all spiritual matters. So, it has three parts. And these three parts are just like the chambers or membranes in our heart. So, absolutely... those parts of the heart, obviously their importance is much greater compared to the limbs that are attached to the heart or the veins that are attached to it. Their importance will not be as great as that of the things inside the heart. So, in exactly the same way, inside the Ka'bah, the cavities (*tajawif*)—they are called *tajawif* in our terminology, *tajawif* means chambers (*khanon*)—so the *tajawif*, the parts, the membranes, in that place were the *A'imma*. All the Imams were there. All the Imams resided there. And the outer parts, where we perform circumambulation (*tawaf*), which is called the *mataf*, where the *Maqam-e-Ibrahim* is, and from where you perform *tawaf*, that... that is, every... this is a wall, draw an arc here. This is... this is called the *bittiqah-e-shumali* (northern section), that is called the *bittiqah-e-junubi* (southern section), this is called the *gharbi* (western), and this is called the *sharqi* (eastern). So these are all *bittiqah*s, *bittiqah* means sections.

These are things that require a lot of understanding. In any case, I am telling you that the *tajawif* have more importance than the *bittiqah*s. So, who were the ones who came to the *bittiqah*s? They were the *Anbiya-e-kiram*. They were the *Anbiya-e-kiram*. And just as this our Ka'bah is the factory (*karkhana*) of life, that all of life that is being distributed and arranged is all from here. The fragrance is spreading from here. Seventy winds are blowing from here. Whether it is *dabr* or *qubur*, whose names have been mentioned, all the winds blow from here. The incidents (*hadithat*) come from here. All matters of life and death (*hayat-o-mamat*) are related to this very Ka'bah. And whatever things are coming into the world, whether it is raining or various incidents are occurring, the connection of all things, the connection of life and death, is with this very factory of the world (*karkhana-e-'alam*). With this very manifest Ka'bah.

This needs to be understood, how it is. So, just as this is a factory in which there are thousands of things and a tremendous work is being done. And what are its great pillars (*sutun*)? Its great pillars are the very things I mentioned to you: its *tajawif*, its *batayiq*, its *ma'e sa'id*, and its *azwa*, *anwa'*, its *hawaiyya*, and its... *Maqam-e-Ibrahim*, its *Maqam-e-Mimbar*, and *Maqam-e-Zamzam*. These are not ordinary things. This water and this... আরে, you will say that this is a living miracle (*mu'jizah*) of Islam, that since then until today, this well has not been able to dry up. But you are looking at the exoteric; I am looking at the esoteric, that the things that are being plundered from there, the grace (*faiz*) that is flowing, can never be stopped. From that spiritual Ka'bah. It cannot be stopped even from this physical Ka'bah. So, when this physical Ka'bah has these capabilities (*salahiyatein*), what will be the state of the spiritual Ka'bah?

Now are you understanding? So that spiritual Ka'bah, where all those souls were made to stop... were placed. And they were not included in the *'Aalam-e-Ruhani*. They did not receive *'ilm ma kana wa ma yakun* (knowledge of what was and what will be), they did not attain *qudrat-e-tammah* (complete power), they did not get *hayat-e-abadi* (eternal life). Meaning, they did not attain *kamal-e-thani* (second perfection). They did not attain it. And it's not that they were cast into this physical world either. "No, you neither go here nor go there, but remain suspended (*mu'allaq*) in between." And the place where they were made to stop, and the manner in which they were made to stop, that is what is called the *qalb-e-'alam* (heart of the world), that is what is called the *qalb-e-ruhani* (spiritual heart).

So, in this *qalb-e-ruhani*, how they were stationed, that is what I was telling you. That their arrangement (*tartib*) was in such a way that those above were all the *A'imma-e-kiram* (noble Imams), and those below, who were they? All the *anbiya-e-'izam* (great prophets). Now, among the *A'imma-e-kiram*, who all? I... I cannot list everyone's names, but I will tell you that there is Amir al-Mominin Ali, there is Janab Hasan, there is Janab Husayn, there is Imam Ali Zayn al-'Abidin, there is Janab Muhammad al-Baqir, there is Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq. There is Janab Mu'izz, there is Janab Mustansir, there is Janab... all these are the manifest Imams (*Imam-e-zahir*). This entire chain of Imams is running. If you go higher up, there is Janab Ibrahim, there is Janab Isma'il. You will see that in the Quran Majid, wherever Allah Ta'ala has mentioned the *Anbiya*, whenever a *Nabi* was mentioned, all the prophets were mentioned. So our Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, was he mentioned? He was also mentioned there. And he was mentioned quite a bit.

whenever a *Nabi* was mentioned, all the prophets were mentioned. So our Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, was he mentioned? He was also mentioned there. And he was mentioned quite a bit. Whose? Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, who was a friend of Allah, who had performed the sacrifice (*zabhiyyat*) of his son, Janab Isma'il. Indeed. The mention of Janab Ibrahim was made, but in what way was the mention made? That he is the one and only *Nabi* about whom it is stated—Allah Ta'ala says in the Quran Majid—*waj'alnahu li'l-nasi imama* ("And We made him an Imam for the people"). "O Ibrahim, We will make you an Imam for the people." So it became known that this was a special quality (*khususiyyat*) of Janab Ibrahim, that we consider him a *Nabi*, but he holds the rank of *Imamat*. He is an Imam.

So, just as, to explain a special quality, I told you, so now the *Anbiya*... these were the *A'imma-e-kiram*, who were takers of the higher relation, who were of the *nisbat-e-ashraf*, or who were the personalities residing above. Now, below... the personalities who came below, who were they? Our Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (*sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*) was there, and Janab... Janab Dhul-Kifl was there, Janab Shu'ayb was there, Janab Yusuf was there, Janab Daniyal was there, Janab Ayyub was there, Janab... Sham'un was there, Janab Dawud was there. There is an army (*lashkar*) of 124,000 prophets. It is a very large army. All were there. Now see, they have all been established. Now they are all established, and the Lord of the Worlds (*Parwardigar-e-'Alam*)—which Lord of the Worlds? ...'Ashir. That one who holds the administration in his hand. And who is that? The last individual (*fard*) of *Labbu nida'*. The last individual of *Labbu nida'* has now done what? To them... he told them... before giving a punishment, a word is spoken. In the same way... their condition was that they were in agony. They were feeling grief for their companions. And just as our human nature (*fitrat*) works here, there it was working even more intensely. And these people started to call out, started to explain, and began to say, "Believe it, understand it. What is it, brother? We have now become correct. See how successful we have become. You too, at least, become successful, and you too believe. And listen to the divine voice, accept the divine call (*da'wat-e-ilahi*). আরে, become *Sulaymani* (followers of Sulayman/submissive)!" This is what they were saying. And when the call was being given, that group to whom the call was being given, what did that group do? It started to listen. But what was the situation? How was the call being given? I want to explain that. Please understand.

The call was not being given in the way that the *'aql-e-awwal* was giving the call, or the *'aql-e-thani* was giving the call, or the third intellect was giving the call, or the last individual of its circle, 'Ashir, was giving the call, or the fourth intellect, or its... or 'Ashir, the tenth one, was giving the call, or the last of *tabu' batuti* was giving the call, or the last individual of *Labbu nida'* was giving the call. It was not a call like that. That was an individual call (*infradi da'wat*). It was the call of one person. Although he was receiving knowledge from everyone, he was receiving spirituality (*ruhaniyyat*), he was receiving grace (*faiz*), but it was one call. He was giving the call alone. He was giving the call alone. The entire administrator (*mudabbir*) was giving the call. The entire Universal Intellect (*'aql-e-kull*) was giving the call. But now the call that was being given, what kind of call was it? Team work. Now, it is to work together, unitedly. "We will all work together. Our community will work. We will work under the name *Hizb al-Iman* (The Party of Faith)." There you have it. Now this *Hizb al-Iman* that is working, this community of faith that is being established, what was it like? It was of all the *awliya Allah* (friends of God). It was of the *A'imma*, who were of the *nisbat-e-ashraf*, and it was of all the *Anbiya*, who were of the *nisbat-e-adna*.

Is it clear to you? Is it perfectly clear? So it was like this for *nisbat-e-'ala* and *nisbat-e-adna*. And all of them, all of them were giving the call. To whom were they giving the call? I told you that those who are minus *tabu' batuti*, minus *Labbu nida'*, minus *Kal-lamam*, who are left behind, they are giving the call to them. And who is sitting among them? Among them, we poor ones are also sitting. We are also sitting. But our rebellion is established. Our rebellion is established, and we were not ready to accept. That's why we were sitting there. Now, the group... our group was also divided. How many were with us? Countless. There were many. There were many of everything. Meaning, there was no deficiency of any kind. There were very many. There were also those who were absolutely not ready to believe. There were also those who were stuck in doubt and astonishment. There were also those who were moving towards a little remorse. They were there with this kind of state of being.

Now this state, which Allah Ta'ala has described... their condition was such that, just as the Quran Majid describes it, a remorseful person, the *nadim*, his state is such that if he is touched even a little, if he is provoked even a little, then look, he will completely... they say, "Oh brother, they've gone, they've become Allah Miyan's cow." But that "Allah Miyan's cow" is very good. We give it this name, "Allah Miyan's cow," or "shift-light," or that he bows his head, he does this or that. We think one should come with some pride, with some understanding, with some... this is nothing. So, the remorseful person has this capability within him, that if he is explained even a little, it is more than enough. Just the support of a finger is enough for him. He will grab hold of it. So this is the leaven of remorse. This is the remorse that is speaking to him, and he becomes ready to accept immediately.

So I was saying that the remorse that was happening there, what kind of remorse was it? It was that we were thinking in various ways. That there was a variation in remorse, there was a state of astonishment, there was insistence. But various were our states. Now, among these *Anbiya* and *Awliya*, first let me talk about their... my masters. What was the state of all these *Anbiya* and *Awliya* who are there? This is something to understand. And it is a very important thing. There, just as I told you, the points were established, and the order was established. And how was the order established? It was established on their remorse. On the leaven of their remorse, on their repentance, this order was established. And what was the order? It was that the very first being, if there was one, who was it? The coming *Qa'im al-Qiyamah*, *'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Are you understanding? The coming *Qa'im al-Qiyamah*, *'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*'s being was present there, and he was greater than all, he was there. Now you will say, "Greater in what way?" I will tell you. In what way he was greater, I will tell you, but for now, establish the order. This was there, and after him, if there was anyone in the order, it was Amir al-Mominin, Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Did you understand? Now you must be understanding what the station of Ali is. They call Ali God, and rightly so, that's the truth. So now it was Ali's station. And after Ali there were Hasan, Husayn, and so on. Now this chain was established and continued, and a complete line was formed. Now, how was this order established? That is what I am going to tell you about how the order was established. What happened was that there, everyone was given the initiative, everyone was given the right to "give the call to Allah." "It's team work. You should also call, you should also call, you should also call." Look, when the noble month of Ramadan comes, there are lessons here, there are lessons there. The people of Allah sit in the mosque, and the beloveds of Allah come and they recite. They are reciting here, they are reciting there. There is a lesson here, there is a lesson there. Even today, in Jamia Azhar, where I went and saw, that mosque where Sayyidna Qadi al-Nu'man used to teach, its platform has been made and elevated out of respect. But in other places, lessons happen, and in the same seating arrangement of the school, lessons happen. And all the different groups, as they sit, they do. So, just as the opportunity arises, in the same way, the lessons will be established. Absolutely the same situation happened. Everyone took their own lesson and sat down, and everyone began to make their own call, to call out. And everyone is calling.

If you say that since the *A'imma* were greater, and since they were elders, of the *nisbat-e-ashraf*, they should have been the only ones to call. They should have stopped this lower call, "What need is there for the *Anbiya* to speak? What need is there for these *Du'at* to speak? Be quiet. We are the ones calling, that is more than enough." No, it wasn't done like that. Since they were remorseful, they were *Kal-lamam*, everyone was given the right to speak. "You should give the call. This group that is unsuccessful and are deniers, they should be called." When they were given this full right, they were all giving the call. So now, they began to look at one another there, "Brother, I am giving the call, but let me see what call the other one is giving." Just as we have a habit here, that if there is, say, a cooking competition, from one pot, people will quickly leave and look at the other to see if they have added the spices or not, or if they have done this or that. So just as it happens here, or in an examination hall, one looks at another's paper to see... "Oh, he's getting up early." If he got up early, then one feels worried, "Come on brother, his is finished, we are sitting here until late, so we will get more marks." So now, just as there is a strange state, just as it is here, a somewhat similar state... there, such things don't happen, but there was a similar state, that they all, all of them who were watching... the inclination of all of them... the focus of all the *A'imma*... was on Amir al-Mominin, Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Everyone's gaze, the center of their gaze, had become... who? Mawla-e-Ka'inat, Mawla-e-Mushkil Kusha, Amir al-Mominin, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, had become the center. And everyone's center, the Ka'bah... he had become the Ka'bah. He had become the spiritual Ka'bah for everyone. Everyone's gazes were fixed there. "Oh brother, what call should we give now? The call..." Janab Fatimah is also observing, Janab Hasan is also observing, Janab Husayn is also observing, everyone is observing, and they are all observing that "No, if a call is to be given, one needs to learn from Ali ibn Abi Talib. If there is a call, it should be like this."

But what happened? Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, accepted the call, and he looked at the call of whom? Of Hazrat Qa'im, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, the coming one who will establish the Qiyamah. His gaze was on his call. Now what happened? If all of you are looking at me, and I start looking at the chandelier, what will you do? You will think that there must be some matter that his gaze has gone there, so we should also look. Come on. Naturally, while looking at me, you will start looking at the chandelier, because I looked at the chandelier. You were looking at me. So, in exactly the same way, everyone was looking at Ali. Ali was looking at Janab Qa'im. Everyone's gaze went to Janab Qa'im. Did you understand? Everyone's gaze went to Janab Qa'im. All the Imams of the Era of the Qa'im were called. The Era of Muhammadi and the Era of Qa'imi were called. All of them, all the Imams became attached to him. Are you understanding? All of the Imams became attached to whom? To Hazrat Qa'im, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Now, the being of Janab Qa'im became what? It is obvious that if you keep praising me, I will surely rise. From anyone's praise, a person... they say that he starts to fly. That state happens. So this is the state of a servant. Now, what happened there was that when everyone's gaze started to fall upon him, everyone started to learn, the state of Janab Qa'im became very lofty. The coming one, the establisher of Qiyamah, *'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*, *'ala dhikrihi al-salam*, his state became very lofty, and he became the Ka'bah for everyone. For all the *A'imma*. But what was the situation? Since everyone had first made their Ka'bah whom? Mawla-e-Ka'inat, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. For this reason, now when the gaze started to go towards Janab Qa'im, it started to go while stumbling a bit, that it is also seeing Ali, and also seeing Qa'im. It is also seeing Ali, and also seeing some of Qa'im. This state began to happen there. So, the gaze of all the *A'imma* was now where? On Janab Qa'im and also on Janab Ali. The gaze was there, and everyone was learning from Janab Ali. Are you understanding?

Now, what happened below? The one who was below, who was of the *nisbat-e-adna*, who were the *Anbiya*, like Janab Shu'ayb, Dhul-Kifl, and Janab Dawud, Sulayman, and all the *Anbiya*, as many as are mentioned in the Quran and as many as are not mentioned, all the *Anbiya*, Sham'un, Ayyub, Yusuf, Daniyal, all... as many *Anbiya* as there are, all of those *Anbiya*, *'alayhim al-salatu wa'l-salam*, within them... this state occurred, that everyone's gaze was falling upon Janab Ibrahim, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*. Understand? Everyone's gaze was falling upon Hazrat Ibrahim. And Hazrat Ibrahim's gaze was falling upon Hazrat Muhammad, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, *fida-hu ummi wa abi*, the master of the universe, the pride of all existence. His gaze was falling upon him, Hazrat Ibrahim's. And what happened? The gaze of all turned towards the master of the universe. All the prophets' focus, all the prophets' center became who? The master of the universe. The pride of all existence became everyone's center, and everyone's gaze is clashing there, and everyone is learning. "Oh brother, if we have to learn, we should learn from here. The method of the call is from here. The call will only come from this. What call do we know how to give? What the call is called, we don't know. What... we are doing it, but the correct way, the way the call has to be given, that has to be learned from the Prophet." So all are in the discipleship of the Prophet, all are learning a lesson from you, are learning. So this was the state, and Hazrat Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, everyone had made him their Ka'bah.

Suddenly a revolution came. What is fact is fact. The revolution that came was this: these relations were in their own place. Those of the noble relation were in their own place, those of the lower relation were in their own place. Suddenly an earthquake came, a great tremor came, a revolution came in the spiritual world. And it was this: Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, moved from his place. Now, I have to say all this because we are sitting in the physical realm. There, there is no place, no moving, no coming, no going. But for the sake of understanding, it is *taqriban li'l-afham* (an approximation for understanding). That the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, began to look down, thinking, "No, brother... the great thing is, the courageous thing is, to learn even from one's subordinate. If he is below, he should not be ignored." His gaze went to where? To those below. And he said, "Let's see what kind of call he is giving." When he turned his gaze to give the call, what was known? That among them, one is shining like the universal sun. And is so luminous that it is beyond description, and its rays are dazzling, and it is a very astonishing state, and its guidance is extremely tremendous. Who felt this? Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, who is in the noble relation. In the higher relation. The moment his gaze fell upon Janab Prophet, he said, "*Amantu*" (I believe). "I have brought faith." Meaning, the moment he brought faith, and the moment he accepted that "No, if there is a way, it is that of the master of the universe." So what happened? The gaze of one from the noble relation fell upon the master of the universe. Now, the gaze of the entire world, whether above or below... are you understanding? Whether in the noble relation or the lower relation, whether they are *A'imma* or *Awsiya* or *Hujjat*s or *Qa'im* or anyone below, whether *Anbiya* or *Awliya* or *Asfiya* or *Asqiya* or *Du'at*, the center of everyone's gaze became the Mercy to the Worlds (*Rahmatun li'l-'Alamin*), Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (*sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*). You became the soul of the spiritual world. And in this way, your state became.

Now, this state of yours that happened, the entire world shrank and gathered around you. And the master of the universe is shining in it as the sun of guidance. You see? But what is it? He is in the lower relation. Your occurrence, your beginning, your coming was in the lower relation. The Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*'s. And there, Ali is in the higher relation. Keep this in mind. Now what happened? Divine Power began to see that a great revolution has come. अरे, the one of the higher relation is doing this before the one of the lower relation, and the one of the lower relation is truly very lofty, which is why he has become the center of everyone's gaze. And the center of everyone's gaze has become him. There must be something in him. So, the moment Divine Power felt this... Divine Power... the last individual of *Labbu nida'*. The moment he felt this, he began to raise the throne. The Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*'s point (*nuqta*) was sent forth (*mab'uth*). And the master of the universe, who is being sent forth, you are being raised higher. This is the essential *Mi'raj*. You see? What will these Muslims tell of the *Mi'raj*? What will they tell of the *Mi'raj*? I will explain to you in full what the *Mi'raj* is. The true, essential *Mi'raj* of the master of the universe is this, that you were lifted from this throne. You were lifted from this floor and brought to the throne. You were brought to the throne. So now, who are the lifters? अरे, they are the *A'imma*. Those who are of the noble relation, they are lifting. Whose throne? Hazrat Muhammad Mustafa (*sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam*)'s throne. They lifted your throne and brought it, and after bringing it, they placed it in the higher relation. "No, no Prophet, how can you stay in the lower relation? You are in the noble relation. अरे, you are our most noble. How can you stay in the lower relation?" So this that happens, a... understand that if, say, he has not studied and passes the exam with a first class, then you look at him with great astonishment. So the Prophet who was coming, he had come in the lower station. अरे, he had come in a very low state, the Prophet, but he did not remain low. So how? Through his own excellence, through his own capability, through his own effects, through the characteristics of his prophethood, the Prophet won. And having won, he is now going where? His throne is rising higher and higher. Going on and on, the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, came into the higher relation. Now, after coming into the higher relation, now don't you ask. Now it is spring upon spring. That spiritual world's state, what can I describe of it? That in that spiritual world... if they have all become fresh flowers, if they have become the suns of guidance, if they have become luminous lamps, then who? The master of the universe. Except for the master of the universe, the lamp of all is extinguished. All are dim. Why? Because Ali is circumambulating around you. And all the *A'imma* are circling. Everyone's gaze is circumambulating him. So this sun of guidance, who was it? It was the being of the master of the universe, that Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*.

This is the very reason that the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, this should not be said right now, but I will tell you in great detail later, that when he came into this world here, what did you do? Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, you were seven or eight years old. When the occasion of *wa andhir 'ashirataka'l-aqrabin* (And warn your nearest kindred) came, you invited all your relatives over a pound of meat and a bowl of milk. And the Prophet said, "In my mission, in my work, in spreading Islam, who is ready to help me? People, is there anyone ready to become my helper?" So Janab Ali gets up and says... a seven-year-old child, what do you see? And he comes and says, "O Messenger of Allah, I am ready to become your helper. I am your brother, I am your supporter, I am your helper." So the Prophet says, "Yes, yes, O Ali, you are my supporter, you are my minister, you are my helper, you are my everything." You saw? This... this matter, what does it indicate? People have seen it in this light, whereas the world of Islam sees it in what light, I am telling you. Because there is animosity towards Mawla-e-Ka'inat, Amir al-Mominin, so they saw it in this light, that they said, "Janab Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, had said... 'Brother, I need a helper.' What else? A child, in his innocence, he was a naive, innocent child, what would he know of the world? Without understanding anything, he raised his hand, just as some children raise their hands in class. In that way, he said yes." আরে brother, if Ali was a child, and was speaking out of incomprehension, the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, was not a child. How did the Prophet accept Ali's call? How did the Prophet accept Ali as his supporter and his helper? The Prophet was accepting for this very reason, that he knew who Ali was. He understood Ali's personality. And there was no one who could read this gaze. If there was anyone there who could read it, it was Janab Salman, Janab Abu Dharr al-Ghaffari, Janab 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Janab Miqdad ibn Aswad. These were the personalities who were reading the gaze of prophethood, or were reading the gaze of Amir al-Mominin, who knew the secret. There were only a few, a handful of people who knew. Not everyone knew. अरे, the situation was, the spiritual knowledge of the Mawla was such, it has been told, that one time Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, the house he lived in... his house is still present in Kufa today. And in that house, Khatun-e-Jannat also lived there, Hazrat Fatimah al-Zahra. And you... often, you would go out for your labor. You would come back, you would rest, it would be nighttime. Qanbar, who was your slave, of Amir al-Mominin, he came one time. And just as Allah has commanded, that "when you enter a house, enter with permission." "May I come in?" So Janab Fiddah, who was Janab Fatimah al-Zahra's maidservant, she said, "Come, Qanbar, come. You can come." He entered. Upon entering, he said, "Where is my Mawla? My master and my lord, Amir al-Mominin, where is he? I need him, where is he?" So Janab Fiddah felt like making a joke. Janab Fiddah joked and said, "Mawla-e-Ka'inat, you are asking about him? You are asking about Hazrat Ali?" He said, "I have been asking the same thing since the beginning, where is Hazrat Ali?" So she said, "He must be in the heavens." "Heavens?" "He must be in the constellations. In the twelve sections that are there, he must be there. He must be in the sun, in Saturn, in Mars, in Jupiter. He must be in the sky, in the stars, in this, in that." Now she started saying strange things, Janab Fiddah, and Janab Qanbar was perplexed, bewildered. He said, "What are you talking about? I don't understand anything." So it became known that Hazrat Fiddah was more knowledgeable than Janab Qanbar. Although she was Fatimah's maidservant, he was Ali's slave. So Ali's slave was weaker in knowledge, but Janab Fatimah's maidservant was greater, that she understood, and she began to describe Janab Ali's conditions. So now, what were these conditions? अरे, the one in whose hand is the key to the spiritual world, who is the focus of the spiritual Ka'bah, who has become the center, what will we say about him? He was the center of gazes. He was the center of the *A'imma*. So, when everything had happened there, then what... Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, after knowing your states, could he make any deficiency? No. He could not make any deficiency. And he had to entrust that thing to you. When I... when I speak of the chain of *Imamat* and *Nubuwwat*, etc., in this world, and I will speak from Adam until this day, at that time I will explain it to you, you will enjoy it. If I speak now, you won't understand, and you won't enjoy it either. And that pleasure will not be there, the pleasure I want to create. So, the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*'s appointment at Ghadir and on other occasions is a matter of great importance, a momentous event, and I will prove and tell you what the inner secrets were, and what was happening. अरे, the Prophet was giving the rightful one his due. He was not just anyone. He was the one of the noble relation there. अरे, he who had become the true Ka'bah, he was that one. The Prophet was giving it to him. For this very reason, the Prophet, with great honor and respect, mentioned Amir al-Mominin. And one time, in excitement, he started to say, "Ali, in your praise I would say all things, but what can I do? The world... concerning 'Uzayr and 'Isa, they declared them sons of God. Concerning you too, what they will think, I don't know." But "For me too, there are not those things, Ali, that are for you." Now the people were perplexed, "O Messenger of Allah, what do you wish to say?" You were silent. For five minutes you were silent. Now the people were astonished, "What does he want to say? Ali has that which I do not have." Now the people were astonished, "What is this mystery that the Prophet wants to convey?" And the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, was silent. He was silent for a while, he tested them with his silence, and after taking the test, he said... *kallimu al-nasa 'ala qadri 'uqulihim* ("Speak to people according to their level of intellect"). "You have to speak to people according to their intellect." Now he saw that the audience is what it is. They always demand miracles. "Sometimes bring down angels, sometimes split the moon, sometimes make the wind blow, sometimes reverse the sun." Now these people, these ignorant Arabs, these Bedouin Arabs, they don't believe without miracles. So now what should I do with them? So in this way, the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, what did he do? He... finished the matter by explaining it away. So, in any case, what I was saying was that the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, concerning Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, you said three such things after that. And you said that "Ali... I did not get such a father-in-law as Ali got. I did not get such a bride, such a wife, as Ali got. And children like Hasan and Husayn, Ali got, I did not get." So, the Prophet said this thing, but that thing which the Prophet had finished, that was something else. This thing, you said it to make the people understand. And that thing was also correct in its own place. This thing is also correct in its own place. But the Prophet wanted to explain something else. And he wanted to show something else. But surely the Prophet, my Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, surely would have told. Those who sat on the mat, who bowed their heads before you, he must have told them. But he doesn't tell every single person. So, in any case, this state continued. And you saw that when all the Imams, the pure Imams, all of those Imams... Now you will say, you will have questions arising in your mind, "Fatimah al-Zahra came here in the form of a woman, in what form was she there?" For now, these forms, these things, the coming, the going, all these things, do not reflect on them for now. Because when I talk about the physical world, I will form this world, and after that, those things will be discussed. For now, what you have to reflect on is that all the noble Imams were there, and their center was who? Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib. For this very reason, he became *Abul-A'imma* (Father of the Imams). From here, the chain began, and *Imamat* remained in your progeny. But you were not an Imam yourself. আরে brother, a person who has done his M.A., to call him a matriculate or a B.A. is an insult to him. You should give him the station he has, the degree he has brought, the capabilities he has created, remember him by that, that is much better. So you, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib... the Prophet is saying, "*al-Hasan wa'l-Husayn, qama aw qa'ada, wa abuhuma khayrun minhuma*" ("Hasan and Husayn, whether they rise or sit, and their father is better than them"). "Hasan and Husayn are both true Imams, whether they rise for their right or they relinquish their right. But their father is better than them." So the Prophet, *'alayhi al-salatu wa'l-salam*, is saying such a thing. If he only had to state the *Imamat* of Hazrat Ali, he would have said, "Ali, Hasan, Husayn, all three are true Imams." The matter would have ended. To say just this much, would the Prophet speak like this, "Hasan and Husayn are both true Imams, whether they rise or don't rise, and their father is better than them"? Saying "their father is better than them" was indicating this, that he is not an Imam, but he is greater than an Imam, he is *Abul-A'imma*. This is what he was showing, that that goodness, that خیر-pan (quality of being the best), that is what the Prophet was showing, that Ali was greater than them.

So, you are at the rank of *Wasayat*. And *Wasayat*, this is not an ordinary *Wasayat*. Apparently, just as Adam's *Wasi* was Seth, Nuh's *Wasi* was Sam, Ibrahim's *Wasi* was Isma'il, and Musa's *Wasi* was Harun, 'Isa's was Sham'un. So... Janab Yusha. So Janab... all these, as many of the *Nutuqa* as had *Awsiya*, আরে not only this, as many *Anbiya* as there were, all appointed their *Wasi*. No prophet passed without appointing his *Wasi*. So if there was a master (*sardar*) of all the *Awsiya*, who was it? *Abul-A'imma*. That was Amir al-Mominin, Hazrat Ali. Now, the one whom you are calling *Abul-A'imma*, Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib, he is *Sayyid al-Wasiyyin* (Master of the Vicegerents). আরে, the matter of *Abul-A'imma* is greater than *Sayyid al-Wasiyyin*. So will you call him *Sayyid al-Wasiyyin*? So, to understand this, as far as explaining is concerned, there you can call him *Sayyid al-Wasiyyin*. আরে, where is *Sayyid al-Wasiyyin*? He has become *Abul-A'imma*. আরে, I don't even feel like saying *Abul-A'imma*. I feel like... the ranks that I counted out for you, I should establish him on those lofty ranks and show you what *Ahadiyyat* and *Samadiyyat* are like.

So, in any case, these were the states of Ali, because of which he is *Badr al-'aja'ib wa'l-ghara'ib*. Look through all of history, you will see that no one in history has been called *Mazhar al-'aja'ib wa'l-ghara'ib* (the Manifestor of Wonders and Marvels), that is, the one who manifests strange things. That has been said for Mawla-e-Ka'inat, Amir al-Mominin. That you... when you used to walk, what used to happen? The trees would also prostrate, the stones would also prostrate, and when animals came, they would speak, they would greet. This state was also there for Janab Amir al-Mominin. All these things were there. And all these things, the whole world was watching. Now you will say, "The historians there, the residents of Quraysh, they were seeing all these things. Then why did they deny? Why did they insult the Mawla so much? For the sake of the caliphate, why did they divide it like that? They should not have done it." What is happening today? Today, have you accepted the noble *Da'wat*? What are you doing? Have you accepted the noble *Da'wat* with your heart and soul? "Yes, brother, we have absolutely accepted it." No. Accepting and accepting are very different things. Accepting is what is called... when the obedience is also of the same kind. Believing also will be in such a way that there is obedience. For this very reason, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq was asked, "*Hal al-din?*" "O Imam, what is religion?" He said, "*Illa al-ta'ah*" (except obedience). "Religion is nothing but obedience." So it became known that the more obedience increases, the more the religion will increase. Whatever our religion is, that will be our faith. Because of faith, our ranks will be high, and we will be successful in the hereafter.

<!-- AUG:hazrat-zia lecture 7 -->

Although we too had an opportunity, but we also made a mistake there. We also made a mistake there, and we were not ready to accept. Had we accepted, we would have been counted among the *taaboot-e taabooti*. Had we accepted, we would have been counted among the *labb-u nida*. If we had accepted, we would have entered into the *kal-lamam*. So now we were not counted among any of them. And where did we remain? We remained included in that same disobedient group. For now, we are included. Now, since the command had come to him, the divine command, which was coming from God, the Lord of the Worlds (*Rabb-ul-‘aalameen*). And who is the Lord of the Worlds? The First Intellect (*aql-e awwal*). The command was coming from the First Intellect that now, *inṭaliqū ilá ẓillin dhī thalāthi shu`ab* (Go forth to a shadow with three branches), that you should go towards a shadow with three prongs. Now cast them down, remove them from here; they are not worthy of living in the sacred realm (*‘aalam-e quds*). This is a pure realm (*paak ‘aalam*), this is a sacred realm (*qudsaani ‘aalam*), a spiritual realm (*ruhaani ‘aalam*). This physical realm (*jismaani ‘aalam*) and the realm of similitudes (*mushabbihaat ka ‘aalam*), or a realm that embraces darkness (*zulmat lene waale ‘aalam*), has no business with this. It is necessary for them to leave this place. Anyway. Now, what happened was that just as every being above looks upon the one below with an eye of mercy (*rahm*) and acts with an eye of grace (*karam*), in exactly the same way, here too, all of them started to work, and here the call (*da‘wat*) ceased to be individual (*infradi*) and became collective (*ijtimaa‘i*). Where was the individual call? It was with the First Intellect, with the Second Intellect (*aql-e saani*), with the Tenth (*‘aashir*), or with the circles (*dawaa’ir*) whose leaders (*sardaar*) were intellects, it was with them, or it was with the Tenth, or it was with the last individual of the *taaboot-e taabooti*, or it was with the last individual of the *labb-u nida*. These were all individual calls. But the call that is happening now is of a completely different kind. And how is this call happening? It is happening in a collective manner; that is, it is a collective call. Everyone is calling, and everyone feels the urgency. They all understand that we are bound by this, and indeed, the last individual of *labb-u nida* had bound them, that you must be reformed by them, and you must reform them. So now, all of them began to make the call collectively; teamwork began. Teamwork began, and everyone started to call them. But as I said to you, I will move forward while reiterating a little. There were two affinities (*nisbatein*) there that the First Intellect had left behind. They proceeded on these two affinities; they began to walk on these same narrow paths. And what were those affinities? The nobler affinity (*nisbat-e ashraf*) and the lower affinity (*nisbat-e adna*). The *nisbat-e ashraf* was related to its existential essence (*ma huwa wujudi*), and the *nisbat-e adna* was related to its own self (*ila-zaati*). That is, the affinity of the First Intellect towards its own self (*zaat*) was weaker, and its affinity towards God Almighty (*Allah Ta‘ala*), towards the Unseen of the Unseen (*Ghaib-ul-Ghuyoob*), towards the Exalted Originator (*Mubdi‘-e Ta‘ala*), that was the higher affinity. On these two affinities that it had left, some people began to run. What does "began to run" mean? Not the people, but their minds (*azhaan*) began to run; their intellects began to work. And their intellects worked in such a way that some people accepted the higher affinity, and some people accepted the lower affinity. These were *‘alafi* (of the highest rank), *‘uqool* (intellects); they were splendid, luminous, souls (*nufus*), sacred (*qudsaani*), spiritual (*ruhaani*). They are all spiritual entities (*ruhaani zawaat*). All are spiritual entities. So, compared to these spiritual entities, those entities—the entity of the First Intellect, or the entity of the Second Intellect, or the entity of the Holy Presence (*Hazrat-ul-Quds*), or the entities of all the intellects of the circles—are immeasurably superior. They have no standing. Are you understanding? And here, what has the world of Islam understood? *ba‘d az Khuda buzurg tu’i qissa mukhtasar* (After God, you [the Prophet] are the greatest; the story is brief). After sending blessings and peace upon the noble Prophet, what do they say? That after God Almighty, if any descend, it is from monotheism (*tawhid*) that they descended, and they came and ended at the Prophetic mission (*risaalat*). So this is the state of the world of Islam. This is the courage of the people of faith (*ahl-e imaan*) and their reward, that the Lord of the Worlds made us aware of such secrets (*asraar*). So that we could know, that look, how many more heavens have been created and how many spiritual things have come into being, and there are countless beings whose names cannot even be mentioned, and whose roles we cannot describe, as to what kind of end they are bringing about. Anyway, they are all high beings. Those who came into the active field, who said "yes" after saying "no," and who affirmed after denying, were countless entities; some took the higher affinity, and some the lower. Some went towards the *nisbat-e ashraf*, some towards the *nisbat-e adna*. Those who went towards the *nisbat-e ashraf* were the noble Imams (*aimma-e kiraam*). And those who went towards the *nisbat-e adna*, who were they? They were their servants, their slaves, their subordinates, their followers, those who obeyed them, who walked on their paths (*shari‘at*), who carried out their commands; they were under their construction, under their command. And who were they? They were the Prophets (*anbiya*), the pure ones (*asfiya*), the friends of God (*auliya*), the proofs (*hujjatein*), the summoners (*du‘at*), the messengers (*rasool-ein*). All of these, as many as there are, the *du‘at*, *anbiya* and all of them, are on a lower level. You could say that if the former are at the level of planning (*tadaabir*), then the latter are at the level of detail (*bataa’ib*). If the former are inside the spiritual Ka‘ba, in the middle, then the latter are in the vicinity of the Ka‘ba. There was a world of difference between them in knowledge. When the affinities changed, then obviously, although in this very world there is night and there is day, the matter of the day is different and the matter of the night is different. So in the same way, what happened here? That despite that, such an affinity was established, and such a great and clear (*bayyin*) difference emerged before you. And I had told you that now when the call began, to understand that call, I had left a point here, and for that reason I will tell you this: that the call that was happening, although it was not individual but collective, along with being collective, that call had another quality. What was that? Meaning, from the First Intellect to the last individual of *labb-u nida*, all the calls that had happened are called affirmative (*musbit*) calls; they were positive calls. They were positive calls, where only one command was coming: "Do." "Practice monotheism (*tawhid*)." No prohibition was coming, no restriction saying "Don't do this." Now what happened? The call that is coming now, what is it? Now it is not an affirmative but a negative (*manfi*) call. That now, along with "do," the command to "stop" is also coming. Commands (*awaamir*) are coming, and prohibitions (*nawaahi*) are coming. Do this, don't do that. This is lawful (*halaal*), this is forbidden (*haraam*). This food is okay, that food is not okay. This clothing is okay, that clothing is not okay. This work is okay, that work is not okay. Now in everything, you will see that religion (*din*) has remained even in clothing, religion has remained even in eating and drinking, religion has remained even in our conversations. So there is religion in everything. So this matter of commands and prohibitions that has arisen, why did it come? It came for this reason, that now it is a negative call. This is why God Almighty said: *ma ataakum al-rasulu fa-khudhuhu wa ma nahakum ‘anhu fa-ntahu* (Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it). That whatever the Prophet gives you, take it, and what he stops you from, stop. Beware, do not take a step forward. *fa-ntahu*, stop. So when the Quran says this, it becomes known that what the Messenger is telling... and the noble Imams were very much inclined towards this, and they explained it clearly. God willing, when that topic comes, I will tell you. But anyway, the person of the noble Prophet is the most clear person, a special person. In that regard, you can see that God Almighty commanded His Prophet: O Prophet, convey it to the community. Whatever you command, they should take, and whatever they are stopped from, they should stop from. So it becomes known that this is the trend of the negative call, and the negative call began. Where? In this teamwork. Along with the collective call. Now, along with the negative call, what happened? Those of the higher affinity were in God's mercy and fragrance (*rauh-o-raihaan*). So were those of the lower affinity not? They too were in God's mercy and fragrance. But the station (*maqaam*) of both is different. The affinities are different. If you take gold and throw it in mud, or take a diamond and throw it in mud, it will still shine. It will keep shining and will glitter. So on it, that dirtiness or muddiness will not come. That diamond will definitely show its luster. No matter what kind of place it gets. So here, they got a good place with God Almighty. And even if they were ahead or behind, whatever station they got, they would have remained in their place, having taken that station. They had taken the higher affinity. Those who took the higher affinity, took it, and those who took the lower affinity, remained below; they became the lower ones. Whether they sat above or below. Anyway, for our understanding, for our minds, I was saying that they are in one line, understand, and these are in another line. Those are above, these are below, so that your minds can properly set it and understand. And I was saying that among all those Imams and entities, among those who took the *nisbat-e ashraf*, whose was the highest self? The Master of the Age (*saahib-e asr*). This one who is the *Qaa’im-ul-Qiyamah ‘ala jaddihis-salaam* (the one who establishes the Resurrection, peace be upon his ancestor), who is the establisher of the resurrection, who is to come, that self was the greatest of all. No self was greater than his self. And if after him... now you will say, "Were numbers assigned there? What?" Nothing. In whatever way the wealth was, in whatever way they achieved perfection, they did it. *man jadda wajada* (He who strives, finds). Whoever tried, found. There, as the call was, so he found. He who expanded his vision, who gave importance to his vision, and who showed his speed, he moved forward. So there, in that race, in that running, we will have to see how much he achieves. So this was the race, that there, inside that contest, whoever came, came. So at that time, the one whose point was established, whose point was it? It was of Maulana *Qaa’im-ul-Qiyamah ‘ala jaddihis-salaam*. And after him, if anyone's point was established, who was it? Hazrat 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, upon him be prayers and peace. And after that, the points of four Imams were established in succession. There is no need to list them all: Fatimah al-Zahra was there, Hasan al-Mujtaba was there, Husain, the Martyr of Karbala was there, Imam Zayn al-'Abidin was there, Maulana Muhammad al-Baqir was there, Ja'far al-Sadiq was there, Ismail was there. They all continued in sequence. But now you will say, Fatimah al-Zahra was also there as a woman... Oh, there is no distinction between man and woman there. Rather, she has the status of a man there, understand. But the distinction between man and woman does not even exist there. It is a spiritual realm. These are all characteristics of the physical realm. When I get to that, I will go into great detail. Right now, I haven't even touched upon the physical realm. Right now it is the spiritual realm. So at that time, when the call to God (*da‘wat il-Allah*) was going on, within that call to God, I had told you that everyone's gaze, while making the call, saw the best call. Whose? That of the Commander of the Faithful, Hazrat 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, upon him be prayers and peace. That there is no one who can make the call better than you. If there is a call, it should be like this; if there is ingenuity, it should be like this; if there is vision, it should be like this; if there is intelligence, it should be like this; if there is a decision, it should be like this; if there are virtues, they should be like this. All those gazes, the gaze of all the Imams... it wasn't necessary there. It wasn't necessary at all. It was possible that Janaab-e Muhammad would move ahead, possible that Hasan would move ahead, anyone could have. But what to do, the way it happened, fact is fact. What happened has to be narrated. What happened became history. Whatever happens becomes history. The history that was made was that the manifestation (*mazhar*) for all, the center (*markaz*) for all, and the candle of guidance (*sham‘-e hidayat*) for all, who was he? Hazrat 'Ali ibn Abi Talib. Hazrat 'Ali ibn Abi Talib... everyone's gazes were falling upon him, and they were learning from your call, understanding that whatever call there is, it is the call of 'Ali, and it was 'Ali and only 'Ali. "Wherever I look, there is only You." It was 'Ali and only 'Ali, on all four sides. 'Ali's name was supreme, 'Ali's drum was beating. But what happened? The Master of the Universe (*Maula-e Kaainaat*) looked where? Towards Janaab-e Qaa’im. As soon as he looked towards Janaab-e Qaa’im... and what does it mean to look? It means to learn, to take from him, to benefit (*istifaada*) from him, to acquire from him, whatever to take from him. So as soon as he tried to benefit and as he took from Janaab-e Qaa’im, what happened immediately? All the gazes, for which 'Ali had been the center, now who became the center? Janaab-e Qaa’im became the center. This was the first state (*kaifiyat*) that was established there. Now, all the spirits (*arwaah*) are in this situation, in this state. All those who are *kal-lamam*, all those who are Prophets and Messengers and Imams, all of them are watching, and such a state is going on there that suddenly, in the lower part... below, the entities that were there, the Prophets who were there, Janaab-e Sham‘un (Samuel) is there, Dhul-Kifl is there, Sulayman (Solomon) is there, Dawud (David) is there, Yusuf (Joseph) is there, Yunus (Jonah) is there, Ya‘qub (Jacob) is there. All these prophets, the chain of 124,000, and many more. All those prophets are in their places, and among them is the Leader of the Universe, the Pride of Creation, the most sacred person of Hazrat Muhammad al-Mustafa, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Now, when everyone's center had become who, here? Now, was it necessary there that a center be made? It was not necessary. This was the first blueprint being made; it wasn't necessary. Whoever wanted to could make the call in their own place. There was no need to accept anyone as a teacher. But what can be done, he was accepted. At the time he was accepted, he was accepted. We are narrating that. Otherwise, there was no need for anyone to be appointed as a teacher. So there, everyone was looking at the most sacred person of the Prophet, peace and prayers be upon him, that if there is a call, it should be a call like yours. For this reason, he became the Master of the Prophets (*Sayyid-ul-Anbiya*). He became the leader of all the prophets. The Master of the Messengers and the Master of the Prophets (*Sayyid-ul-Mursaleen o Sayyid-ul-Anbiya*). Whose person became this? The Prophet's, peace and prayers be upon him. As the Master of the Prophets, Master of the Two Worlds (*Sayyid-ul-Kaunain*), Master of the Messengers (*Sayyid-ul-Rusul*), you are the Prophet, peace and prayers be upon him, that this state is going on, above and below. This affair is happening that Hazrat 'Ali... that Hazrat 'Ali, leaving everything, started to look down, that there is a need to learn from the Prophet, peace and prayers be upon him. If a call is to be made, this is the call, and this is the style of making a call. Now look, as it is said among us, that if one has to learn, what difference does it make if it's from a junior? If the junior has knowledge, then take knowledge from the junior, learn it. So it is the same matter. Although the Prophet was lower (*dani*), inferior (*adna*), junior, but what did Janaab-e 'Ali do? He turned towards him and started learning from him. And as soon as he turned towards him, what happened? All the noble Imams turned. Those who were looking at 'Ali now started looking at the Prophet. All the prophets were already looking at the Prophet. Now, the center of the entire spiritual realm, of the Ark (*taabuut*), who became it? The most sacred person of the Prophet, peace and prayers be upon him. This is the Ascension of the Prophet (*mi‘raaj-e nabi*), peace and prayers be upon him. That such was the sharpness of his vision, and such was your grandeur, and your specialty of Prophethood was so tremendous, that what happened now? That you... God Almighty said that your throne (*‘arsh*) should be raised. Accordingly, your throne was raised, and you were lifted from the lower affinity and placed in the higher affinity. As soon as you were taken from the lower affinity and placed in the higher affinity, *dana fa-tadalla, fa-kana qaba qawsayni aw adna* (He drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer). He reached that station; the *mi‘raaj* of the Prophet was achieved. Now it is another matter, that distance of two bow-lengths or nearer, to understand this, these are secrets; God willing, when you read it in the tradition (*taqleed*), you will understand. But for now, understand that station, *fa-awha ila ‘abdihi ma awha* (And He revealed to His servant what He revealed). God Almighty revealed to His Prophet what He had to reveal. So all these things that are happening, for whom are they happening? For the person of the Prophet, peace and prayers be upon him. The *mi‘raaj* is being bestowed upon you. And the Prophet's *mi‘raaj* happened, and you were established in the Praised Station (*Maqaam-e Mahmood*). The crown of excellence was placed upon you, and you, for this entire universe, for that entire spiritual universe, what did you become? You became the crown. And you began to shine as the candle of guidance.
