So for one thought, you have to do a lot of thinking. So a person's blood burns, that's when thought occurs. So in the same way, some part of the person was consumed in it, it was spent, then it became *naatiqa*. Some was spent, then it became *hissiya*. Some was spent, then it became what? *Naamiya*. Now the degrees that were established, they were established according to that, there. According to their own respective levels. Now whoever created their *naatiqa* in a certain way, it was created that way. *Naamiya* was created as it was, *hissiya* was created as it was. Now what happened? Here, for you, the *naamiya*... what is the storage of *naamiya*? The moon. The moon is the center for all the *naamiya* of the world. You might think, does the moon only do this job? No. The moon has twenty jobs in our *da'wat*. In the *Da'wat-i Haadiya-yi Sulaymaaniyya*, the moon has many jobs. But the moon also does this job, that it has become a station for the *naamiya*. Now, explanations will come to you, Insha'Allah, about the moon, many of them. About the sun also they will come, about all the stars they will come. But the moon also handles this *naamiya*, and when do you get this *naamiya*? When that waste product is ready and prepares its son, then that thing is given to it. You say, "Life has entered, brother." *Wa 'ansha'naahu khalqan aakhar* (Then We developed him into another creation). The Quran says that We created a new creation. So what is this new creation? It is that life that was put into it. Where did the life come from? Did God, *'alamiyya*, take it out of His pocket? *Na'oozubillah*. Hey, it is its own thing being given to it, which was entrusted from the moon. And what was the storage for *hissiya*? The sun. A ray was received from the sun, due to which sensation (*hiss*) was created. And if sensation is not created, then see, the nurse spanks that child so that life enters it. Sensation comes into it. So she makes it cry so that life comes into it. So this means that sensation... But the thing to cry about is that if, suppose, one has reached maturity and we are not mindful of the noble covenant (*'ahd-i shareef*), it means that the original life that is to be taken, we are unaware of it. What is that original life? It is the *naatiqa*. That is our *naatiqa*. It is lying there, we are sitting here, we are not taking the noble covenant. So whose fault is this? It is our fault. If we took the noble covenant, then that thing which we are to receive, we will surely receive it. And all three of your souls (*nafs*) will be present with you. Now what will we have become? A perfect human, that all three souls are present with us. Now, just as these three souls have come, they will also go in the same way, and the description of their going will come. Insha'Allah, I will explain it then. For now, I was explaining how these three souls come: the vegetative soul (*nafs-i naamiya*), the sensory soul (*nafs-i hissiya*). And whose are they? They belong to that same one. And how are they? The form (*shabeeh*) it had, the intellect it had, something from within it was spent. It is its own thing that it is receiving. The *naamiya* is receiving its own. Life is its own thing. Life is not something that Allah is putting in a new way into it. No. The body, life, everything is one thing. The thing is one. Some was called soul, some was called body. Because it was one thing, so see, oil does not mix with water. But it was one thing, so you will say, this is the power of Allah, that Allah joined the body and the life. But why did He join them? Because it was its own thing, and it joined. Otherwise, it would not have joined at all. So one thing was this, and the second thing I said was the intellect. And the substance of the intellect is a very transparent substance, a very pure substance, which Allah Ta'aala gave. And what is it? It is a thing from there, from the world of creation. What is intellect called? On this, an incident came to my mind. Of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam, one time, it was Wednesday, it was the day of *chaarshamba*, it was the month of Rajab, and you were consuming rice and yogurt. These two things, rice and yogurt, you were eating them mixed, when Janab Abu Hanifa, who is the Imam of all Muslims today, he came. He was a student of Hazrat Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam. The whole world acknowledges this. Anyway, he, there... Janab Abu Hanifa Saaheb, who was there, he was the Grand Mufti (*Mufti-yi A'zam*) in Baghdad, he had become the Chief Justice, he used to give fatwas, and he... So, since he had studied with the Imam 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam, the Imam 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam would always caution him, saying, "Brother, why are you starting to give fatwas? This is all wrong work, this is a very wrong thing." He had explained this to him in the beginning. But despite that, he did not listen and went and started giving fatwas regularly, and he became a mufti, a very great, the most prominent mufti of that era, and he was working in the capacity of a mufti. Since he was a student of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam, you came to meet the Imam one time. Janab Abu Hanifa. Now he came, and when he came, it was a Wednesday, and by chance, you were eating rice and yogurt mixed together. So the Imam said, "O Abu Hanifa, come, join me in the meal, Bismillah." Abu Hanifa Saaheb said, "Imam, what you are eating, by chance, I have just eaten the same thing and come." You said, "Look, what you have eaten is not what I am eating, and I am eating this specifically, and you must have just eaten it casually. But I am telling you that on Wednesday, this is eaten with a special intention, with the intention of expanding one's provision, as is the custom with us." On Wednesday, on some Wednesday of Rajab, these things are done. It was only rice and yogurt. With us, since we add a lot of things, we added a lot of spices to it, and also put coconut and sugar in it. And until there is sugar, it doesn't even feel right. And sweetness and all sorts of things are in it, then stomach ailments also come. So all these ailments and so on, that wasn't there. What Imam 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam had initiated was just rice and yogurt. Anyway, he was eating and... So Janab Abu Hanifa said that, "Brother, I have eaten this and come." The Imam fell silent. After that, when you had finished eating, you got up, and the Imam, leaning on a staff, after washing his hands, leaning on a staff, you came to the veranda. So as soon as you came, Janab Hanifa stepped forward, and stepping forward, he began to say, "Imam, you are not so weak, and you have already taken a staff. This is not such a state of old age for you. Why did you take a staff?" So, Janab Hanifa said... Janab the Imam said, "You are commenting on me taking a staff, that I am not so weak. Well, I have not taken it because of weakness. This is not my staff of old age (*'asaa-yi peeri*). I have taken this because this is the staff of the Prophet 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam, and I have kept it in my hand for blessing (*tabarrukan*)." So, quickly Abu Hanifa bowed and began to say, "Wow, I should kiss this staff, it was in the hands of the Prophet 'alayhi 'l-salaatu wa 'l-salaam." So the Imam got extremely angry, and his eyebrows furrowed, and you pulled the skin of your hand like this. You pulled it hard and raised it, and raising it, you said, "O Abu Hanifa, just tell me, in these veins that are beneath this, whose blood is flowing?" Because they had not done *musaafaha* (handshake). He had not kissed the hand. He said, "Whose blood is flowing in this, tell me." Immediately, Abu Hanifa realized, "No, I have made a mistake," and he bowed to kiss it. The Imam pulled up his sleeve. He pulled up his sleeve and did not let him kiss it. After that, you said, "O Abu Hanifa, it is a disaster. I am seeing your fatwas, and you are working based on opinion and analogy (*ra'y-o qiyaas*). And why are you doing this work of giving fatwas? Being my student, you are doing this. I feel very sorry for you." Janab Abu Hanifa said, "Imam, I give answers from the book of God. I give answers from the book of God, and obviously, I am... in this matter..." "I regularly study the book of God properly and give answers." The Imam immediately and spontaneously said, "Okay, if you give answers from the book of God, then just tell me... *fa-dalnaa feeha 'l-sayr, seeroo feeha layaaliya wa ayyaaman aamineen* (And We ordained therein journeys. Travel through them by night and by day in safety). This verse of the Quran Majeed you read, and you said, what is its meaning and what is its implication, explain it to me." In it, Allah Ta'aala says, "Journey, day and night, and in امن (peace/safety)..." which is a place of immense peace, and Allah has mentioned this in it. Janab the Imam said, "If this is the path from Makkah to Madinah, how many examples can I give you of caravans being looted here. People were killed, caravans were looted, their belongings were taken. Now how are they in peace, tell me?" Janab Abu Hanifa fell silent. You said, "Okay, Abu Hanifa, if not this verse, then tell me another verse: *man dakhalahu kaana aaminan* (Whoever enters it is safe). This verse of the Quran Shareef is a famous verse. Just tell me its translation, what does it mean?" He said, "Imam, 'whoever enters it is safe,' this is about the Sacred Precinct of the House of Allah (*Harami Baytullah*), about the Ka'bah." "And..." So you said, "This verse is about the Ka'bah?" He said, "Yes, of course. What place could be more secure than this? Hey, the house of Allah, the pure house, what could be more secure..." You said, "Then the two famous murders which I can list for you: 'Abdullah bin Zubayr and Sa'd bin Zubayr, both of them were killed, which is something that generally every person knows, you must know too." "Yes, yes, I know." You said, "Then how were they killed? If this were a place of peace, then Allah should have protected them here. How were they killed in this place of peace?" He fell silent. You said, "Okay..." So, quickly Abu Hanifa Saaheb said, "Imam, I work based on analogy (*qiyaas*)." You said, "*Awwal-a man qaasa Iblees* (The first one to use analogy was Iblis). The one who uses analogy, he had said... the teacher of the angels had said, *khalaqtani min naar wa khalaqtahu min teen* (You created me from fire and you created him from clay). Adam was created from clay, and I was created from fire. So he had asserted his superiority. Do you think this is correct? This analogy of yours is not right." "No," he said, "with analogy, I absolutely figure things out. Why has Allah given intellect? We... get a lot from it." You said, "Okay, tell me. If you can tell by intellect, then tell me, is fornication a bigger sin, or is murder?" "Which is a bigger sin, murder or fornication?" Immediately he said, "To take a person's life, what could be a bigger sin than this? In fornication, a person doesn't die. It is a sin, God's, but fornication is fornication and murder is murder. Murder..." So the Imam said, "O Abu Hanifa, just tell me, why are two witnesses required for murder and four witnesses for fornication?" He became distressed. He started to say, "Now this is..." You said, "Why?" Then you said, "Okay, tell me, if not this question, then I'll ask another. Is the substance of procreation (*maadda-yi tawleedi*) impure, or a drop of urine?" He said, "A drop of urine is impure." The Imam said, "Upon the emission of a drop of urine, ablution (*wudu*) is required. And upon the emission of the substance of procreation, a full bath (*ghusl*) is required. Tell me, which is more impure?" Now he's distressed. At that point, the Imam said, "Okay, tell me this, Abu Hanifa, that here... Janab Musa was commanded, Janab Musa and Janab Harun were commanded, *Is'hab ila Fir'awn innahu taghaa* (Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed). O Musa, O Harun, go to Pharaoh, for he has rebelled. Now you will have to work to reform him." After that, Allah Ta'aala says, *la'allahu yatazakkaru aw yakhshaa* (Perhaps he may be mindful or fear). "Perhaps he may remember and become afraid." He may remember and fear God. So "perhaps," Allah is saying, *la'alla*. The word is *la'alla*, "perhaps" he will. So, did Allah have a doubt? Does Allah have a doubt? *La'allahu yatazakkaru aw yakhshaa*. "Tell me." He fell silent, Abu Hanifa Saaheb. So the Imam said, "Okay, if not this..." He said, "Imam, I use intellect to make decisions. Different forms are created for me, and I choose from those forms and extract [the answer]." You said, "Okay, if you say so, then I will present a form to you." You, there, raised various limits and the continuity of the Shari'ah, you explained its continuity. I am leaving that because I don't want to create confusion for you. Leaving those ambiguous matters, I am telling you. At that time, the Imam said, "Okay, tell me this, Abu Hanifa. There are two people. One is a master, one is a slave. You understand master and slave. And for the Arab people, this is a very famous thing, and even now, slavery is going on somewhere or the other. Master and slave. The slave is bought with money. A slave is a slave, a master is a master. Both of them got married at the same time. And at the same time, Allah Ta'aala granted both of them two sons. To the master and to the slave. Both were granted two sons, and after the two sons were granted, both of them went away. Where did they go? Before these boys were born, both of them went on a journey. Obviously, the slave would be with his master. He went on a journey with the master. When they went on the journey, both their children were born, and as soon as the children were born, that house collapsed, and both their mothers died. Now only their children are left. Now tell me, Abu Hanifa, out of these, which child belongs to the master and which belongs to the slave?" He said, "Mawla, this is a rather difficult matter." You said, "What is difficult? You talk about using your intellect. I am asking you based on that." "Okay, leave this. You say that you work with intellect. I will ask you a question of pure intellect. Tell me, a blind man poked out the eye of a man with good vision. The Quran is commanding retribution (*qisaas*). And the meaning of *qisaas* is *al-'ayn bi 'l-'ayn, al-'uzn bi 'l-'uzn, al-yad bi 'l-yad* (The eye for an eye, the ear for an ear, the hand for a hand). An eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, retribution should be taken. This is a Quranic verse. Now, this is a Quranic verse, and there is retribution for it. Now tell me, what's the point of poking out the eye of a blind man? He is already blind. What will be achieved by poking out his eye? Now how will retribution be taken?" He started to say, "Imam, you have asked a rather strange and difficult question." So the Imam said, "Am I asking all difficult questions? You are not answering any of them." He said, "You... please... you have put me in such a dilemma." Well, the Imam said, "Okay, brother, I... I am also knowledgeable in the science of the body (*'ilm al-abdaan*). I am knowledgeable in the science of the body, I am knowledgeable in all things," Janab Abu Hanifa said to the Imam. You said, "You, being my student, are boasting of knowledge in front of me? Okay, I will ask you a question from the science of the body. Tell me, in a person's head, Allah has created four fluids (*lu'aab*). There are four fluids that have been created in a person's head: the tear of the eye, the wax of the ear, the saliva of the mouth, and the fluid of the throat (*lu'aab*). Four fluids. You might say that the saliva of the mouth and the fluid of the throat are one. No, they are different. The fluid of the throat is different, and the saliva of the mouth, the saliva of the lips, is different. And the tear of the eye is different, the wax of the ear is different. You said, tell me, what was Allah's wisdom in this, that He created four fluids in the head? Why is the ear wax bitter? Why are the tears of the eye salty? And why is the lip's... that thing, sweet? And why is the fluid of the throat tasteless?" "Tell me the reason for this." Janab Abu Hanifa said, "Imam, this seems very easy, but I will think about it and tell you. I will think and tell you." You said, "No, no, there is no time for thinking. If you are to tell me, tell me now." He said, "Mawla, you are, after all, my teacher. Please be so kind as to tell me this." When he... pleaded a lot, you explained, "Look, the eye is salty so that if any dirt gets into the lens of the eye, it will come out because it is salty. If it were sweet, it would not come out. It comes out because it is salty. And the ear wax is for this reason, that if insects and bugs, even if they happen to go in, they will... first, the paths are made crooked so that they do not go in. But if they do go in, they will die from that fluid. It is bitter for this reason, it is poison for them. And the saliva of the mouth is made sweet for this reason, that we... Allah Ta'aala says in the Quran Majeed, *min al-maa'i hayaat* (From water is life). Water is life. Everyone's life is from water. Allah has said this in the Quran. So it becomes known that when a person drinks water, it should feel sweet. Water itself is not sweet. The saliva of the mouth makes it sweet. That is why it has been made sweet, so that the taste of water is sweet. Now, as for the fluid of the throat being made tasteless, it is for this reason, that all the different tastes of the world, you can feel them separately. You eat chocolate, you get its taste separately. You eat something else, you get its taste separately. So the throat's tasteless fluid has been made so that you can feel every taste separately." He began to say, "Yes, Imam, your place is empty and that is so." You said, "O Abu Hanifa, you make such a claim, that you have figured things out with intellect, with opinion and analogy, and you work with intellect and conjecture. Just tell me, then, what is intellect?" Because I was talking about intellect, so let's get to the topic of intellect. You said, "Okay, tell me, what is intellect?" He said, "Imam, this is also a matter? Intellect is a very, very simple thing. It is to distinguish between good and bad." "To distinguish between good and bad, this is a tool that Allah has granted us." You said, "If this is the tool that Allah has granted, then this power has also been given to animals." He said, "How so?" You said, "Look at the animals, they also distinguish between good and bad. You have them... first, keep them hungry. In front of a hungry animal, put stale fodder. It will definitely eat it. And a little way off from it, put fresh fodder. It will leave the stale fodder and go eat the fresh fodder. So it becomes known that it distinguishes between good and bad." So he started to say, "Imam, I am defeated. And you yourself please grant me the favor, what is intellect called?" You said, "Look, this is the power of distinction, which has been given to animals. And man has been given intellect. This is a substance, this is a substance from there. This is the substance, the substance of the intellect, and its meaning is this: to distinguish between two good things and to distinguish between two bad things, this is the job given to man. That he should distinguish between two good things and take the better good and leave the lesser good, and leave the greater evil and take the lesser evil. For example, if a lion is coming in the jungle and you are also there, then it is better to fall into a well than to be torn apart by a lion. At least there is some chance of survival. The use of intellect will remain. So it's like that: to take the lesser of two evils and the greater of two goods is the job of man." He started to say, "Mawla, your place is empty." So anyway, there are many such debates, many such discussions, which... not everyone understands them. Not everyone has these things. Anyway, the Imam took him to task and explained to him. So that was the subtle substance, from the world of intellect, granted, which needed to be understood, and he did not understand it. And taking that same thing, those who did, they wandered in the valleys of opinion and analogy. The whole world is wandering, they themselves are wandering, and stacks upon stacks of commentaries have been written, and don't even ask what the condition is. Their own lives are ruined, and the lives of others are also ruined. The commentator Tabir Saaheb wrote so much commentary, so much commentary, that in the end, even the animal's back broke. It was loaded onto it, and that animal also perished. An animal like a camel. Now, God knows if this is a correct tradition or a wrong tradition, but there seems to be some truth to it in this sense, that there are so many books that no one can even take up the task of reading them. The scholars finally said, all of them agreed and said, "Brother, this disaster that Tabir has caused, writing so many books, that like Baha'ullah, who wrote 200 tablets and created a problem, who will read this? Who will read this commentary?" So they coined a saying for Kabir, the scholars of Islam. And what was that saying, you know? *Kullun fi Kabeer illa 'l-tafseer* (Everything is in Kabeer except the commentary). In Kabir, there is everything, but there is no commentary. There you go. *Kullun fi Kabeer illa 'l-tafseer*. Did you see? This is the commentary. So I was saying that this is the substance of the world of creation. And this, which Allah has granted, is His bounty, it is His mercy. But what work was to be done with it? The only work to be done with it was to try to understand the teachings of the Messenger of Allah, that is, whichever Prophet of the time it is, whichever God has sent, the one to whom He has given the responsibility of conveying the message. This is the function of the intellect. If you separate the intellect and work with it, you cannot. You will have to work with the intellect along with the coming messenger. You will have to work with both messengers. Until you combine both these messengers, you cannot get guidance. So anyway, I was saying that these two were the substances that were given to man here. Now, there was another thing I needed to tell about there. The physical world is still not coming up, I want it to come quickly, but the physical world is not coming. The point was that there, when we were falling... when we were falling, at the time of falling, we had made various intentions. I mentioned this. So you have heard that intentions must have been made. Now, one doesn't understand how that intention would have been made. Now, that we... we go and settle in Kuwait, and we will eat this, drink this, do this profession, do that... do such and such work. All these kinds of intentions were made. And according to those intentions, we are getting the fruit, we are getting this and that. But what was the reality? Along with these intentions, as I had given you a clue, a special point, that special point was that the *shaaq-i mutahhir* were also attached to your side, and the *musirr-o mustakbir* were right there. Why? We all fell together. At the time of falling, we all fell together, from there. The whole group fell. The *naadim* also fell, the *musirr-o mustakbir* also fell, the *shaaq-i mutahhir* also fell. They had 35 types, they had 20 types, we had 15 types—leave those types aside, but everyone fell. And in the state of falling, what happened? They became jumbled up. Some are meeting with the *shaaq-i mutahhir*, some with the *musirr-o mustakbir*, someone's... is meeting with someone else, someone's head with someone's feet, someone's feet with someone's head. Anyway, in various ways, we had gotten mixed up. When we were mixed up, then there, our gazes, with each other, had created a strange state. We had created some relationships, some situations. These situations and relationships that we created, those situations of creating, those relationships are described in three words. And what are those three words? One is *maylaan*, the first is *istehsaan*, the second is *maylaan*, the third is *qisaas*. What is the first thing? *Istehsaan*, meaning to consider good. The fact of the matter was what? We were very good. That is, we were *naadim*. Now, there, we are sitting with the *shaaq-i mutahhir*. The effect of company... *by the company he keeps*. The effect of company comes. The effect of company. So how did we accept that effect of company? There, we accepted the effect of company in such a way that we created *istehsaan*. What is *istehsaan* called? And we also created *maylaan*, we also created *qisaas*. See, these are different terms. The first is *istehsaan*. The meaning of *istehsaan* is to consider a bad deed good. One person is doing a bad deed... "He's doing such a good job." Hey, you understand that this is a bad deed, but you are praising it. "What a good job he's doing." So this is called *istehsaan*. And *maylaan* is called, that when a person is doing a bad deed, you assist them. "He's doing such a bad deed, let me help in this." To help in it. And *qisaas* is called when you yourself do that bad deed. Did you understand? The first is *istehsaan*. *Istehsaan* means to consider a bad deed good. The second is *maylaan*, meaning to participate in it. And the third is *qisaas*, meaning you yourself do that bad deed. *Istehsaan*... meaning to consider a bad deed good. For example... for example, what thing? Brokering (*dallaali*). Now, brokering also happens in good things, but I am taking it in a bad sense because a famous saying is *koyle ki dallaali mein haath kaale hote hain* (In the brokerage of coal, the hands get black). So now what are you? You are... you are looking at it with a good eye. There will be many examples. Now that I have given you the hint of brokering, you can find many things from it. Figure it out for yourself. I don't need to give examples. So *istehsaan* is this. And what is *maylaan*? *Maylaan*... meaning you participate in it. Participation. And what is participation? For example, false testimony. What is false testimony? To be a witness, a false witness. Which the Master of the Universe, Amir al-Mu'minin, has counted as a major sin. So what is false testimony? You are participating in it. If, suppose, the murderer has committed murder, and you give false testimony against him that he has not committed the murder at all. So it is as if you have participated in his deed. You have participated. Do you understand? And *qisaas* is that you have done that deed yourself, and that deed will be done to you. The price of murder is murder, the price of everything is a price, and the price will be paid. As you sow, so shall you reap. How is Allah? As you are, so is He. So this will happen. So it becomes known that these three things... now where did we create these three things? When we were falling from the world of pre-existence (*'alam-i azal*). When we were falling from the world of pre-existence, there we also did *maylaan*, we did *istehsaan*, and we did *qisaas*. With whom did we do it the most? The one who is a neighbor, our dealings with them become very numerous. If they are sick, then here we play the radio very loud so that they can get proper sleep. Or if they are sick, then we do something else. Now, this rivalry flares up and such things happen. So this... our dealings were more with the *shaaq-i mutahhir*. They were less with the *musirr-o mustakbir*. But for whoever it was happening, it also happened with the *musirr-o mustakbir*. But this happened more with the *shaaq-i mutahhir*. And when it happened with the *shaaq-i mutahhir*, now what will happen? There will be adopted brothers, everything will happen, they will become brothers, they will become sisters, all sorts of things will happen, and everything will happen. What will be the state? You will be feeding them with your own hands, making morsels. Now where has this love come from? You have brought it with you after making that intention from the world of pre-existence. So what you did there, its impression will sit here. So this *maylaan*, *istehsaan*, and *qisaas*, these states, we created them right there. So this... all these things, at the time of falling, we were doing all this. And at the time of falling, we... as I said, there are some such factors, we created them, because of which homeland, clothing, form... so this... all these things, at the time of falling, we were doing all this. And at the time of falling, we... as I said, there are some such factors, we created them, because of which homeland, clothing, form, circumstances, our appearance, children, parents, wife, relationships, connections, all worldly things, work, business, profession—the links for all these things were created right there. All... Now you will say, which factors were at play? If we were to know, we would be ready to correct everything right now. There is no question of correcting now. At that time, you were given the full opportunity to correct, but you did not correct at all. Now, whatever you have done... *az-maast ke bar-maast* (what is from us is upon us). What grace may Allah show? What is our poverty? What is our affliction? What is our illness? All of this is our own doing. *Maa kasabat aydeekum* (what your hands have earned). Allah Ta'aala says, *maa asaabakum min museebatin illa bimaa kasabat aydeekum* (No misfortune befalls you except by what your hands have earned). No misfortune will befall you except that which your hands have earned. Whatever your hands have earned, Allah is just a caretaker. He is just the one who delivers. How is Allah? As you are, so is He. You did it, that is why the Lord of the worlds says, *laysa bi-zallaamin li 'l-'abeed* (He is not at all unjust to the servants). Allah is not one who is unjust to His servants. Beware, do not think this, that Allah is not unjust. Allah is not unjust, He is never one to be unjust. So it becomes known that all these things, we did them there. And now, in this state, the condition that we are in, that state—when we have made intentions, we have repented in various ways, the *shaaq-i mutahhir* have become *shaaq-i mutahhir*, the *musirr-o mustakbir* have become *musirr-o mustakbir*, and the three groups have become jumbled up with each other—so the primordial matter (*hayoola-yi oola*), when they fell, length, breadth, and depth came into being. That state, and this state, there is a big difference. This is called the second matter (*hayoola-yi saaniya*). This is called *hayoola-yi saaniya*. This *hayoola-yi saaniya*, upon which length, breadth, and depth have come, now what is the Divine Power doing to it? It is punishing this. It is punishing this, and to give this punishment, what happened? This was removed and it was said, "You... now this whole group, whether it be the *naadim*, or the *musirr-o mustakbir*, or the *shaaq-i mutahhir*, you are not fit to live here." "You are not fit to live in this spiritual world. Go. Fall from here. *Ihbitoo*." The Quran says, "*Ihbitoo*," fall. Fall, you. And now you are not fit for this spiritual world because evil has been created in you, a flaw has come into you. You are not fit to live in this spiritual world. And you, go from here. Now, when we were removed, after being removed, when the physical world is about to be formed, so how was it formed? It was formed from us. It was made from us, everything. So they say, don't they, that *kooza-gar o wa kooza gil o khud gil-i kooza* (The potter and the clay of the pot and the clay of the pot itself). Meaning, everything is of clay, and the one who makes it is also of clay. The potter is also made of clay, and what he is making, he is also making from clay. In the same way, the entire universe that was made, it was made from this. Now how was it made, I will begin that. It... entirely, that how Allah Ta'aala formed it. Who is Allah? The last individual of the realm of *labbu nidaa'*, whom we call the *aashir-i mudabbir-i hakeem*. The *aashir-i mudabbir-i hakeem*, the form that he gave to this world, how he did it, this form that you are seeing today, how he made that form, I have to tell you about it being made, how it was formed. Since a... now I am coming to the physical world, so before that, I have finished these few preliminary matters, that you should keep these few things in mind regarding the intellect, regarding the body, and regarding this soul, and the three things *naamiya*, *hissiya*, and *naatiqa*, and regarding speech, know this, that this is our Pillar of Light (*'amood-i noor*), in which that angle of ours is noted. That upon what we repented, in what capacity we accepted repentance. You might say, here I repent a lot, here I... It is not a question of repenting here. There, the repentance you did, how much you repented, that has been noted. Now how will it be here, what will it be, in the world of action, in this world, I will tell you that. But for now, you should understand that at the time of falling from there, whatever you did, you are getting that here. So Allah is *laysa bi-zallaamin li 'l-'abeed*. He is not unjust to any servant. You will say, "The Lord of the worlds has given me everything. Allah has done everything, just if my height were a little... a little longer, it would have been very good." And those who are a full seven feet tall, they say, "If my height were a little shorter, it would have been very good." Someone is complaining about their color, someone about their height, someone fat is complaining about being lean, someone... about worldly things. Anyway, someone about health, someone about illness, on some thing or the other, one definitely weeps in this world, that "I wish I had obtained this thing too, I wish I had gotten this thing." So this "I wish," it never ends, this "I wish." This is what Ghalib said, "*Hazaar'on khwaahishein aisi ke har khwaahish pe dum nikle, mere nikle magar armaan lekin phir bhi kum nikle*" (Thousands of desires, such that for each desire, a life is spent; my desires were fulfilled, but the longings were still too few). So these desires do not end. For this, our *du'at* have given a very profound example. Now listen to that desire as well. They say that our desires never end. If our desire was, "Let us see our children get married," that is one... "Just one desire is left, what can I say? My children's marriage." "Okay, fine." The marriage is seen. Now after that, "Now what? Now you should depart." "It's done now, the marriage has been seen." "Now what is it?" "No, just if the children's children are born," this is a desire. Okay. Now their children also get married. "Okay, let's see that too." So the desires, they are a continuous chain, a series that is attached and never ends. So, to describe this state in this world, that desires do not end, a wise man explained it so well. They said, "Look, there are three very strange things in the world. One is gold. The moment the word 'gold' is uttered, the tongue starts to smack its lips. Ah, gold..." Gold is gold. But a person says, "How shiny this metal is, and what a beautiful thing it is. And it is a very radiant thing, a very shiny thing. How... gold is gold. But I wish it had some fragrance, it would have been very good." "I wish it had some fragrance, how good it would have been." Now he sees the flower of sandalwood. Sandalwood flowers... that "how fragrant they are, this is a sandalwood flower." "Hey, these are sandalwood flowers. If sandalwood had a fruit, what would it be like!" Or that... I don't know if they have flowers or not, but if they had flowers, what kind of flowers would they be and what would its fruit be like? Meaning, if the wood of sandalwood has so much fragrance, then what would its fruit and flower not have? In the same way, a person says that... that sugarcane (*ganna*, *nay-shakar*), he sees the sugarcane and says, "What... what has Allah created! That there is so much sugar in its stem. If it had a fruit, what would it be like?" If there is so much sugar in the stem, if it had a fruit, what would it be like? So it becomes known that a person's desire is never fulfilled. His desires are never completed. His desires will always continue. So this is a custom, an incident of the world. What can you and I do about it? These desires of ours do not end. So why do they not end in this world? It is because for us, it is a punishing form. In this confinement, this thing has been imposed on you, that your mind will always be working like this. This thing is done, now this thing should be done. One house is built, no, a second house should also be built. A second house is built, a third house should also be built. One car comes, no, a second car. This is maroon color, a blue colored one should also come. There you go. Okay, this desire. So in the same way, desires never end. So this continuity is there, and in the same way, our states continue to be, and our desires are never fulfilled. So the *aashir-i mudabbir-i hakeem*, the greatest punishment that he gave us... the *'aql-i awwal*... I am finishing... that *'aql-i awwal*, the punishment it gave, what was that punishment? That it trapped us in time and space (*zamaan-o makaan*). It trapped us in time and space. What is time called? Time (*waqt*). The revolution of the sun and moon. And what is space called? The place where you take support. The support you have taken, that has become space. And the revolution of the sun and moon is called time.

<!-- AUG:hazrat-zia lecture 10 -->

...that there in the `alam-i arwah` (world of spirits), from which we have come to the `jismani `alam` (physical world), the thing we have received is, first, `jan` (life). Which was granted to us in the form of `namiyah` (vegetative) and `hissiyyah` (sensory) faculties. And the second thing is `aql` (intellect), which is a `latif jauhar` (subtle essence) that has been bestowed upon us, and here we are. But, along with that, I had also told you that in this `alam-i jismani` (physical world), the punishment we were given for leaving that world, what is that punishment? It is to be imprisoned in `zaman-o makan` (time and space). `Zaman-o makan` (time and space) itself is a punishment. It is such a great punishment that you cannot even imagine it. `Tajassum` (corporeality), `jism` (the body), is a very great punishment. And that body... no one can ever imagine the extent of its `jismaniyyat` (physicality). Many things come before you appearing `latif` (subtle), but they are extremely `mujassam` (corporeal). And so many things that appear to you as extremely `mujassam` are actually very `latif`. Do you understand? For example, there is water. It has a lot of `kasafat` (density), but it looks `latif` to you. Whereas you think of a mountain as having a lot of `kasifat` (density). It has such great `kasafat`. But the `kasafat` of a mountain is nothing at all. And that thing which has been forbidden, which has been made `haram` (unlawful) to drink, even to utter its name is forbidden. It is that `haram`. So, that thing is of `intehayi kasafat` (extreme density). So it means that the `kasafat` of a mountain is many times less than the `kasafat` of that water. So, our sight cannot differentiate equally between this `kasafat` (density) and `latafat` (subtlety). It cannot separate them. So it is very difficult to separate it. But you see, where will we count `kasafat`? We will count `kasafat` as a `jismani` (physical) thing that has come over us; this is `kasafat`. And... but the reality is that the greatest `kasafat` is found where? In minerals (`mirrors`), in `madhan` (minerals). And less than that is in `nabat` (plants). And less than that is in `haywan` (animals). And less than that is in `insan` (humans). That is `kasafat`. And many things will appear to you as shining and glittering, like `jawahirat` (jewels) and so on, so you will say, "Oh, such shiny, glittering things, how `latif` (subtle) they are." Whereas they possess the most `kasafat` of all. There are more veils (`parde`) there. So, you cannot separate `kasafat` and `latafat` with your external sight. Our sight is deceived. It is for this reason that `Qudrat` (Nature/God) did what? Since we could not judge anything, it kept `halal` and `haram` in its own hands. The system of `halal` and `haram` was kept by `Qudrat` in its own hands, and they came and told us, "Look, wear this, don't wear this. Eat this, don't eat this. Drink this, don't drink this. Do it this way, don't do it that way." All these "yeses" and "nos," the commands (`awamir`) and prohibitions (`nawahi`) that kept coming from the prophets, came for this very reason: that we know nothing. Anyway, when the time comes for the discussion of `tadbir` and `taqdir` (providence and predestination) and many things related to it, then all these matters will be further clarified and explained. For now, I was explaining to you that when we fell from there, from the `alam-i latafat` (world of subtlety), and got stuck in this world, then what are the things we have been put into? The prison (`qayd`), the `qayd-o band` (imprisonment), the greatest of all, what is that prison? That of `zaman-o makan` (time and space). It is the prison of `zaman-o makan`. You have come and gotten stuck in this prison of `zaman-o makan`. There, there was neither time nor space. You were in a state of `latafat`. And you cannot even conceive of such a thing from here, that if we remove time and we remove space, you cannot even imagine it. It is for this reason that the Noble Prophet had said that *ma la `aynun ra'at wa la uzunun sami`at wa la khatara `ala qalbi bashar* (what no eye has seen, nor ear has heard, nor has it occurred to the heart of a man). Jannah (Paradise) is that place which has not crossed our hearts, meaning it has not come to our hearts, what Jannah is. And neither our ears have heard it, nor our eyes have seen it. So that thing is called Jannah. So it means, what is Jannah in reality? It is the name for going into the `ruhani `alam` (spiritual world). This Jannah is not those gardens (`baghat`) that are mentioned. Now, why did the Quran Sharif mention it like that? Well, insha'Allah, those details will come aplenty. But the point to be made is that reaching the `ruhani `alam` is the greatest thing of all. There is a couplet by Hazrat Maulana Shakir Sahab that, "Give such strength to my wings that I may reach my nest. A long time has passed since our nest was left behind by us." What a fine couplet he has stated, Maulana has, that "A long time has passed since our nest was left behind by us." You are wishing that, "I wish we would gain that strength, that `ruhaniyyat` (spirituality), due to which we could go to that pinnacle, reach that `'arsh` (throne)." So that arrival will happen when? When you leave `jismaniyyat` (physicality). So to leave `jismaniyyat` and adopt `latafat` (subtlety), to adopt that `ruhaniyyat`, you will think that from here you should go on a diet, or do this or that, or do something else, and you will become `latif`. No. You can become `latif` only by one formula: by acting upon the `shari'at`. You observe fasts, give `zakat`. Give `zakat`, perform `hajj`, do `taharat` (purification), do `wilayat` (allegiance). Do all these things, and along with doing all of them, also do the `wilayat` of Amir al-Mu'minin, because that is the soul of it all. Only then will you be capable of going to that `ruhani `alam`, otherwise not. So it means that this is a very formidable `kasafat`. To be free from this `kasafat`, we will have to pass through many stages. The `transformation` that will happen for us, from `maddiyyat` (materiality) to `ruhaniyyat` (spirituality), cannot happen without the `shari'at-i ghara'` (the resplendent Shari'ah). It cannot happen except by adhering to the `shari'at`. And you may adhere to the `shari'at` a million times... for example, a person... a person brings books to his home, say he wants to do his `matric`, or wants to do an `M.A.`, or a `PhD`. So all the things that are in his `course`, he brings them all home and is studying and working very hard, and after that, when he goes to take the exam, he will not be allowed to enter the exam hall. Why? They will say, "Sir, how have you come? Did you register? Do you have a `registration`?" They will ask this. So it means that `registration` in an `institution` is necessary. If you don't have a `registration` in the `institution`, you will not be allowed to enter. But a person who has not studied at all, if he comes and has a `registration`, he will be able to enter. But you, being so educated, will not be granted entry. It is just like that. The `'ahd Imam al-Zaman` (covenant with the Imam of the Time) is an extremely necessary thing. If you have performed all actions after taking the `'ahd`, then all your actions are `maqbul` (accepted), they are all `valid`, and your going is possible. And if you have not taken the `'ahd`, then nothing of yours will be of consequence. So, absolutely, this is the only way to get out of these `kasafats`. For now, I am telling you, how did these `kasafats` come about in the first place, and how did we fall from the `alam-i ruhani` into `kasafat`? This is the very discourse that is beginning today. So the point was that in the `alam-i ruhani`, a level was established which I had told you about yesterday, `kal-lumum`. And `kal-lumum` had invited us, and we accepted the invitation only when the command of `ehbitu` (descend!) had already been given to us. The command of `ehbitu`, to fall, had been given. The `punishment` had arrived. And after it was enforced, we had repented. And while falling, we felt `nadamah` (regret) and said that we repent, we become remorseful. But along with us, what was there? There were also the `shak wa mutar` (doubters and waverers), and the `musirr wa mustakbir` (insistent and arrogant ones), those who persisted (`israr`) and were arrogant (`takabbur`). These three... we were all mixed together. We had all joined hands, we were all mixed up, and the entire group had to fall. But Allah Ta'ala said this... a message came from `'Ashir`, and the entire `firqah` (group) of `kal-lumum`—it was a full `teamwork` effort—they said that you will fall, but we will first... *summa nunajji 'llazina 'ttaqaw wa nazharu 'zzalimina fiha jasiyya* (Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, kneeling). That we... those in this world who are pious, meaning those who believe, who perform good deeds, who are going to change themselves, who are going towards `ruhaniyyat`, we will save them. But those who are `zalim` (wrongdoers), meaning those who practice `ghayr-i 'adl` (injustice), who place things in their improper place—*waz`u 'sh-shay' `ala ghayr-i mahallihi*—we will leave them in this world. So this was Allah Ta'ala's promise. So now, we have to see that our world, in which we are all mixed together, the Lord of the worlds commanded it: *ihbitu ba'dukum li-ba'din `aduww* (descend, being enemies to one another). The Quran is saying this. *ihbitu ba'dukum li-ba'din `aduww* (descend, being enemies to one another), *mustaqarrun wa mustawda'un ila hin* (a dwelling place and a provision for a time). This is a verse of the Quran Majeed. That you should descend, and descend as enemies to one another. Are you seeing? *ba'dukum li-ba'din `aduww* (enemies to one another), and you will be enemies to each other. Enemies how? Like fire and water. What is the situation today? What is the situation of the `musirr wa mustakbir`? They are at odds with the `shak wa mutar`. What is the situation of the `shak wa mutar`? They are at odds with us. So why did this opposition of temperaments happen? It was born right there. And the Prophet... this very verse that the Lord of the worlds is stating, what did you say in its commentary, O Noble Prophet? You said that "the souls are gathered armies" —*arwahun mujannada*— that were created there in the `alam-i ruhani`. They were an innumerable army that Allah Ta'ala had created. *arwahun mujannada, man i'talafa i'talafa wa man i'tanafa i'tanafa* (gathered souls, those who were familiar [there] are familiar [here], and those who were averse [there] are averse [here]). They were innumerable souls. Those who loved each other there, loved each other; those who were enemies, were enemies. So what is the situation now? How will we explain that enmity and love here? If you meet a person, you see that upon meeting, what happens? Your heart feels strangely drawn. You say, "I don't understand, I'm so drawn to him," and that person is also so inclined towards me that we have formed a very deep friendship. How did this friendship happen? You live so far apart, but how did you become friends? This is a matter from there. Because you were joined there, you will be joined here too. And what is the situation? And if there is hatred, what is it like? That they are full brothers, brother and sister, everything is there, but despite that, there is `bugz li 'llah` (hatred for the sake of Allah). In technical terms, what do they call it? `bugz li 'llah`. Just by seeing their face, you feel aversion and displeasure starts to arise. You say, "May God not show them to me. It's better if they stay away." So why do they become `abusan qamtarira` (scowling and grim)? It happens because of that. So all these... it was at this juncture, at this stage, that the Noble Prophet, may peace and blessings be upon him, was stating and explaining, "Look, this is the matter of the souls there. Whatever you did there, you have done. The love you made there, you made; the enmity you made there, you made." Anyway, this was the condition, and Allah Ta'ala said that you have become enemies to each other. You will say, "How can Allah be like that?" The enmity was done by us. How is Allah? As you are, so is He. Whatever we did there, `Qudrat` is nurturing it, explaining it, and managing it in the same way. That it's a good thing, the way you want it, God will want it in the same way. There will be no change in it. If you want to remain `musirr wa mustakbir` (insistent and arrogant), so be it. If you want to remain `shak wa mutar` (doubting and wavering), so be it. If you are going as `nadim` (repentant), that's a good thing. You are repenting, so We have sent messengers to save you. Messengers will come, they will guide, and they will take you away. Now, when the mention of the messengers comes and the mention of the `da'wah` (call) comes here, I will explain in detail what their real purpose of coming is. What is the reason for sending the messengers? We just think it's to give guidance. What is the meaning of guidance? Couldn't you have received guidance? We don't go into the depths. Insha'Allah, those things will come. Why were the messengers sent? Why did the divine books come? What was the reason? All those things will come. For now, I was saying that when Allah Ta'ala gave the command of `ehbitu... ba'dukum li-ba'din `aduww* (descend... as enemies to one another), at that time, the state was that we were all mixed together. So which groups? `Nadim` (repentant), `mutar` (doubter), and `musirr wa mustakbir` (insistent and arrogant). These three were mixed together. These three groups that were mixed, their form was of this kind. Meaning, this which is formed, this is called `hayula` (prime matter), and this form that is visible is called `surah` (form). They were in the form of `hayula` and `surah`. It is obvious that now, since it took a shape... until now it had no shape, but now a shape came, as the three dimensions came: `tul`, `'arz`, and `'umq` (length, breadth, and depth) came, so it took a shape. And this... in our terminology, they say that the `surah` (form) is called `hissiyyah` (sensory), and the `jism` (body) is called `namiyah` (vegetative). `Namiyah` and `hissiyyah` are the names for `surah` and `hayula`. And there are books on this. There are books on `hayula` and `surah`. I am just mentioning it briefly to you because these are very philosophical discussions (`falsafiyanah bahs`). For now, I am explaining `hayula` and `surah` to you in such a way that you can understand it well. That this lot that was formed, of the `musirr wa mustakbir`, `shak wa mutar`, and `nadim mustagfir`, this entire lot had the form of `hayula` and `surah`, and it was `hayula-i saniyah` (the second matter) which had taken on a form. And that is what is called `namiyah` and `hissiyyah`. And Allah Ta'ala is commanding this lot, that *ehbitu ba'dukum li-ba'din `aduww* (descend, as enemies to one another). Now you fall, and now you go in a state of enmity towards each other, go, into this world. So as soon as the command to fall was given to that lot, now that... that entire part began to come. `Tanazzul` (descent) began from there. You will say that it was coming from up to down. So, indeed, that was the case. It was coming from up to down. They call it `tanazzul`. It is not that every `tanazzul` is of coming from up to down, but the `ruhani `alam` (spiritual world) is above. So the `ruhani `alam`... from it, the `jismani `alam` is below, and `kasafat` comes below, and this came below. But how far below did it come? What did it come to? If you sit there and measure it, there is no measure, there is no `kasafat`. That is a `latif` world. What can you say about that `latif` world? It was removed from there, and after being removed, this `hayula` that was there, `hayula` and `surah`, this entire block that was... which consists of the `shak wa mutar` and `nadim mustagfir` and `musirr wa mustakbir`, this whole thing came downwards. And after coming, `Qudrat` willed for a time that it should go down, and after going down, it stopped it. Now, `Qudrat` stopped it. You might say, "Well, it was Allah's `Qudrat` (power) that wanted it, and as it wants, `Qudrat` does as it wants." But now what is it? In the `jismani `alam`, `Qudrat` will never act directly. Remember this. Without means (`asbab`), `Qudrat` will never act. Meaning, this is the `dar-i asbab` (abode of means). Here, a cause (`sabab`) will be formed. So much so that the belief of common Muslims that a miracle (`mo'jizah`) is a miracle, not a single such miracle has happened. Not a single miracle, in the sense that Muslims understand it, has happened. It was only a feat (`karamat`) of sight. It was appearing to our eyes. Neither the sun turned back, nor the moon split, nor did anything happen. In the world, not a single miracle... indeed, the thousands of miracles that the prophets showed, they all happened, but how did they happen? As things visible to the eyes. But in reality, had they changed their form (`qalib`)? Or had the sun changed? Or had such and such happened? Nothing. It is for this very reason that this thing does not happen, but is visible to the eyes. What will `Qudrat` do here? It is the `dar-i asbab`. Here, if our cause (`sabab`) is hot, there will be heat; if it is cold, there will be cold. It is the `dar-i asbab`, and in the `dar-i asbab`, all these things will happen. The prayer we make to Allah Ta'ala is only this: that our means (`asbab`) be changed, our means be altered. So, in the `dar-i asbab`, everything will happen by a cause. Without a cause (`cause`), without a `sabab`, nothing is going to happen here, in this world. So now, when this `hayula` fell, `Qudrat` stopped it, and it stopped it through them. Now, what is it? For example, understand that if in the community here, I see that we are having a confrontation with someone, God forbid there is a fight, then we will take such young men who are well-built, who are like good wrestlers, we will call them and say, "Please come and help, such and such a thing is happening." Why, sir? Today you are not looking for highly educated people, but such people? So if such a matter arises, then it will be like that. If it is an intellectual matter, we will choose scholars from among them. If some other matter arises, we will choose some other people. So for every aspect, a selection is made. For every aspect, a selection is made. For whichever aspect it is created, for that aspect it is chosen. So now what happened here? `Qudrat`, on that falling group, that entire block that was falling, in it, `Qudrat`'s sight was on a few people, and through them, `Qudrat` saw that they are such, whether they are `musirr wa mustakbir`, or `shak wa mutar`, or `nadim mustagfir`. They can be in any of them. Do you understand? It is a technical (`fanni`) matter. So, from a technical perspective, there were some powers, there were some among those falling, whom `Qudrat` entrusted with this task, that you should stand firm in your place and stop. So they became firm in exactly the same way as pegs (`mekhein`) are. To pitch a tent, there is a peg, and the tent is pitched with the help of the peg. In exactly the same way, like a peg, they stopped that `hayula`, and there were four pegs. It was through these four pegs that this entire `hayula` was stopped. Their names are Ghalib, 'Ashir, Rabi', and Talib. Talib, 'Ashir, Rabi', Ghalib. These are four powers (`quwwatein`), and these are the names of the four powers. And these are four powers that, like nails, like pegs, they caught hold of it and controlled it, and this `hayula`, this `hayula` and `surah`, stopped at one place. When it stopped, `Qudrat` began to give it shape. That to it... in it, whatever had fallen, this falling group, in this group, `Qudrat` had already made an arrangement from the beginning, that he who is high is high. Meaning, the one who repents, the one who repents, the one who repents the most, is always like cream on top. No matter how much you churn, the froth comes on top. So that cream was on top. And it was on top. Through that cream, what did `Qudrat` do? It gave it rotation (`gardish`). This `hayula`, `hayula` and `surah`, it gave it rotation through that cream, which is the leaven of `nadamah` (regret). From the leaven of `nadamah`, it gave this rotation, and that entire `hayula` and `surah` went into rotation and began to spin. And its spinning was just like if we take an onion and pierce it with a skewer and spin it very fast. In exactly the same way, this entire `hayula` and `surah` were spinning. And they were spinning on whose weight? From the top surface. The top surface, which was `awwal al-nawadim` (the first of the repentant), it was the leaven of the most `nadamah`. And through it, `Qudrat` made everything spin. As soon as they spun, what happened? `Qudrat`, since it now wanted a workshop (`karkhanah`) to be made, a prison (`qayd-khanah`) to be made, and in it there should be some prisoners, and some wardens for the prison. So all these things, the prison, the requisites of the prison, and the wardens of the prison, and whatever else there is, who will all these be? They will be from among them. `khud kuzah gar o khud gil-i kuzah` (He is the potter and the clay of the pot Himself). Meaning, everything will be from among them. The prisoner is the same, the prison is the same, living is the same, eating is the same, and their comforts are the same, and the punishment is also the same. All things, all provisions, are also the same. So there is no difference in anything, it is all the same thing. The wall and this and that, the house and the mountain and the tree, all these things, what are they? They are all one. They are spirits (`ashbah`) that have taken on different forms. So this entire `hayula`, when it fell from there, now this upper part, when it started spinning... this leaven of `nadamah` that was there, when it started spinning, it made the lower parts spin too. And when it started spinning, this uppermost part, it is obviously a sphere. So the entire upper part, this which is, it is called `falak-i muhit` (the encompassing sphere). It is called `falak-i muhit`, it is called `atlas`, it is called `bab `alam al-quds` (the gate of the world of holiness). Do you understand? `Atlas` is the name of a cloth which has no embroidery (`bel buta`). You know `atlas`, you must have seen it, that it has no embroidery. That's why it's named `atlas`. And it is also called `basit`. It is also called `muhit`, and also `basit`, and also `atlas`. It is called `muhit` because it encompasses everything. It is called `basit` because it is completely transparent, there is no obstructing thing in it. And it is called `atlas` because it has no embroidery-like pattern. So it was given various names in various ways. And it is called `bab `alam al-quds` because if you enter from there, where will you go? You will go towards `kal-lumum`. If you take a step towards the `alam-i ruhani`. So it means that this is the most `basit` (vast/simple) part, and this `muhit` spun the lower part. Now `Qudrat` wanted... `Qudrat` wanted, the way it wanted, it is making it. Just like a potter takes clay and gives it the shape he wants. Now, in the same way, why? Because you... just as to give an animal an injection or to operate on it, you first restrain it with a sliding door. First you tie it down. After tying it down, you can give it an injection or whatever. Otherwise, if you go to give an injection to a lion, it's not a small matter. So in the same way, first we were tied down. And after being tied down, all this was done in this manner. When it was tied down, now `Qudrat` is giving it shapes. So as soon as they spun, the upper part, along with its spinning, the lower part also started to spin. And the lower part that spun, and the part below it also spun. But what happened was that if the upper part was spinning in this way, then the part below it was spinning in this way. And the part below that was spinning in this way, in the opposite... in the opposite direction it spun. In the opposite direction it began to spin. So when the upper part spun, the part below it that spun, the part below the `falak-i muhit` that spun, that was called `falak-i buruj` (the sphere of constellations). And the part below the `falak-i buruj` that spun, that was called `zuhal` (Saturn). `Falak-i zuhal` (the sphere of Saturn). The part below the `falak-i zuhal` that spun in this way, that was called `falak-i mushtari` (the sphere of Jupiter). And the part below it that spun, that was called `falak-i mirrikh` (the sphere of Mars). The part below it that spun, that was called `falak-i shams` (the sphere of the Sun). Below that, `zuhrah` (Venus), `utarid` (Mercury), and `qamar` (Moon). In the way it spun, it was called `falak-i mushtari`. And the part below it that spun, it was called `falak-i mirrikh`. The part below it that spun, it was called `falak-i shams`. Below that, `zuhrah`, `utarid`, and `qamar`. It means that these are the seven `kaukab` (planets), the seven planets have seven `falak` (spheres), and these are its suspended spheres, and all these planets are revolving in their own spheres. Now, `Qudrat` wanted it to be this way, so the upper part, as soon as it spun, its... just as the layers of an onion are separate, in the same way, these were breaking off, they were becoming separate. So the first part that happened, I told you, was the `falak-i muhit`, which encompasses everything. And inside it, the first part that separated, it is called `falak-i buruj` (the sphere of constellations). Now why `falak-i buruj`? I will tell you, insha'Allah. And the part below the `falak-i buruj` was `falak-i zuhal` (the sphere of Saturn). In this, there is only one `kaukab` (planet), and that planet is revolving, and the name of that planet is `zuhal` (Saturn). Below Saturn was Jupiter, below Jupiter was Mars, below Mars was the Sun, below the Sun were Venus, Mercury, and the Moon. These seven stars, seven spheres, are revolving, and on the seven spheres, the `falak-i buruj` is the eighth sphere, and above the eighth, the highest sphere is which one? `Falak-i muhit`. `Falak-i muhit`, I said, is `falak-i basit` (the vast/simple sphere), and it is `atlas`, and there is no star or anything there. It is a completely ethereal quality. And it is completely a `basit` quality. Now below it is the `falak-i buruj`. What is `falak-i buruj`? It is such a sphere in which all the stars we see are in it. All these stars are in it. It is obvious, after that the planets began. Among the planets, the first was Saturn (`zuhal`). After Saturn came Jupiter (`mushtari`), after Jupiter came Mars (`mirrikh`), after Mars came the Sun (`shams`), after the Sun came Venus (`zuhrah`), Mercury (`utarid`), and the Moon (`qamar`). These seven `sayyare` (planets) came, and `sayyare` are those which move. And `sitare` (stars) are those which are fixed in their place, they do not move, from their place... that's why they are called `sawabit` (the fixed ones). These are `sawabit`, and these are `sayyare`. There is a big difference between the two. Now, this which was `falak-i buruj` became the second sphere. The third sphere is Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon. Why did Allah Ta'ala establish this order? I will explain that a little. The matter is actually this, that... if you see, the seven... first the spheres were formed. On the seven spheres, the eighth sphere was `falak-i buruj`. And on `falak-i buruj` was `falak-i muhit`. This is the matter of nine, which is why a child's birth takes nine months. Otherwise, the completion (`takmil`) of the child happens in seven months. In seven months, the child is alive and is completed. And these seven planets are responsible for the seven months. But this eighth and ninth, these two months that are extra, they allude to these two spheres. Okay. And the second thing is that if you... this whole arrangement... if you want to see it within this cosmos, it's possible from an intellectual perspective that you may or may not understand it, but just as Allah Ta'ala says that "We... what are you... from an extract of clay" —*salatun min tin*— "We drew you like an extract from clay." *fa-ja`alnahu fi qararin makin* (then We placed him in a firm lodging)... *fa-ja`alnahu nutfatan fi qararin makin* (then We made him a sperm-drop in a firm lodging). And We made you a `nutfah` (sperm-drop) and placed you in a secure place. *fa-ja`alnahu nutfatan `alaqatan fa-khalaqna 'l-`alaqata muzghatan fa-khalaqna 'l-muzghata `izaman fa-kasawna 'l-`izama lahman summa ansha'nahu khalqan akhar* (Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump of flesh, and We made the lump of flesh into bones, and We clothed the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation). This is a verse of the Quran Majeed. The Lord of the worlds explains seven stages of the birth of an embryo. Now tell me, look, first of all, `sulalah`. `Sulalah` means to draw out. That which is the water in the father's backbone, that is called `sulalah`. That `sulalah` is the `muhit`. And `falak-i buruj` is the `nutfah`. And the `nutfah`... the seven `aflak` (spheres), these seven spheres are `muzghah` (a lump of flesh). And `alaqah` (a clinging clot), `izam` (bones), and `lahm` (flesh) are `madhan`, `nabat`, and `haywan` (mineral, plant, and animal). And `insan` (human) is the `khalq-i akhar` (other creation). It is in this way. Okay. From another perspective, if you see, I will show you a map from another perspective. That `Qudrat` made this arrangement, that if you want to take a print (`naqsh`) of something, you first have to make a reverse print on the ring. You will make a reverse print, then you will get a correct print. If you don't take a reverse print, you will not get a correct print. So `Qudrat`, since the birth of man had to happen, for the birth of man, `Qudrat` made a reverse map. How did it make the reverse map? That first the feet come. And after that, the heart's part comes, and after that, the brain comes. The brain comes last. So this is the reverse map. So Saturn and Mars are the feet. Saturn and Mars, which are above, they are in the place of the feet. And the heart is the sun. And the moon is the brain. And the brain is the `wazir` (minister). The moon is the `wazir` of the sun. The sun is the king of the spheres. So this entire map, you see, is of a reverse man, because of which a correct man was established here. Anyway, this was a philosophical matter, but I was saying that `falak-i muhit`, `falak-i buruj`, and the spheres below it, what are they made of? `Qudrat` selected them... just as a potter has clay in his hand, and he takes the clay as he wishes and does with it, in the same way, we were caught in the hands of `Qudrat`. We were stuck. Now we are in the hands of `Qudrat`. How did `Qudrat` select? It selected in such a way that all the `nadim` (repentant ones)... listen carefully. The repentant ones, all the repentant ones... from the repentant ones, this shining world was made. The ones who fell with repentance, from those repentant ones, this `jirmani `alam` (corporeal world), this shining, glittering world was made. From `falak-i muhit` down to `falak-i shams`. All the `nadimin` (repentant ones) were spent, were used up. In what? In the making of... from `falak-i muhit` down to `falak-i qamar`. They were all finished in the making of it. This... in other words, what will we say? This is the storage of the `nadimin`. The `nadimin`... The world below the spheres is called `ummhat` (mothers). These are all called fathers, and these are called mothers. The world below is called mothers, and this is called fathers. The result of the union and marriage of this mother and father, what is it? The children are `madhan`, `nabat`, and `haywan` (mineral, plant, and animal). And a type of animal is man. Now, you have seen from top to bottom that the entire `jirmani `alam`, the shining, glittering world, all of it, is made from the `nadimin`. So the `ummhat` below, what are they made of? From the `shak wa mutar`. And who are they? `Ab wa atish, bad wa khak` (water and fire, wind and earth). Meaning, these are the four elements. First, the sphere of fire was made, after that, the sphere of air was made, then the sphere of water was made, and then the sphere of earth was made. Now, how they were made, I will tell you. But you are being told that these spheres are the `ummhat`. Now, who was spent in the `ummhat`? The `shak wa mutar`. The `shak wa mutar` were entirely spent within this. Now you see, the power and quality of `ab wa atish, bad wa khak` (water and fire, wind and earth)... what is its nature? That if a sphere of fire is made, then fire is that thing which, as you observe day and night, has flames (`shole`), `lab`, `ilhab`, `iltihab`. That is, that flaring up and that which happens... so you see the flames, there is no rest (`chain`). Just as the `shak wa mutar` has no rest, a person in doubt has no rest, so is the nature of fire. And then, what is the state of the air? It is being buffeted. And what is the quality of water? It is a flowing wave. Wavy water, and what is the quality of earth? Dust rises from it. So it means that these four things, this turbulence (`tamawwuj`) that is in them, this restlessness (`be-qarar pan`), why did it come? It came from the `shak wa mutar`. That's why Iqbal said, "Stability is only for change in time." Meaning, if anything has stability in this time, then what does it have? Change. To change, to keep changing, only this one thing has stability. So change is inherent in this world. So it means that these `ummhat` that were made, they were made from the `shak wa mutar`. Now, you see, who has been spent? The `nadimin`... from them, the entire `jirmani `alam` was made. And the `ummhat` were made from whom? From the `shak wa mutar`. Now who is left? The `musirr wa mustakbir`. `Musirr wa mustakbir`, of which there are 35 `firqas` (sects). These, which are the most numerous in number, and the most severe in their power and their denial. These `musirr wa mustakbir`, what did `Qudrat` do with them? Just as here in the dungeon, the biggest prisoner is put, and they are tied up with plenty of fetters, and are put in a dark place, in exactly the same way, `Qudrat` also decided that these who were `musirr wa mustakbir`, they were put under the feet. They were put under the feet. This earth that we see, this is the upper part of the earth. This solid (`saladi`) part of the earth, the hard part, this part and the part inside the earth, this entire part was made from whom? From the `musirr wa mustakbir`. And from the `musirr wa mustakbir`, this part was made. And now `Qudrat`'s artistry is evident, that `Qudrat` wanted this prison... this itself is a prison. This whole world, this world of water and clay (`ab-o gil`), is a prison. Although you... in this prison too... it is obvious that you may be disheartened with your life, but what happens? Man adjusts himself. In exactly the same way, we... what are we doing? Despite knowing that temperaments are very strange and so on, but we don't bring complaints to our lips. We say, "We'll take some medicine, we'll do something, but we'll adjust." So we keep adjusting ourselves. So in exactly the same way, our condition is here. And `Qudrat`... these `musirr wa mustakbir` were put under our feet. And `Qudrat` made this arrangement, that this prison is for everyone to live in, but within this prison, another prison needs to be made. Within this prison, another prison needs to be made. Just as every country has a prison, a `prison`, in the same way, this whole world should have a prison, which `Qudrat` named what in the words of the Quran? Jahannam. Jahannam. Now, ask all Muslims, "Where is Jahannam?" Amir al-Mu'minin... people came and asked during the time of the caliphs, they asked, "Maulana, tell us, where is Jahannam?" The breadth of the heavens and the earth (*Arz wa samawat wa al-arz*) is so vast, so where will this Jahannam be? He said, "Tell me this, when it is day, where is the night? And when it is night, where is the day?" Strange, strange questions the questioner asked. Anyway. So the point was that for them, there is no fixed location for Jahannam, nor any fixed location for Jannah. No fixed location at all. If you ask about Jannah, they will show it on their palm. They will tell you Jannah... this is the date palm tree, and these are fruit-laden branches, and these are `hur` and `ghilman` roaming around, and four rivers are flowing. This is the map of Jannah. This is the Jannah of the Muslims. And indeed, if the Quran has called this Jannah, then that metaphorical Jannah (`majazi jannah`), I will tell you about that too. How that will be. But that... when its time comes, it will come. For now, you must believe that the most important thing is that Jannah for us is to reach the `ruhani `alam`. This is Jannah. And to remain in the lowest part of `jismaniyyat`, to remain in this prison, what is this? This is Duzakh (Hell). And it was made a Duzakh in the true sense. Now, the state of Duzakh... it is such that this whole... I want to start explaining the state of Duzakh from this because things start from the feet, so it is better if the explanation starts with Duzakh to reach Jannah. The matter of Duzakh is this, that `Qudrat` did this, that this earth, this solid (`saladi`) earth that we have, in the inner part of this earth, Jahannam was made. But since the center (`markaz`) is the `Ka`batullah`, it... Jahannam does not come exactly perpendicular to it, but the... some part of Jannah... it is not opposite to it, but is made slightly shifted. And how big was it made? Those going to Jahannam are also many, after all. For this reason, a very big Jannah... uh, Jahannam was made. Duzakh is quite large. And it is so large that its... no calculation can be made of it, but those who can calculate have its complete dimensions. How long it is, how wide it is, what its quality is, what its temperature is, how many parts it has, how many zones (`mintaqe`) it has, how many valleys (`wadiyan`) it has, and what the names of those valleys are. By God, all this exists. But for your information, what I am telling you is this, that in it there are 70 valleys. 70 valleys. There are mountain ranges inside too. And how deep is it? This is the central core. What science calls the central core, that is in reality Jahannam. For example, this is the sphere of the world, and it is spinning. So its inside (`jauf`), its belly, and the central core, which is called the central core, in the words of science, that central core is in reality Jahannam. And science, till today, has not been able to find out about it. Till today, it has not been able to research it. It only says that it is in liquid form or in gas form. It is possible that it is gas, possible that it is liquid form. It is only this much that science has said and left it. But what is the reality? It is neither in liquid form entirely, nor... nor is it in gas form, but you will have to understand. Anyway, it has 70 valleys and it is quite vast. And the mention of this very thing, the Quran Majeed, in one surah, in one `ruku'`, Allah Ta'ala has described Jahannam completely. That *taghliyul hamim* (boiling of heated water)... the words that have come in this way, and the whole of Jahannam has been described in it. Now what is there in Jahannam? There... it is not... as we think, that if there is a spark here, then there... the real fire is there. This is actually just for explaining, for making one understand. That there... the atmosphere (`fiza`) there is a fiery atmosphere. An inciting (`bhadka denewali`) atmosphere. So inciting that there is no limit to it. No limit. Imagine that this sun, which is so hot, what do we estimate about the sun? Its heat... science has measured how much heat there is. And today, what they are saying is that its heat is decreasing. We have been saying for 1400 years that its heat will decrease. And its heat is decreasing. The sun is losing its heat. And this sun, the flames that are in it, the biggest flame that emerges from it is 200 miles long. A 200-mile-long flame is what science has seen emerging from the sun's... from the sun. And imagine, this sun, which is giving you life, which is providing heat, and is providing heat to the whole world, this sun, despite this, it is so hot and has so much of everything, but this is not Jahannam. Jahannam is much worse than this. And it is much greater than this. Its heat and its... you can't even ask. `na'uzubillah`, `na'uzubillah`, it is much more. Now, Jahannam is... how deep is it? Science has... what it has measured of this earth, has drilled it, has dug it, that is 80,000 feet. So far, science has gone 80,000 feet deep. It has not gone further than that. And this is just like pricking an orange peel with a pin. As he has written about an orange, that it is like pricking an orange peel with a pin. It has only gone that deep so far. It has not gone deeper than that. So now you tell me, how deep must it be? It has only gone 80,000 feet, and this is the central core. It is very deep. And its... there are valleys, there are different divisions, there are different qualities, and... anyway, when the detailed discussion of Jahannam comes, I will explain it then. For now, I was telling you this, that Jahannam was made from the `musirr wa mustakbir`, and they were placed in Jahannam. So anyway, the divisions that `Qudrat` made, from the `nadim wa mustagfir`, the shining, glittering world was made. The `alam-i ummhat` (world of mothers) was made from `shak wa mutar`.
