And the same process was repeated, as I have stated, that whole process, after happening, now this tashkil took place, in the same way, the a'za'-e ra'isah were formed, the sun... on it... the heart and brain worked, Zuhrah formed the distinction of male and female, and 'Utarid made its features, etc. Anyway, after all this was formed, now that which was being formed, they were all women. All of them who were being formed in the pits were women. And this man who was born, and the woman who was born from the same pit, they were brother and sister. So, the ma'mla (matter) of brother and sister, here... we... our nasl (lineage) that continues, in this too it happens that she who is the bahan (sister), it's not just a ma'mla of perspective, but there are some ma'mlat of this kind as well. There are some ma'mlat of this kind, as I have stated. Anyway, these newborns, both of them were brother and sister. This is what the Prophet, may peace be upon him, stated in his time, that the children of Janab-e Adam were being born in this way, and then they were married to each other, and after their marriage, their nasl continued, and people spread in the world. But the 'awam (common people) and the 'ulama-e Islam (scholars of Islam), how do they state it? I will tell you. The 'awam state that since Hazrat Adam was such a great nabi (prophet), so in their time... Adam, such a great, great nabi, although the lowest of nabis is Janab-e Adam. Among the nutuqa' (speakers), the lowest is Janab-e Adam. Above him, the ulu'l-'azm (of high resolve) nabi is Janab-e Nuh. Above them, the ulu'l-'azm is Janab-e Ibrahim, and after Ibrahim are Musa and 'Isa and our Prophet, may peace be upon him. But they consider Janab-e Adam so great that if it were possible for them... now, since he is buried next to Janab-e Amir al-Mu'minin in Najaf al-Ashraf... Hazrat Adam and Janab-e Nuh and Janab-e... Janab-e 'Ali, these three are buried in the same place. There is one qabr (grave) for these three. Hazrat 'Ali, Janab-e Nuh, Janab-e Adam, in one place. Otherwise, if they had their way, they would have made a qabr of one or two miles for him. So, they couldn't fulfill their hasrat (desire) on him, so where did they fulfill their hasrat? On Amma Hawwa'. The qabr of Amma Hawwa' that they made in Jeddah, its condition is such that if you visit the feet, then you have to travel by car and after traveling, you go and visit the head. So the ziyarat (visit) is of a furlong or two. I have also had the sharaf (honor) of ziyarat, and I visited in the same way. One has to visit while sitting in a car. So now what can be done? The feet are in one place, and the head is in another, and that too so far away. Now, of course, the amma (mother) of the entire universe. So Amma Hawwa', after all, how big would she be? So, anyway. Now, of Amma Hawwa'... I was saying that the 'ammatul-muslimin (general body of Muslims) and the 'ulama-e Islam, they especially write this, that they are asked, "How was the world created, and how were humans born and how did they spread?" "Oh, it's very easy. Hazrat Adam and Janab-e Hawwa', they... one jhol (birth), that is, one haml (pregnancy), that haml was so large that... the situation was that one लड़का (boy) and one लड़की (girl). In every jhol, nature had specified this. Although for the children of Adam, this is not specified. But since Janab-e Adam was the first, so for him it was specified that in their jhol, the haml, there should be one male and one female. A brother and sister. And after that, what? So the second jhol that would happen, the brother and sister of that jhol, this boy with that girl, that girl with this boy, they married them off, and in this way, the nasl started to grow. We ask, "Why didn't Janab-e Adam marry that boy with that girl?" They say, "Is there a rishta (relationship) between brother and sister?" Oh, good man, if you don't count the brother-sister rishta this way, then you are counting it that after one jhol, the second jhol is also their children. This is the Muslim, and this is their 'ilm (knowledge). So they marry one jhol with the second jhol, although this was not the case at all. There was no zikr (mention) of Adam, no zikr of Amma Hawwa', no zikr of their children. The baat (matter) was of the child of the earth and sky, of the लड़का and लड़की born from this earth. That they, who were being born from one pit, were brother and sister. They were brother and sister, and the sahib-e waqt (master of the time) who was the Qaym-rut-e A'zam at that time, whose details you will know now, they promoted this and they explained. What science now generally calls the Stone Age, and after that, civilization slowly started to begin. Anyway, it was a matter of the very beginning. They explained how humans should interact with each other. So they explained that look, a brother and sister born from one pit, they are brother and sister. They should be married to the one born from another pit, this boy with that girl, that girl with this boy. They performed the nikah, and the marriage happened, and in this way, later the nasl continued. Anyway, what I am stating is that it remained in this way, and in the entire universe, the pits that were formed, first the women... the men were formed, and the bachawa pani (leftover water) from that, on which the barishen fell, from that the women were formed. And after the birth of the women, these two, 'awrat (woman) and mard (man), both were brother and sister, and they were married to each other. But when they came out of the pit, whether it was a boy or a girl, when they came out of the pit, they needed ghiza (food), just as our child starts to cry and needs ghiza, and dudh (milk) has to be given, things have to be done. In exactly the same way, he also needed ghiza. But who was there to feed him now? This is why he is so qawi (strong), that he is equal to a four-year-old child. He was running, and he started to run, and nature has grown many fruits and flowers, and everything is present in the universe. Mewe (fruits) are present. And such mewe that do not need to be peeled. That is, it's not like oranges or such things that you have to peel. It's not like that, but rather there are mulberries, there are grapes, and such things that can be eaten without peeling. So such things are growing, and he was plucking and eating them. Such mewe that are without peels, he was plucking and eating them, and from this, he was getting ghiza, and the child of the universe was keeping himself alive in this way. But now what happened? Along with this, as time started to pass, their age started to increase. The matter of shadi-byah (marriage) happened later, of course, but along with that, they started to have this samajh-bujh (understanding) that we should make arrangements for our sardi (cold) and garmi (heat). We should protect ourselves from the sardi and in the garmi, we should go out, we should do that. So, just as the khayal (idea) of making a ghar (house) came to them, and the ibtida (beginning) was such that they didn't even know how to make a ghar, so they made gharon (caves) their ghar. They started living in caves. And just as you see that the Stone Age, which is mentioned in the beginning, the halat (conditions) of that zamana (era) which you have read about, exactly the same waqi'at (events) happened, and they, in the same way, started living in pits... in caves. And to get their ghiza, they would kill animals by hitting them with stones, and from that stone, they would also make some hathiyar (weapons), and with that, they would slaughter them and eat. And along with that, slowly, tahzib (civilization) started to spread among them. But the sabab (cause) of the spread of tahzib was due to our Imam, may peace be upon him, that along with the zuhur (appearance) of this universe, the Khaliq (Creator) of the universe had also come into the world. The Khaliq of the universe had also created the malik (master) of that universe, and he is our first Imam, whom we call Qaym-rut-e A'zam. Whom if you look at in the encyclopedia, Qaym-rut means the first badshah (king) who appeared in the world. So they were the first to spread tahzib in the world, about how we should live, how we should protect ourselves, what we should do. Now, where did this happen and what happened? Its ahwal (account) is such that I had told you in the beginning that when in the universe, these vapors that had risen, and from which the barishen had fallen, among those barishen, there were some such barishen also, which Allah Ta'ala had preserved. And I had told you that they were the vapors of the muhallal haywanat (permissible animals). Either they were coming from gold and silver, or they were... from better grass and leaves and mewe, from their perishing, the vapors were rising, or from the death of halal animals themselves, the vapors were rising. Nature was collecting that and bringing it to such a maqam (place) where nature wanted it to rain. So, that maqam was of Lanka. It was of Ceylon, it was of Lanka. There nature took these vapors. And there, at that place, which nature had specified, it rained there, just as barishen had fallen in other places, but the barishen here were special. You will say, "How can there be such special barishen?" So today, whether you believe it or not, that there is also a thing called the abr-e naisan (April cloud). That which you have been believing about the abr-e naisan, that when the abr-e naisan rains over the seas, then moti (pearls) are formed in sip (oysters). So how did this abr-e naisan come into existence? So just as this is, so in the same way, you should understand that when nature intends, it does everything. So the bandobast (arrangement) was made, and Lanka at that time was the best place where nature took it, and after taking it there, the barishen fell. And that too at this maqam, which perhaps... we don't know, and... there is no correct estimation of it, what to locate. But Adam's Peak, which is called, that... even today it is famous by the name of Adam's Peak in Ceylon. That perhaps was the same maqam where nature took that abr (cloud). And this abr rained there, and after raining, there too pits were formed, and from the pits, in the same way, the man and woman were born. But, this nature which was creating them, it is clear that in 6000 years, they were so khasusiyat (special) that they were the very khulasa (essence), that is, they were filtered, very good, clean and shaffaf (pure). From their barishen, these are happening. So what does nature intend? It is that nature is bringing ujale (light) from andheron (darkness). It is bringing light from darkness. And what to say of its tathir (purification), what to say of its filtering? They are being filtered in a big sieve. So, that nature, as it intended, they are coming with great ehtiyat (caution) and great ehtemam (care). And they were brought there, and the pits that were formed were 28. They were not 29, and they were not 26. But there were 28 pits. And those 28 pits were such that the 28th pit was at a 'ala maqam (high place), which nature had specified for it, that this is the highest and most muqaddas (sacred) maqam. Here too, just as no name is given to a thing, but when it becomes muqaddas, then you kiss it as muqaddas and you visit it, you... so in the same way, that would be a muqaddas maqam, where that 28th pit would be, and 27 pits would be around it. It seems as if this is a jama'at (congregation) of muqtadis (followers), and he is their pesh-imam (leader of prayer). So in exactly the same way, that the kaifiyat (condition) of these 28 is such, our du'at say, that if you consider all of them to be in the state of a yaqut (ruby), of a ruby, in the state of a yaqut, then consider the entire world to be a patthar (stone). If the entire world is in the state of a patthar, then in terms of their tanasub (proportion) they are saying. The patthar is not the meaning. To show the tanasub, in terms of fazilat (virtue), that if you consider them to be a patthar, then this is in the state of a yaqut. And if you consider the 27 to be a patthar, then that 28th one is in the state of a yaqut. You understand? This is the qawl (saying) of the du'at, and they have said that he was the most ashraf (noble), the most bartar (superior), and the greatest. The baat (matter) was that I should tell you the pichhla sabaq (previous lesson), that kallamam. The kallamam who were... those kallamam, in kallamam I had told you that there, some were of a nisbat-e a'la (high relation) and some were of a nisbat-e adna (low relation). Some were unche (high) and some were niche (low). Nisbat-e a'la and nisbat-e adna, `ma 'anhu wujudihi ila dhatihi`, two relations are there, which reason has left. Due to those two relations, two relations were established. So I had told that two relations, just as they were established there, so in their tawatur (succession), I had told you that the zaat (being) of Qa'im al-Qiyamah, the zaat of Amir al-Mu'minin, and after that, the zawat (beings) of all the Imams, and among the anbiya' (prophets), as many anbiya' as came, 124,000, they were in the nisbat-e adna. The Imams were in the nisbat-e a'la. This I had told you in mukhtasar (brief). But now I want to add a little to it. The baat was that at that time if I had said it, you would not have understood it. But now I add that before Janab-e Qa'im, there were also some nuqte (points). There were some nuqat-e nur (points of light) which were in the Bayt al-Ma'mur, and they were written with the qalam-e nur (pen of light). And who were those nuqat? Who were the people of that order? Who were the kallamam? Whose... whose nadamat (repentance) was even greater than these. And they were the sahiban-e anwar (masters of the lights), aqwar (cores), and adwar (cycles). Now you will also find this a bit mushkil (difficult) to understand, but anyway, now I have explained to you the dawr, qawr, and mawr. So you should understand that he who covers the dawr, who covers the mawr, and who covers the qawr, he is the sahiban-e anwar, aqwar, and adwar. But those who were coming here, at the beginning of the qawr, of every qawr... that is, a dawr of 400,000 years, and such 400,000 dawrs make one qawr. So at the beginning of every qawr, the paida'ish (creation) happens here. In the universe. Everything is destroyed, and after that, the paida'ish happens. Now what is yours? What is our position? That 399 qawrs have passed. Of the 400th qawr, in the first dawr, we are at the end of the dawr-e sitr (cycle of the veil). This is our position at this time. So 399 qawrs have passed, and we are proceeding in the 400th dawr, and its... in the first dawr, our... is ending at this time. So it becomes clear that the 400th qawr, our... when did it begin? 400,000 years ago. And that... 400,000 dawr, in its qawr... and it... where did it begin? That is, the ras-e qawr (head of the core) which began, it began in Ceylon, it began in Lanka. I am telling you its hal (situation). You would be understanding. So after this destruction, this construction that happened, so I am telling you about this construction, not the first construction of the universe. The first construction of the universe that happened, I will tell you that when the mauqa' (occasion) comes. But for now, you should understand that we have to look at our own ghar (house). So I am telling you how your ghar was built. That our duniya (world), that which is the 400th qawr, we are ending its first dawr. But this 400th qawr which began, it began in Lanka, and it happened in this way, that 28 afrad (individuals) were born there. And these 28 afrad were all such that they were so unche (high), in terms of their maratib (ranks), and in Imamat, they were all of the nisbat-e a'la (high relation). All 28 of them were of the nisbat-e a'la, not in the nisbat-e adna. Not a single one was in the nisbat-e adna. But in the nisbat-e a'la also, they were very unche. Our Qa'im, who is to come, they were many times unche than him. Our Qa'im who is to come, who is the jami' (collector) of all, the bahr-e zakhkhar (ocean of knowledge), they are much unche than him, and they... where are they coming? They are being born in Lanka. Of our qawr, the ibtida (beginning). Now, their 28th one, it's clear that if the 27 are equal to a patthar (stone), then this one is of the misl (likeness) of a yaqut (ruby). So now the nisbat (relation) that has been established here, you will have to understand that that 28th one will be the behtarin (best), and in nisbat, he will be much uncha (higher). So now, to differentiate this, we will keep giving him a naam (name). Now we will say this, that this one who is being born, who is the 28th, whom we consider the Imam-e Awwal (first Imam), or whom we call Qaym-rut-e A'zam, or whom we call the sabiq (precedent), or whom we call the jussa-e ibtida'iyyah (primary essence), or whom we call the jussa-e tabi'iyyah (natural essence), or the पहला Imam (first Imam), or whatever naam you give it, which I am telling you now. So that Imam-e Awwal who is coming, he is the 28th. It is clear that he, in terms of his sharafat (nobility) and 'azmat (greatness), is be-misl (peerless). In his place, he is be-misl, and the 27 are बिल्कुल हेच (absolutely nothing) before him. And those 27, although they are hech before him, they are many times greater than us. And there is no nisbat between us and those 27. These 27 afrad who were born there, nature created them in the same way, because the fitrat-e ilahiyyah (divine nature) wants to keep it ek (one). It does not want to change it. So our Prophet also came, he had the same aankh aur naak ka naqsha (features of eyes and nose), and our Amir al-Mu'minin also came, he had the same aankh aur naak ka naqsha, Fatima Zahra came, she had the same 'awraton ki kaifiyat (feminine features). So it does not want to bring any tabdili (change) in them. So in exactly the same way, their halat will also be the same, khana, pina, rahna, sahna (eating, drinking, living, bearing), everything, sardi, garmi (cold, heat), everything will be in the same way, as it is with us here. So in exactly the same way, those 27 afrad were also so unche afrad, and they were born with the same kaifiyat, in which all the newborns from the pits in the world had their own asarat (effects). Just as all the newborns from the pits in the world, the kaifiyaten (conditions) of mard and 'awrat were there, the same kaifiyat was theirs, whether they were 27 or 28. That is, as they were to be born, they were born in the same way. The farq (difference) was only ek. What was that farq? It was that the 28th one, we cannot count it, nature was counting it with its own qalam (pen). Nature had its shumar (count) of the 28th one. We didn't know. But we are learning and understanding it in an 'ilmi (knowledgeable) way. So it is clear that the halqa (circle) of 27 and their Imam, and that 28th one is the most fazil (virtuous) and the most... in the 'alam-e tabi'i (world of nature), he is in the muqabil (place) of 'aql (intellect). Just as there is the 'Aql-e Awwal (First Intellect), in the same way, in this 'alam-e duniya (world of the world), he stands in the muqabil of the 'Aql-e Awwal. So now, this one who was born, as soon as he came out of the pit, the very first kaam (work) he did was that he did sajda (prostration) to the rububiyyat (lordship) of Allah Ta'ala. This was the first sajda in the universe that happened. First. You will say, "Who taught him, who gave him this samajh-bujh (understanding)?" So the baat is that the cheez (thing) which he could not get there, this is a very aham cheez (important thing), listen carefully. The cheez which he could not get in kallamam, after coming here, in this 'alam-e dani (lowly world), when they changed from bil-quwwah to bil-fi'l (from potential to actual), they got that cheez from the 'ilm-e ma kana wa sa-yakun (knowledge of what was and what will be), which they had not gotten there. You understand? That is, the kallamam were made to stand in the darmiyan (middle), that we will neither include you there, nor are you fit to be sent to this 'alam. You have been made to stand in the darmiyan. So those who were made to stand in the darmiyan, these are the same kallamam who are coming to this 'alam. Now, how are they coming? This is a very bada sawal (big question), and a very aham sawal. And I will try to explain this to you as well. And I will. But what I have to tell you is that this is a very aham cheez to understand, how those kallamam came to this 'alam. You should not think, God forbid, that the kallamam came down here. It's not like that. Neither should you think this, nor that, that it is just a sayah (shadow). No. Neither should you think it's a sayah, nor should you think that they just came down. It didn't happen like that, nor like that, but it was something else, and I will present it to you in that way. But you should understand that these are the same kallamam who have attained the unche se unche maqam (highest of high positions) there, and their asar (effect) has been established, and the asar is the same thing that creates the shakl (form) and comes. There is a grapevine, you have picked grapes from it in the season, and you have eaten them. Now when the next season comes, grapes will grow again, and you will pick them again. So these grapes that are coming, those grapes and these grapes are not ek sa (the same), although angur (grape) is angur. So in exactly the same way, but what is it? That the asar that has been left, that asar will always phal la ke rahega (bear fruit). So in exactly the same way, that the asar cast from there is what is qaym (establishing) them. And they are being qaym. And when they are qaym, then it is clear that they also get that cheez, and nature gives it, that you have done nadamat there as kallamam, and you have done nadamat in such a way that no one has done nadamat. We had not done nadamat. They had said "yes" by not saying "no". And there was no doubt that they too would have been joined to the 'alam-e ruhani (spiritual world). They too would have had a sutuh (breakthrough), they would have been shamil (included). With whom? With the tenth, with the ninth, with anyone they would have been shamil. But what was the wajah (reason)? That the punishment had come, and the saza (sentence) had come down from there. For this reason, they were made to stand, and they stood. And it was said that you do one kaam, that the one whom you have called here, go and call him in the universe too. Here you have sentenced them, you have put them in jail. Now go into this universe as a jailer and take care of them. You will have to go as a jailer, and you will have to take care of them, you will have to give them hidayat (guidance), you will have to free them from this universe. So now, if they came to this universe, then just as a shikari (hunter) goes to a shikargah (hunting ground), to tame the shikar (prey), if he wears the libas (clothes) of a shikari, wears khaki libas, and puts ghas-pat (grass and leaves) on himself, then he doesn't become the shikar, God forbid. But the shikari remains the shikari, the shikar remains the shikar. But the nufus-e habitah (descending souls), they are coming to hunt them, and it's clear that they had to take this roop (form). And they came as mithlukum (like you). `Ana basharun mithlukum`, the Prophet said, "I am a bashar (human) like you." The Prophet did not say, "I am a bashar." This is a very tahalukah machane wala (controversial) ayat, which all Muslims say this, that on the mi'yar (scale) of insaniyat (humanity), the Prophet is in a mi'raj ki kaifiyat (state of ascension). Oh brother, what is insaniyat? For the Prophet, you want to see in terms of insaniyat. This is the reason for seeing the Prophet that insaniyat fell into the ghar-e mazallat (abyss of misguidance), and they started saying about the Prophet that he was a jahil nabi (ignorant prophet), God forbid, God forbid. All these Muslims consider the Prophet to be jahil. They had to accept him as ummi (unlettered). So these Muslims who measure on the mi'yar of insaniyat, they believe in the Nabi-e Ummi. So anyway, what I had to tell was that since those coming from there, these... since they are coming to shikar karne (hunt), they are coming as wardens, as jailers. For God's sake, don't consider them qaidi (prisoners). Don't consider them an insan like yourselves. And that's the truth. What happened in the time of the Prophet? The condition of the people was that they would come in the time of the Prophet, and they would sit looking at the surat (face) of the Prophet. After looking for a while, they would go out and go into the galiyon (streets) of Madinah, and what baten (conversations) would they have? "Oh brother, I am coming from the Prophet." "Oh, what happened?" "Oh brother, I saw, he is بالکل apne jaise hi hain (exactly like us)." The first jumla (sentence). He is like us. I saw him, he was khajur kha rahe the (eating dates). Exactly like us, he is eating. I saw him, he was bagh me phir rahe the (walking in the garden). Exactly like us, he is walking. I saw him, he was suk me chal rahe the (walking in the market). He is doing it just like us. So the Quran took this in its own alfaz (words): `ya'kuluna at-ta'ama wa yamshuna fi al-aswaq` (they eat food and walk in the markets). `Ma li-hadha ar-rasul` (What is wrong with this messenger?). What has happened to the messenger? That he eats and drinks like us, and in the same way, he walks in the bazar (market). There is no farq between him and us, in the rasul and us. So these were the zahir-bin musalman (outward-looking Muslims), who saw the rasul with their own ankhon (eyes), with these lehmi-shehmi ankhon (fleshy, fleshly eyes). So that is why Allah Ta'ala... a ayat came, this ayat struck their azhan (minds) so hard that they are still tadap rahe hain (writhing). What is that? `Wa tarahum yanzuruna ilayka wa hum la yubṣirun` (And you see them looking at you, but they do not see). "O Prophet, you see that they are looking at you," see, the word `tara` in Arabic also means to see. `Tubsirun` also means to see. `Yanzurun` also means to see. Allah Ta'ala has brought three words, and all three words are different, and all three have different meanings. What hikmat (wisdom) of the Lord! `Wa tarahum yanzuruna ilayka`, "O Prophet, you see that they are looking at you, but in haqiqat (reality), they do not see you." These andhe (blind), these of the eyes of the dil (heart) are andhe, what will they see you? With these lehmi-shehmi ankhon. They see nothing but the charbi wali ankh (fatty eye). They cannot see you at all. So the Quran itself refuted this. So it becomes clear that these... the prophets who were coming, so just as the Prophet, in the same way, a being much greater than the prophets.

<!-- AUG:hazrat-zia lecture 14 -->

I had explained before you that the era of Hazrat Nuh, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, lasted for approximately 1,000 years. And the one who established the *da'wah* for Hazrat Nuh, the name of that personality was Maulana Hud. Imam Hud, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, was the one who established it for him. And Hazrat Nuh remained established in his apostleship (*risalat*) and prophethood (*nabuwwat*), and when your era came to an end, the Imam of that time was Maulana Salih.

Maulana Salih was from the progeny of Janab Hud. And after one comes another Imam, which is a universal principle (*qa'ida-e-kulliya*)—that after the father comes the son. That chain was continuing, and Janab Salih, his son's name is Janab Ibrahim, who is called by the name Khalil al-Rahman (the Friend of the Most Merciful). Allah's *khalil* (intimate friend), whom Allah Ta'ala called his *khalil*.

He is a very great prophet. In many respects, you have superiority over all the prophets (*anbiya'*). One is that you are the son of a prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam. And the second is that Allah Ta'ala bestowed upon you the rank of *khullat* (close friendship), He made you a *khalil*. And the third point is *wa ja'alnahu lil-nasi imama* (And We made him an Imam for mankind), that for you, the Imamate... which Allah Ta'ala expressed in the Holy Qur'an.

So that mention of a *nabi* (prophet) is of a *nabi* who was established by Janab Ibrahim, and he was a *da'i* (caller) to whom you had granted prophethood (*nabuwwat*) and apostleship (*risalat*). Who? Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman.

Hazrat Ibrahim is separate, Nabi Ibrahim is separate. Both are separate. And a strange thing was that there was a strange resemblance between the two: that Hazrat Ibrahim, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, who was the Imam, he was, it is apparent that an Imam should provide the guidance (*hidayat*) and teaching (*tanzim*) that he must. He was providing that guidance. And he said, "O people, what has happened to you that you worship idols? *Ma hadhihi al-tamathilu allati antum laha 'akifun* (What are these statues to which you are devoted?). Why do you worship idols? Why are you caught in this degradation (*mazallat*) and misguidance (*gumrahi*)?"

And this same message you had delivered through a *da'i*. And that *da'i* is the one whose name was Ibrahim, and about whom it is said, *rabbahu azhar* (Azar raised him). He was raised by Azar. And in the Qur'an, he is addressed as a father. In reality, Janab Azar was not his father. Azar was an idol-carver (*but-tarash*), and he was the one who raised Janab Ibrahim. The one who was a *da'i*, who later became a *nabi* (prophet) and *rasul* (messenger), he was the one who raised him and provided for his upbringing (*parwarish*). Whom? Janab Ibrahim, the Nabi.

Anyway, this upbringing and so on happened. And now, his stories are very strange and wondrous. That *da'i* was very courageous (*jurratmand*) in his own place. He was very courageous, to whom Allah Ta'ala had granted *sahuliyat* (a special quality), meaning that in *da'wat* (the call), what is called *sahuliyat*, a special rank (*martaba*) of influencing (*kasar*) and breaking the things of the opponent. That quality was within him, and he had great courage within him.

Janab Ibrahim, who was a *nabi*, had great courage. And he... first of all, when he was of a young age, Azar made him sit in his shop, which was a shop of idols. They used to carve idols, and he was made to sit in the idol shop, saying, "Son, you do the work of buying and selling (*kharid-o-farokht*). I will go do some work and come back." Whenever he went outside, he would make his child, whom he was raising, sit there. And Janab Ibrahim would sit there and say very strange and peculiar things.

And it was this: whoever came to buy... There is a book of the Jews (*yahud*) whose name is *Midrash Rabbah*. In that book, and in other Torahs (*tawrat*), Gospels (*injil*), etc., its references are found. The Qur'an-e Majid does not have very detailed accounts, but this Ibrahim, who was Prophet Ibrahim, used to sit in that shop at a young age and buy and sell, and Janab Azar would sell the idols he carved.

Now, when Azar was about to leave and made him sit there, people would come and buy idols. He would say, "Brother, what will you do with this idol? They don't speak, they don't express anything, they don't feel pain (*taklif*), they don't... it is of no harm (*mazarrat*), nor can they express happiness. What do you do with such idols?"

So, instead of selling, he would disillusion the buyer in this way.

And one incident (*waqi'a*) is famous (*mas'hur*): an old woman came one time and she said that... because, just as it happens in our India, that wherever idols are carved or made, worship of them begins right there. Similarly, before Hazrat Ibrahim, an old woman brought an offering (*nazrana*) for the idols; she presented a lot of wheat, saying, "I have brought this offering as a gift (*ahmak*) and I present it to these idols."

Janab Ibrahim took it, and he accepted that offering with great joy and placed it before the idols. And he said to the old woman, "Your offering has been accepted by them, and these gods (*khudawand*) have given you many prayers. You can go."

This poor old woman left from there, happy that her offering had been accepted. What did he do? He took an axe (*kulhada*) and destroyed all the idols, completely ruining (*satyanas*) his shop. Janab Ibrahim.

Now, Azar came. He came and began to say, "Brother, what has happened to the shop? Today, there has been a great calamity (*qayamat*). All the idols are broken. And what have you done, Ibrahim?" He said, "What can I do? An old woman brought this offering. All of them pounced on this offering, and this commotion (*hangama*) happened."

A good example (*namuna*) of civilization (*tahzib*) was presented, and such a war broke out among these gods, that this was the state of the offering.

Azar was very embarrassed. Now what could he say? He said, "Brother, what can I do? Look, ask your gods. All your gods have fought amongst themselves. What can I do?"

So, this was actually a rehearsal for Janab Ibrahim. He wanted to try this on a large scale. And he did try it. And what used to happen was that he left no stone unturned in humiliating (*zillat*) the idols. What he would do was, he would put a rope around the neck of an idol—because idols were made in human form, obviously, what other form besides human and animal shapes could they find? So putting a rope around its neck, he would drag it in the sewers, which were the sewers of that time, in those sewers, he would hang the idols and drag them through the water.

Now, the people would say, "Brother, after all, these are our idols, we worship them. Why are you humiliating them so much? What is this?" He would say, "Brother, you say something, but this idol doesn't say anything. It doesn't know how to speak, it doesn't do anything, this poor thing isn't saying a word. Why are you making such a fuss?"

So, these kinds of actions were done by Janab Ibrahim. And those people were becoming very fed up with Ibrahim, thinking, "This boy has become very strange, and we are very afraid. A very difficult situation has fallen upon our gods. What are these things Ibrahim does?" And where was Hazrat Ibrahim getting this encouragement (*shay*) from? It was from Hazrat Ibrahim, Maulana Ibrahim, who was the Imam of the time, the God of his time, and all the guidance was coming from him. And he was saying, "Yes, Ibrahim, do it, do it well."

The point, in fact, was that a counter-call (*dawate-e-zid*) was also established against Janab Ibrahim. Always remember that wherever there is guidance (*hidayat*), along with it, there is also misguidance (*gumrahi*). And the more guidance increases, the more misguidance comes forth. You may try your best to produce butter (*maska*), you may extract butter, but to extract butter you have to churn yogurt, but buttermilk (*chhaach*) will surely be produced.

So, if you want to separate one thing, you don't want to make it, but buttermilk will be produced. It's the same thing. The struggle between good and evil has been perpetual in the world since time immemorial. *Chiragh-e-Mustafavi se sharar-e-Bu Lahabi* (From the lamp of Mustafa comes the spark of Abu Lahab). It will keep happening. This conflict is always there.

So here, the *dawate-e-zid* was that of Nimrud bin Kan'an. He was the son of Kan'an, and his name was Nimrud, and his fire is famous. And he had performed great spectacles, and the biggest thing he did was that he claimed that he... this was a lesser claim than Fir'awn's in terms of gain. Fir'awn had claimed divinity, saying *ana rabbukum al-a'la* (I am your Lord, the Most High). Nimrud did not say that he was God, but he did say that he was everything of God—his son and everything—and that he was going to meet God.

People started asking, "Brother, when are you going? At least if a date is set, we can also celebrate a bit, that you are going to meet God." He said, "I will, Insha'Allah, go." And he had built a big minaret (*minar*). To this day, it is present in Babylon. That minaret is still present in Babylon today. He had climbed that minaret and, after climbing, he thought he would reach God.

He had gathered a very large army to fight with Hazrat Ibrahim, the *Khalil*. But Allah Ta'ala sent an army of mosquitoes against this huge army. Which army did he send? He sent an army of mosquitoes. Against them, he sent an army of mosquitoes, which destroyed their army, leaving only their skeletons (*pinjar*), and they were finished. This was the last time for Nimrud to be finished, when he came to be finished. But in between, many incidents happened. I will tell you those incidents first.

What happened was that on one side, they were greatly insulting the idols. Nabi Ibrahim, and he tried this formula when the community had gone to a big fair (*mela*), which was known as the fair of Sahaba. The whole community, women, children, everyone used to participate in it. He saw that it was a very good opportunity. There was a very big temple (*ma'bad*), a big church (*girja*), in which all the idols were kept. This Janab Ibrahim secretly went into that idol-house (*but-khane*).

And after going there, Nabi Ibrahim... what did he do there? He broke all the idols and finished them. And on the shoulder of the big idol, he placed the axe (*tesha*). He placed the axe on the shoulder of the big idol and then secretly left from there. When the people returned from there, they saw that a calamity (*qayamat*) had befallen the temple; all the idols were broken and lying there. Now they started consulting among themselves, "Brother, who could have done this?"

Now, the Qur'an mentions this, saying: *rajulun yuqalu lahu ibrahim* (a man called Ibrahim). "Oh, oh, it seems like such a thing, we have seen or heard of a young man, a... *rajulun*... we have heard of a man whose name is... who is called... what is he called? He is called Ibrahim." Look here, look, *rajulun yuqalu lahu...* Ibrahim. Here, the Qur'an-e Majid has clearly said, has stated the matter clearly, that Khalil al-Rahman is someone else, and this *rajulun yuqalu lahu ibrahim* is someone else.

So, *rajul* is always what a *da'i* is called, a *nabi* is called, the first of the *da'wat* is called. And they were the first of the *da'wat*, for whom the word *nabi* came. And they pointed towards Janab Ibrahim. They caught Janab Ibrahim and brought him. And the people said, "Brother, what have you done?" He said, "I haven't done anything. I didn't even go there."

So he said, "Look, ask this big idol, on whose shoulder the axe is placed. Ask him if he can speak."

So, since the matter had escalated, a deputation (*delegation*) of the entire community went, and that delegation (*wafad*) reached Nimrud and began to say, "Brother, this is what is happening, and we are fed up." Nimrud saw that this... since he was the master of the counter-call (*dawate-e-zid*), he understood that this Ibrahim... the real Ibrahim is behind him, in the curtain, who is doing the work, and that is Imam Ibrahim. He had him summoned. And he said to Janab Ibrahim, "O Ibrahim, I am tired of these incidents. Such incidents are happening in our government. It is better that we reach some compromise (*compromise*), or it would be good if you are dealt with through argument (*dalil*), that would be better." And first, he thought it better than a compromise to convince Janab Ibrahim through argument.

So, he said to Janab Ibrahim that, "Let's do this: that Ibrahim, it's better that you don't believe in my idols, and I don't believe in your unseen God. Let's do this, it's better that we accept water as God. And you also accept it, and I will also accept it."

Janab Ibrahim said at that very moment, "But why shouldn't I consider the cloud as God, which brings the water?"

He said, "Alright, brother, let's go. You say this, so I am ready to consider the cloud as God." He said, "Why shouldn't the wind be accepted, which blows the clouds?"

He said, "Alright, we will accept the wind." He said, "But fire has control over the wind. Why shouldn't fire be accepted?" He said, "Alright, we will accept fire." He said, "Why will you accept fire? The one that has control over everything is death. Why don't you accept death?" "Alright, let's accept death." "Then why don't you accept the Angel of Death (*malak al-mawt*), who brings death?"

Now he said, "You are doing something terrible! You don't stick to anything. The Angel of Death... now you are again going towards God." He said, "I have understood, Ibrahim, what your motive is. You are not ready to believe."

So, Janab Ibrahim said, "My argument is this: my God brings the sun from the east and makes it set in the west. Can yours do that? Can you bring it out?"

So, he... the answer he gave was not this. Who? Nimrud. He said that... Nimrud said, "O Ibrahim, my... you, the claim you make... you had first claimed that your God brings it out from the east... and before that, you had claimed that my God causes death and gives life. He is the one who kills and the one who gives life. I can do that work too."

And at that very moment, what did he do? He called a good man from his court and had him killed. And a prisoner who had a death sentence, he had him released. "See," he said, "I have also given life, and I have also killed."

So Ibrahim gave this argument about bringing it from the east and west, and at that moment, Nimrud saw that arguing with Ibrahim is futile. Now it's better to punish him. And since I am a king, I can give punishment. He gave the order to light a fire, and a massive fire was lit.

So, it was famous that the fire was so massive that its flames were miles high, and its heat was reaching the sky, and the atmosphere had become quite hot. And them... at that time, Shaytan came to Nimrud and... you know, I told you from the beginning, now you have a good acquaintance with Shaytan. You have understood that Shaytan always comes in new forms, but it is the same one. It is the same one. The one who stops you from good deeds. Any good deed, even if it's collecting charity, any good deed he stops, that is the work of Shaytan, remember this. And the best of the best work in today's time is this. And this is the work of today's time. And if he stops in this, *manna'in lil-khayri mu'tadin athim* (a preventer of good, a transgressor, a sinner). The Qur'an says, the one who stops a good deed is a great sinner.

So, these proofs and arguments are things to make our own hearts understand. Everyone understands, but the things to make others understand are very different. But the matter, in fact, is that this is all the work of that Shaytan. That Shaytan came and said to Nimrud, "Look, if you want to throw Ibrahim, how will you throw him? You can't even go near the fire." So, it is better that you throw Ibrahim with a catapult (*ghofan*). Meaning, tie him in clothes and swing him in a certain way, and after swinging, release him in such a way that Ibrahim goes and falls in. Otherwise, you won't be able to get close and throw him.

The same was done. And at that time, it was told that Nimrud's daughter, whose name was Holi... Holi, whose name was that, she was sitting up high and watching, and this sight... because she had become a believer (*mominah*) from the heart, and she had accepted faith in Janab Ibrahim. And when she saw that this fire was lit and the Lord of Fire, Janab Ibrahim, was thrown into it, she also jumped and fell in. In memory of whom, to this day, they burn Holi. These wretched ones, these Hindus who burn Holi, the origin is this thing.

Are you understanding? So the matter is, in fact, of some old things which have been given a new, new form. So Holi is from there. And it was burned in this way... she passed away and was burned, but Janab Ibrahim, Khalil al-Rahman, the fire became *bardun wa salaman 'ala ibrahim* (cool and safe for Ibrahim). *Kunu bardun wa salaman 'ala ibrahim* (Be cool and safe for Ibrahim). As soon as you fell upon the fire, Allah Ta'ala gave the command, "O fire, become cold, become cool upon him." Who was the one giving this command? This was Janab Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman.

The one who fell, but the one who gave the command, in reality, was from the *'Ashir al-Mutimm* (the Tenth of the Perfected Ones). Because now, if your gods are to be counted, the sky above you will be counted, then who? The *'Ashir*. And if it was from the *'Ashir*, then it is that, just as we believe, that the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam... *kuntu nabiyyan wa adamu bayna al-ma'i wal-tin* (I was a prophet when Adam was between water and clay). You had said, "Adam was still in the mud, he was still in the earth, he was not even made yet, and I existed. I had become a prophet." In the same way, 'Ali was also from that very time. So these commands, which are from above, they are from above. So, in any case, from them, the command of *bardun wa salaman 'ala ibrahim* happened, and this *Maula-e-Kainat, Mushkil-Kusha* (Master of the Universe, Remover of Difficulties) solved his difficulty, and that fire became cool. And after the fire became cool, although at that time angels were descending, the angel of water descended, the angel of mountains descended, saying, "I will destroy the people, I will bring down a landslide upon the people, I will create a whirlwind of winds." But you did not accept anyone's help. You said, "I trust in Allah." And Allah gave this command and made the fire cool, and Janab Ibrahim remained safe and sound and was saved.

So these incidents happened in this way. And you had victory over Nimrud in such a way that Nimrud was left biting his finger, wondering how Ibrahim was saved. And after that, he led his army, and the result of the military expedition was that from Allah Ta'ala's side, the army of mosquitoes destroyed him. And one mosquito entered his nose in such a way that it took his life and then left. And it is famous that Nimrud's life was taken by a mosquito. Anyway, in one way or another, he was, in any case, destined for hellfire (*innar wa saqar*) and was finished.

But the biggest strange incident of Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman's time, and the most magnificent incident was that your noble *da'wat* (call)... there was the establishment of that noble *da'wat* and its strengthening. And you, after you, wanted to continue that chain of Imamat. Obviously, it had to be continued. The son of an Imam becomes the Imam. And Hazrat Ibrahim, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, in his progeny, you had Janab Hajra and Janab Sarah, two of your wives. From Janab Sarah, Janab Ishaq was born, who had become old. And from Janab Hajra, there was no offspring yet. So you raised your hands in prayer and began to say, "O Lord, grant me offspring from Hajra as well. *Wa hab lana min al-salihin* (And grant us from the righteous)." Allah Ta'ala mentions in the Qur'an-e Majid, the prayer of Janab Ibrahim: *Wa hab lana min al-salihin*. "O Allah Ta'ala, grant me something from the righteous."

*Fa-bashsharnahu bi-ghulamin halim* (So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy). Allah Ta'ala blessed him with a young, good son, He gave him the good news. *Fa-bashsharnahu bi-ghulamin halim. Fa-lamma balagha ma'ahu al-sa'ya qala ya bunayya inni ara fi al-manami anni adhbahuka* (When he reached [the age of] exertion with him, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you"). When that child was able to run with him... the Qur'an is narrating... that child became equal to Janab Ibrahim, he became able to run and move about. Which child? That was Janab Isma'il. Hazrat Isma'il, who was born of Janab Hajra, when he became able to run and walk, at that time, the father, addressing Janab Isma'il, began to say, "O son, *inni ara fi al-manami anni adhbahuka fa-nzur madha tara* (Indeed I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think)." "O son, I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you. *Fa-nzur madha tara*. What is your opinion? Tell me."

Did you see? Now, what is your opinion about this? You also tell me your wish. I have seen such and such, that I am slaughtering you. And what comes to me, the dreams that come, I am a sent prophet and messenger, and true dreams come to me. What sent prophet and messenger? I am the Imam of the time. I am the Imam, true dreams come to me. And I have seen this. It is apparent that I want to slaughter you. Now, what do you... what is your opinion?

So you said, "*ya abati if'al ma tu'maru sa-tajiduni in sha' allahu min al-sabirin* (O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the patient)." "O father, whatever you have been commanded, carry it out. Insha'Allah, you will find me among the patient."

Now this... Janab Isma'il's miracle was that you upheld your father's word. And Janab... you said to Janab Ibrahim, "Whatever you have been commanded by God, carry it out." And Janab Ibrahim took him, and began the sacrifice of Janab Isma'il. Even if the apparent story happened... as I have told you, there are many such incidents in the Qur'an-e Majid that happened in the apparent and also happened in the inner (*batin*). But here, along with this apparent story, the real story was the *batini* story. That *batini* story, what was the matter in fact? That Hazrat Ibrahim's elder son was Ishaq, who was from Sarah. And from Hajra was Isma'il, who was the younger son. The entire world of Islam is in agreement that Janab Isma'il was the elder, Janab Ishaq was the younger.

Did you see? Meaning, there is a difference in age, a difference in names, a difference in deeds, a difference in understanding, a difference in everything. Now, this Janab Isma'il was the younger son, and he was from Hajra. And you saw this, and you... So, what was the matter in fact? That Hazrat Ibrahim wanted to entrust *nabuwwat* (prophethood) and *risalat* (apostleship) to his son, and to keep that thing going as well. Why? Because he himself was the Imam. He himself had to send someone as a messenger. Whom had you sent? That was Ibrahim, whose name... the *da'i* who was yours, to whom you had entrusted the task. But after that, you had to continue it. After that, too. And since you yourself were present, after that Ibrahim who was the *nabi*, after his passing, you wanted to grant *nabuwwat* to one of your sons. To grant *nabuwwat* to your own son. Imamat, of course. But you wanted to honor your son with *nabuwwat* and *risalat*. At that time, your gaze of grace fell upon whom? Upon Hazrat Isma'il. That ancestor of the Prophet (*jadd-e-rasul*), Hazrat Isma'il, who was the Imam, who was the son of his father, the son of Ibrahim, and the younger son, your gaze fell upon him, and you wanted to honor him with *nabuwwat* and *risalat*. This is the *zabihah* (sacrifice). Whenever *nas* (appointment) has to be done, *nas* is called *zabihah*. When *zabihah* comes, you should understand it is *nas*.

So, by *zabihah* is meant... this is our terminology in the entire Qur'an-e Majid, that *zabihah* is always *nas*. Appointing someone. *Man suyyida zubha bidun sikkin* (Whoever is made a leader is slaughtered without a knife). The one who is made a leader in any place... the Prophet says, he is slaughtered without a knife. That was the real *zabihah*. And this slaughter of Janab Isma'il, what was it? It was to appoint him for *nabuwwat* and *risalat*. And you took Janab Isma'il and when you wanted to perform the *zabihah*, what happened at that time? That when you... *falamma aslama wa tallahu lil-jabin* (And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead). You laid him face down. It's not like you cut a goat's throat, in that way. No, no. *Falamma aslama wa tallahu lil-jabin*. He laid him on his forehead, and from the back of the neck, he wanted to cut.

*Wa nadaynahu... nadaynahu... ya ibrahim qad saddaqta al-ru'ya inna kadhalika najzi al-muhsinin* (And We called to him... We called to him, "O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the vision. Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good"). "And We called out from Ibrahim's side, 'Ibrahim, what are you doing? Oh, oh, not like this. You are indeed among the doers of good.'" So what was it? Janab Ibrahim wanted to run the knife on Janab Isma'il. Meaning, he wanted to make this *nas*. He wanted to write it down and give it, that I am honoring you with *nabuwwat* and *risalat*. When you had decided this, and you were about to hand over that paper or sign it, at that very moment, Allah Ta'ala stopped you. And a call came to you, "O Ibrahim, what are you doing? *Risalat* and *nabuwwat*? अरे, this one is the heir to the Imamat. He is going to be the master (*aqa*). How can you make him a slave (*ghulam*)?"

Did you understand? Is it becoming clear? This one is going to be the master. How are you giving him such a small thing? अरे, he is the master. He is the Imam. How can you give him *risalat* and *nabuwwat*? Give *risalat* and *nabuwwat* to Ishaq. It is not so, that the younger is the elder and the elder is the younger. You are giving it to him? He is the heir to the Imamat. He is the heir to the Imamat. He is the master. And give prophethood to Janab Ishaq. At that very moment, what did you do? Allah Ta'ala immediately sent a ram, which it has been said by the Prophet that it had been grazing in Paradise for 40 years. That ram was very plump and healthy. Obviously, Paradise... the grass of Paradise, and then the ram of Paradise, and how much it must have grazed. It must have been so fatty, like the ones here in Kuwait. It must have come. We get so much to eat, but the goat doesn't get fat, but its life is taken. Here in the desert, but the ram is fat. It came, and Janab Ibrahim sacrificed that ram. So this fatty ram... and this... where from? It had been grazing in Paradise for 40 years. In reality, it was not that the ram was a ram, nor was Paradise Paradise, nor was grazing grazing. And in reality, it was this: that Hazrat Lut, the prophet, who among all the prophets is the highest prophet, meaning after Janab Ibrahim, if the greatest prophets are counted, it is Lut, the prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam. Your being is very high, very great, of great majesty. And this you have achieved merely through your own effort (*kasb*), because you were sent to such a people who were steeped in misguidance. And you extricated them from great degradation (*zalalat*). Because of this, your rank became high. And that Hazrat Lut, the prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, he was similar to that ram. In reality, that ram was meant to be Janab Lut, who in Paradise, meaning in the knowledge of the Hazrat-e-Imami, had been studying for 40 years, and he was sent, that "sacrifice him." Meaning, grant him prophethood and so on. Now, don't look towards Ishaq yet. Here, Janab Lut came, and you sacrificed Janab Lut, meaning you entrusted him with *risalat* and *nabuwwat*. But when you were entrusting *risalat* and *nabuwwat*, a sign came from the Imam towards you, "Look, Ibrahim, you are giving it, but make him a trustee (*mustawda'*). Make him only a trustee (*amanat-dar*) for your son Ishaq."

This... but it is that Ishaq could not receive prophethood and *risalat* until Lut received it, because he had achieved that greatness. So these were those rams, which Janab Ibrahim sacrificed. And after that, *wa fadaynahu bi-dhibhin 'azim* (and We ransomed him with a great sacrifice). This was the great sacrifice which Janab Ibrahim fulfilled. And Allah Ta'ala said, *inna hadha lahuwa al-bala'un mubin* (Indeed, this was the manifest trial). This was a very severe trial, which... meaning, it was a battle between two sons, and Allah's... not a sent prophet, but the Imam of the time faced a great dilemma, as to whom to give prophethood and *risalat*, and to whom to give Imamat and apostleship. This dilemma arose. Indeed, this was a great trial for an Imam, but you came through this trial very successfully, and you distributed what you had to. You gave it to Janab Isma'il, but making whom a trustee? Janab Lut, who was in place of the ram. And you entrusted everything to him. After that, what did you do for Janab Ishaq? From Janab Lut's side, that thing was a trust (*amanat*). That trust... trusteeship is trusteeship. Even if they sit with the money, the trust has to be handed over. He handed over that trust to whom? To Hazrat Ishaq. This Hazrat Ishaq, Janab... whose... Janab Ayyub's father. Janab Ayyub, whose father? Janab Yusuf's father. And the chain continued, of father and son, for some time, and the chain of prophethood continued in this way for some time, and in the progeny of Janab Ishaq, prophethood continued. There, prophethood and *risalat* continued, and here, Isma'il, the Imam, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, whom Janab Ibrahim, after him, his younger son, honored with Imamat. Now, along with honoring with Imamat, what happened was that a story from your childhood is that you were still young, this incident had not even occurred yet, that Janab Hajra took you and left, and where did you reach? Nature wanted these wonders to keep happening in the world, and you reached Mecca the Honored. Who? Hajra, with Janab Isma'il. Now, this is all written in the *Tiskar-e-Ibrahim* (Memorials of Ibrahim). That there were some relics of Hazrat Ibrahim, these are his memorials, these are his miracles, these are his signs, because of which this Hajj came into being in the world of Islam. What Hajj came, brother? That she brought Janab Isma'il, Janab Hajra, and there it was a desert, a barren valley (*wadi ghayr-i dhi-zar'*). There was no sign of water there, a desolate, barren land, and Mecca the Honored. And after arriving there, Janab Isma'il became thirsty. He became so thirsty that Janab Hajra became restless for her child. A mother's love awoke, and you started looking to see if any water was visible. For that, you climbed a small hill. The name of that hill was Safa. And from that hill, she saw if any water was visible. She saw that it was not visible. She ran and went to another hill, its name was Marwa. And reaching Marwa, she looked again, and again, that there is no water. In this way, she made seven rounds, and despite making the rounds, no water was found. Exhausted and disheartened, she came to her son and saw that from the rubbing of his feet, a spring was gushing out from the ground, and so much water was flowing that the water would not stop. And that child was quenched with water, but even after that, it would not stop. So Janab Hajra said, "Zam, zam" (stop, stop). And as soon as she said "Zam, zam," the water stopped. But to this day, that miracle of Islam is apparent. There are many miracles of Islam, and among them, one miracle is this, that today that small well... look today, that people from all over the world are quenched from it. Since when? From Janab Adam's time until now, they are being quenched. You will say the story of Ibrahim is starting. No, it starts from there. That water which has never finished is always flowing and has always been available. And the world has been quenched. So, this... and this running that she did, Allah Ta'ala instituted the *sa'i* (ritual running) because of it, that "you too, just as my pure wife, Hajra, ran, you too run." And in this way, she performed the *tawaf* (circumambulation), so you too perform the *tawaf*. And that Janab Ibrahim and Isma'il... *tahir baytiya lil-ta'ifina wal-'akifina wal-rukka'i al-sujud* (purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who are devoted and those who bow and prostrate). For them, we... this House has been purified. Janab Ibrahim and Isma'il built it. You circumambulate this House. These things were not like this. अरे, this House, as you know, *inna awwala baytin wudi'a lil-nasi lalladhi bi-bakkata mubarakan* (Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed). This was God's first house. Are, Kamru-te-Azam was born here. And its glory and majesty was that the first point of the *Tamur* came here. It's not as the Shi'a say, that because 'Ali was born here, the Ka'ba gained honor. No, no. Of course, in its own place, this honor is very true, but 'Ali being born in the Ka'ba is an honor because the first *ibda'* (origination) was born there, he was born there, Janab 'Ali. This is certainly an honor, there is no doubt in it. But along with that honor, this thing is also necessary. So, the world of Islam took it that this... what is Hajj? It is the memorials of Ibrahim. Janab Ibrahim, when he was taking Janab Isma'il for sacrifice, Shaytan met him on the way. And I always tell you that Shaytan's biggest job is what? To stop. To stop from a good deed. He said, "Ibrahim, what are you doing? You are going to cut your beloved son? You are going to kill him? What is this? What are you doing?" At that time, you picked up a stone and threw it, and said, "May Allah's curse be upon you. You stop me from a good deed." Then he went further, another Shaytan came, you threw a stone at him too. A third Shaytan came, you threw at him too. So they say, look, three Shaytans had come, that is why three Shaytan pillars were made, and stoning those idols in this way became a memorial of Ibrahim. Apparently, it is certainly correct, but in the inner (*batin*), there are great depths. These are manholes. All the corrupt things that are going on in the world, you don't open the entire sewer, you open the manhole and look. So this, in their respective places... whatever doubts arose in the time of Nuh, in every era, the three who have been, Qarun and Haman and Fir'awn, you see them in their place. There is mention of these three. In this way, all who have been, in their own place, these are their residual bodies, their dirty bodies' locations. And when you throw a stone at them, reciting the prayer, then you should be certain that nature does this: that the bullet that you will fire from a gun will not have that effect which that pebble will have, whether it hits or not, but it will have an effect. It will have an effect, and nature... at that time, when it is meant to be hit, it is like a living human being, that idol is standing there. You see it as a stone pillar, but in reality, it is alive. And the blow lands on it, and it feels the blow. And nature wants it to be hit. And the blow lands. So anyway, the matters of Hajj are different. What to go into those details for. In any case, all this happens. So, it happened in the apparent, and it happened in the inner. And this was the kind of incident with Hazrat Ibrahim, and Janab... Hazrat Isma'il. And then Janab Ibrahim, searching for his son, reached there. So, reaching the Baytullah, you took Janab Isma'il and you, taking him there, in building this House... *li-l-ta'ifina wal-'akifina wal-rukka'i al-sujud*. Allah Ta'ala says, "*Tahir baytiya* (Purify My House)..." Meaning, they built this House for Allah. *Wa idh yarfa'u ibrahimu al-qawa'ida min al-bayti* (And [mention] when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House). They raised the House high. They built that House, Janab Ibrahim. And for whom did they purify the House? For all those who perform *tawaf*, who bow, who prostrate, for their sake, it was purified and cleaned, and built. Even today, that place where Janab Ibrahim stood and built, where the marks of his blessed feet are, that is the Station of Ibrahim (*Maqam-e-Ibrahim*). It is a great sign (*mash'ar-e-'izam*). And today, the entire world of Islam that is misguided... misguided... the state of the world of Islam is that that Baytullah, which is Allah's most blessed House, there Allah Ta'ala has kept only one grave. And whose grave is that? Hazrat Isma'il's. The grave of Hazrat Isma'il, Zabihullah (the one sacrificed to Allah), is right there. And where is that grave? It is in that arch, which is under the *mizab* (waterspout). That is why the *tawaf* is done from the outside, but despite that, Muslims enter inside, they recite prayers there, they trample the grave with their feet. That is why it is forbidden for us to... from inside... only at the time of Hajj, to make the intention under the *mizab-e-rahmat* (waterspout of mercy) is allowed. Otherwise, it is not, because that is the grave of Janab Isma'il. That small crescent, that part which is between the *rukn-e-shami* and *rukn-e-'iraqi*, that arch that is built, that crescent, inside that crescent, Hazrat Isma'il is buried. You understand? So in any case, these wonders happened, many such wonders. And it happened in this way. And Hazrat Ibrahim, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, distributed his spiritual lights (*anwar*) in such a way that he gave this to Janab Ishaq, and he gave that to Janab Isma'il. But you wanted that just as all these things are being given by me, you, in your own time, also wanted to acquire them in the same way. One thing that happens is that you think an Imam, whether a child or an adult or whatever, an Imam is an Imam, what need is there for him to read or write? No, no. Just as nature desires, in the same way, a child will have to read, he will have to write, he will have to learn. The entire process will be the same as it is for our children. Why so? Because he has to present the character of a human being before us. He has to present the character of a human being. That is why, when I will mention the Prophet of Allah, sallallahu 'alayhi wa-sallam, the biggest misguidance in the world of Islam is regarding the Prophet, that they call the Prophet the *nabi-e-ummi* (the unlettered prophet). Na'udhubillah, na'udhubillah (God forbid), they call him an ignorant prophet. They say that this is the greatness of the Prophet, that the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, despite being ignorant, taught all the people, the entire world of Islam. So they consider this a sign of greatness, but they don't understand that this is a great insult. Na'udhubillah, it is to be insolent in the honor of the Prophet. The Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, was a tremendous scholar. And what can be said about the knowledge of the Prophet? Whose knowledge can compare to the Prophet's knowledge? And the Prophet's knowledge, how was it? He had learned it. There are teachers, there is a school, there is a madrasa, everything, Insha'Allah, when the mention of the Prophet comes, I will tell you. Where he read and where he learned, who the teachers were, what was the age, what he was learning. It will all come. But in the same way, Hazrat Ibrahim, the ancestor of the Prophet, the Prophet's grandfather, he also learned in the same way. In the same way, you also received education, and how did you receive that education? You, at that time, you received education in such a way that you... first of all, as the Qur'an-e Majid mentions, that at that time, because *kahanat-parasti* (soothsaying-worship) was very prevalent, at that time, *sitara-parasti* (star-worship) was very prevalent. So in the story of Hazrat Ibrahim, it comes in this way, that you saw the star, and said, "*Qala hadha rabbi* (He said, 'This is my Lord')." "This is my Lord." *Fa-lamma afala qala la uhibbu al-afilin* (But when it set, he said, "I do not love those who set"). When that star set, he said, "I don't like those who set." *Fa-lamma ra'a al-qamara bazighan qala hadha rabbi* (And when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my Lord"). When he saw the moon, he said, "*Hadha rabbi*. This is my Lord. It is absolutely certain. This big moon is surely my God." *Fa-lamma afala qala la uhibbu al-afilin* (But when it set, he said, "I do not love those who set"). "I don't like those who set." The Qur'an is mentioning this. *Fa-lamma ra'a al-shamsa bazighatan qala hadha rabbi hadha akbar* (And when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my Lord; this is greater"). When he saw the sun, so bright and so luminous, he said, "*Hadha akbar* (This is greater). This is very big." And he said that this... this is surely God. And after that, he says that *la-in lam yahdini rabbi la-akunanna min al-qawm al-dhalimin* (if my Lord had not guided me, I would have been among the erring people). "If my Lord does not guide me, I will be among the wrongdoers." Now you should laugh and cry at the state of the world of Islam. Whatever you do, but the entire world of Islam says that this Janab Ibrahim, according to the custom of that time, he called the star God, and when it set, he left it. Then he called the moon God, and when it set, he was disillusioned. Then he called the sun God, but it also... but then what? In this way... but Janab Ibrahim could not understand, and such things happened to him as was the talk of that time. And so Janab Ibrahim's state was also like that, and he remained misguided, but then Allah Ta'ala guided him, because he had to be made a messenger, a prophet, that is why Allah Ta'ala kept guiding him. All these things are not so. And for God's Imam to have such things said about him, it is not so. Are, this is presenting the nature of a human being, Allah Ta'ala is. And Hazrat Ibrahim's matters are being presented, how his education and upbringing was in his childhood. You, when you first saw the star... this star is Janab Hud. The great personality of that time, whose name was Hud. That Hud, when he came as a teacher to you and began to teach Janab Ibrahim, you began to say that this teacher... just as these incidents happen to you and me, that we consider the teacher an angel. "What a teacher we have, he is a treasure trove of all knowledge, and how excellently he knows." Just as we form a conception about our teacher, in the same way, Janab Ibrahim's conception for Janab Hud was that he is everything. *Fa-lamma afala*, when they set, meaning when Ibrahim became proficient in that knowledge and reached the level of his teacher's knowledge, and Janab Ibrahim saw that "Are, this is nothing, there are many scholars above him. This is like the camel who saw its own height under the mountain. Now what is his status? Are, this..." *Fa-lamma afala*, they set. So he said, "I don't like those who set." Meaning, "I don't like those who limit knowledge. I want knowledge to soar." Allah Ta'ala says, "*fawqa kulli dhi 'ilmin 'alim* (And above every possessor of knowledge is a Knower)." Above every scholar, there is another scholar. So in this way, above every scholar, there is another scholar. So that meant exactly this. That Janab Ibrahim, what did he do after that? He saw the moon. What is the moon? That is Janab, who were the great personalities of your time, whose name was Salih. That great personality was your teacher, and he started your education and upbringing. Now he started their education. And when their education was finished, he said, "Brother, I was thinking that he is everything. Now he is also finished. He was a great teacher, and that great teacher is also finished." So he said, "But I was thinking that he is everything, but he has also set." And after that, the sun of the universe shone. This is Janab Salih. Janab Salih's... who? Your own father. Your own father. Janab Salih is teaching and bringing you up. And when he finished teaching you, he said, "Ibrahim, now you have acquired everything." So after that, he says that if Allah Ta'ala at this time... all this has been acquired... now he too... this sun of the universe, I thought that he is everything, but my father has also taught me whatever he had to, I have understood everything. At that time, you say that if my Lord does not guide me, I will be among the misguided people. So it is known that, na'udhubillah, what the world of Islam gives the fatwa on, that Hazrat Ibrahim was going towards disbelief (*kufr*), and Allah Ta'ala saved him, did this, it was not like that. If it was a matter of *kufr*, as other great scholars of Islam have applied this word to Janab Ibrahim, have done this injustice, that he was going towards *kufr*, it was not like that. If he was going towards *kufr*, then why did Allah Ta'ala present the words of Janab Ibrahim, *la-in lam yahdini rabbi la-akunanna min al-qawm al-dhalimin*? That "if I... if I... if my Lord does not guide me, I will be among the wrongdoers."

These matters were all of teachers and of his studentship. And after that, you received guidance, and you were honored with Imamat. So these were matters of education and upbringing, which were stages you had completed. Janab Ibrahim. Just as the ancestor of the Prophet, Hazrat Ibrahim Khalil al-Rahman, completed it, in the same way, our Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, also, when those incidents befell him, you also completed them. And you fulfilled them completely. When the mention of the Prophet comes, I will tell you how you completed them. But nature wants that just as a life story is presented, the entire life story should be presented. There should be war and battle, there should be struggles, there should be illness, there should be travel, there should be migration, one should also be beaten, one should also be whipped, everything should happen. There should be comfort, Gabriel should also descend, there should be a Mi'raj, everything should happen. A life story should be presented. And there should also be miracles, that you are left at a crossroads, wondering what kind of personality this is. So, for the life story to come before us, it was presented in this way, and every prophet left his life story in this way, so that it would be a source of guidance for us. If only those from the Tamur had come here to the world and had come in that state only, in a spiritual state, in an intellectual state, and had given a call, "Come, O people, and accept our guidance," then you would see that if such a voice came here, what would happen? The entire group here would leave the house. "Oh brother, it seems there is some problem here." And the matters that are seen are different. The matters that are seen are different. Voices are coming from here and there. "What kind of thing is this? We have never heard such a voice. We are not ready to learn such a lesson." So you would neither learn the lesson nor would he give guidance. So the matter, in fact, is that Allah Ta'ala did not keep the method of giving guidance in this way. He sent them in human form so that we, as human beings, can take complete guidance from a human being, and understand and comprehend. And he also, before us, presents the same kind of life story. There is war, there is battle, there is illness, there is sickness, he laughs, he cries, there is assembly, there is poetry, all the incidents happen in the same way. Husayn is coming running, the court of the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, is assembled, and coming, the dates that are kept in the dish, and Janab Husayn comes and takes the dates and eats them. He is a child. And all the people are watching, saying that Husayn is a small child, he came, an innocent child, and took the dates and ate them. It is a completely innocent manner, a gesture. He must have eaten. But the Prophet, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, says, "O Husayn, look, charity (*zakat*) is forbidden (*haram*) for us. What have you done? How did you put this in your mouth?" Although he is a child, the Prophet is saying so... but if the Prophet said this, why? Because he wanted to inform the Ummah, so that this thing is noted, and it is told, "Look, *zakat* is forbidden for the Ahl al-Bayt." And you put your hand in his mouth and took out the date with the saliva and threw it, saying, "No, this is forbidden for us." So, did Husayn not know this? अरे, Husayn knew. He knowingly came and ate, and this was all a complete understanding between them. This is all a matter of understanding. That "we will eat, and you will take it out." So that such a precedent is set in the world, such a thing happens, so that all the people know that such and such a thing happens. When Janab Mufaddal... Janab Mufaddal, who is the Babul-Abwab of Janab Ja'far al-Sadiq, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam, who is the highest personality, you are coming with whom? With Janab... with Janab Ja'far al-Sadiq, 'alayhi al-salatu wa-salam... he was the Babul-Abwab, but you were the *kalb* (dog/servant), but you were the Babul-Abwab of Maulana Zain al-Abidin, 'Ali Zain al-Abidin. You come, Maulana 'Ali Zain al-Abidin is performing Hajj. As soon as he is performing Hajj and circumambulating, what happens? First of all, you kiss the Hajar al-Aswad (Black Stone). As soon as you go to kiss it, the people part like moss, just as moss parts on water, they part like that, and he goes. Hashim bin 'Abd al-Malik is standing there and watching with great amazement. And he recognized that this is Imam 'Ali Zain al-Abidin, the son of Imam Husayn. The son of the Imam is the Imam. These are the grandsons of Janab 'Ali. He understood, Hashim bin 'Abd al-Malik. But because of the pride of his state, he asks his courtiers, "The king of the time... he asks his courtiers, 'Brother, who is this? Who is this?'" See the pretended ignorance. "And... who is he, what is this? He is being given so much respect. What is this?" So at that very moment, Farazdaq, the poet, was there. And Farazdaq, the poet, could not bear it. He came forward and says, "O Hashim, you don't know him? अरे, *hadha alladhi ta'rifu al-batha'u wat'atahu wal-baytu ya'rifuhu wal-hillu wal-haramu* (This is he whose footstep the valley knows, and the House knows him, and the sacred and the profane precincts). Are, this... you don't know this personality? Are, him... the Ka'ba knows him. And him... the place which is lawful (*hill*) and the place where one has to wear the *ehram*, they know him." And the ode (*qasida*) that Farazdaq began to recite, what can be said of that ode? *Zahabiya*, which is written with golden water, meaning the golden ode, it is called. And he recited tremendous verses. So when he started reciting the verses, he says while reciting, that these are the personalities from whose mouths the word *la* (no) has never come out. The word *la*, meaning 'no', has never come out. To refuse a supplicant is not in their nature. These are people of generosity and bounty (*jood-o-bakhshish*). Their hands have always been open. So, *ma qala la qattu illa fi tashahhudihi lawla al-tashahhudu kanat la'uhu na'amu* (He never said 'no' except in his Tashahhud; were it not for the Tashahhud, his 'no' would have been 'yes'). They never said 'no'. And in the *tashahhud*, if the word *la* in *la ilaha illa allah* did not come, they would have never said the word *la* in their entire lives. Did you see what a verse he recited? He said that in the *tashahhud*, if... if in reciting the Kalima Tayyiba, the word *la* did not come, they would have never uttered the word *la* from their mouths in their lives. So he was startled. And he said, "Farazdaq, you are my stipendiary (*wazifa-khwar*), you are from my courtiers, but you have never written such an ode in my praise." He said, "Brother, I am certainly, O king, your stipendiary, I am everything. You too, develop those qualities in yourself that are in the Ahl al-Bayt. I am ready to write that ode for you too." Develop those qualities. At that time, he was imprisoned. And after that, as soon as Maulana 'Ali Zain al-Abidin found out, you sent a sum of money with a slave, that... the slave kissed his feet, Farazdaq's, and said, "But I have recited the ode in the praise of the Imam. I have not said it for the sake of money." Anyway, he did not accept the gift and placed the Imam's letter on his head. So these incidents happened.
